h: Window Style Editor (2026-10-27)
x: Window Style Editor (2026-10-27) Windows app (id 12) : live preview of two sample windows, a colour picker and an inspector (chrome kind, geometry, title bar gradient, buttons, body, shadow, motion, nine colour schemes); every control restyles all open windows at once. WinStyle : ws[] in desk3/01-core.HC , drawn by desk3/01-winstyle.HC , edited by desk3/03e-windowstyle.HC . -1 follows the desktop style, so defaults are pixel identical to before (Aiwnios, five styles, measured). Themes : the five styles are read-only bases, Customize makes an editable copy; Export prints ws1 ... on COM1 and B:/WINSTYLE.TXT, Import reads it. Minimise and maximise buttons now exist (minimise closes with its own animation). Aiwnios: avoid A(1)<=x<A(2) chains. Details, numbers and limits: docs/apps/window-style-editor.md . Screenshots: shots/window-style-*.png . Not run on the x86 VM yet. Icon Style Editor (2026-10-27) The Icons app ( desk3/03c-iconstyle.HC , key i or the paintbrush in the dock): a live preview of every app icon at three sizes on light and dark backdrops, and ten pages of controls (shape, fill and gradients, colour schemes, tone, bevel and gloss, shadows, glyph, border and glass, glow and grain, dock layout), eight presets, Export and Import of a one-line style string ( KSI1 rd50 sq1 ... ) through Notes. One style, one function. is_v[] is the style; DrawIconTile(x,y,size,app,state) draws for the dock and the preview. The default style draws exactly as before; any other is built once per (app, size, signature, state) into cached colour tiles from shared alpha planes and blitted per frame. docs/apps/icon-style-editor.md has the controls, the format, the numbers and the limits. The dock calls the renderer through the pointer ks_ictile (forward declared calls do not reach a later definition). Works on Aiwnios unchanged; aiwnios/drive-icons.HC is a headless driver. Screenshots: shots/icon-style-*.png . Dock backdrop and Monitor (2026-10-27) Translucent dock. The pill is a 205-alpha tint over a blurred copy of what is actually behind it: wallpaper and any window under the dock. Outside the rounded shape nothing changes (no rectangle). The backdrop is sampled every fourth pixel, box blurred and enlarged by four ( DockBackdrop ), and recomputed only when the scene in the dock band changes; the dock's own redraws (hover, magnification, icon size) reuse it. DockGlass composites it through the corner coverage, so the edges are anti-aliased at 1x and 2x. Cost at 2x: the rebuild is about 2.4 ms (shown as "Dock backdrop" in the Monitor; 0.7 ms at 1x); a warm dock sweep is 3.4 ms, against 3.1 before. Monitor. The graph takes one sample per 100 ms of wall time (the largest frame in that time, 0 when idle) on a fixed 0 to 50 ms scale, drawn as an anti-aliased line that scrolls between samples. An open Monitor redraws only its numbers and graph, ten times a second, instead of the whole window once a second. Settings and Monitor pixel readouts show the real screen size (they read the window width while a window was being drawn). Screenshots: shots/fix-*.png . Boot experience (2026-10-27) scripts/run.sh /path/to/TempleOS.ISO opens the QEMU window on the Kosmos splash: a near-black screen, one mark (a ring with a dot set into it) and a thin loading bar, then a 600 ms crossfade to the desktop (a cut when Settings, Animations is off). The TempleOS terminal is never shown. How: the desktop is loaded and compiled once into a saved VM image ( scripts/build-image.sh , about 2.5 minutes, headless; savevm splash ) with Main parked on the splash at 0 percent. run.sh starts QEMU with -loadvm splash and sends a go byte over the serial port ( scripts/ks-go.py ). The guest then does the real remaining start-up work, with the bar following it: icons, window state, the wallpaper (about 1.4 s, reported row by row), the first frame; it then fades from the splash to that frame. The image lives in ~/.cache/kosmos-os/desk3-s<scale>.qcow2 (not in the repo); run.sh builds it on first use and rebuilds it when desk3/*.HC or the assets change. KS_S, KS_W and KS_H each get their own image. Display changes in Settings work as before (the splash code is not used again after start-up). Keys: T on the splash shows the original TempleOS screen (the 640x480 gr.dc2 , enlarged 3x at 2880x1800, 1x at 1440x900, on a dark ground); F12 returns to Kosmos, from the splash and also from the desktop (F12 on the desktop opens the original view at any time). R on the splash restarts: QEMU is started with -no-reboot , the guest tells run.sh over serial, and run.sh reloads the image. The Kosmos menu (top left): Restart reruns the whole session through the splash (a full guest reset that run.sh reloads from the image, because the desktop state cannot be rebuilt cleanly in place; if Notes were edited the row first asks once, as Notes live in the RAM drive that a restart reloads; outside run.sh it ends at the TempleOS prompt), and Quit Desktop opens the original TempleOS view (F12 returns). In the original view keys go to a TempleOS terminal (forwarded by Kosmos), the pointer is the TempleOS pointer. Cold path (old behaviour, about two minutes, the TempleOS terminal is visible while the files go in): KS_COLD=1 scripts/run.sh ISO . The dev loop is unchanged: scripts/snap.sh , then KS_S=2 KS_MODE=desk3 KS_RESTORE=1 scripts/send-to-vm.sh (it shows the splash too, with KS_PARK=0 ). KS_PARK=1 is only for building the image. Measured (QEMU on Apple Silicon, 2880x1800): from QEMU launch to desktop ready about 3.6 s with the image, of which about 1.9 s was the guest's start-up work after the go byte plus the 0.6 s fade (after the performance pass below the guest work is 0.56 s, KS-READY 1.5 s after go, as the wallpaper now builds in about 60 ms); the cold path is about 2.5 minutes after the 50 s boot. Drag benchmark after the change: 9.5 ms a frame (unchanged). Screenshots: shots/boot-*.png . The splash crossfade uses the two-source blend KsLerpRow ( LerpRow ); the KsMix3 routine this work first added was the same loop and was merged into it (see the performance pass below, which also replaced the style crossfade with a blend of two snapshots). Window and animation performance pass (2026-10-27) Branch perf/window-animation-speed . Everything below was measured in QEMU (TCG, x86-64 emulated on an Apple Silicon Mac) with the benchmark suite behind the b key: each scenario renders real frames through Render and records the average and worst frame; the Monitor app (key 6 ) shows the table and the same lines go out on the serial port ( bench|name|avg|worst|frames|phase split , tenths of a millisecond). t runs a self-test that checks every assembly routine against the HolyC formula and times the big copies. Before and after, milliseconds a frame (average / worst) Scenario 2880x1800 before 2880x1800 after 1440x900 before 1440x900 after Target Full redraw 31.1 / 31.6 14.0 / 14.9 19.8 / 26.6 3.4 / 3.5 Drag large window (Projects, 700x500) 10.3 / 12.3 5.0 to 5.6 / 6.0 to 6.8 8.0 / 27.5 1.3 / 1.4 5 Drag small window (Calculator) 12.0 / 20.8 3.6 / 4.3 8.3 / 28.8 0.9 / 1.0 Open and close animation 9.9 / 33.2 5.6 / 8.7 3.8 / 14.7 1.4 / 2.3 12 Focus change (shadow animation, both windows) 19.1 / 29.0 9.4 / 17.5 5.2 / 8.0 2.3 / 4.5 Style switch, first time (wallpaper build, snapshot, first frame) 1830 163 429 69 250 Style crossfade frames 277 / 297 60 / 63 50.4 / 54.9 3.7 / 3.8 25 (missed at 2x) Dock magnify sweep, cold (icon sizes seen for the first time) 42.9 / 116.6 3.4 / 5.1 14.5 / 60.8 1.0 / 2.0 no hitch over 20 Dock magnify sweep, warm 12.3 / 13.7 2.7 / 2.9 3.7 / 4.3 0.8 / 0.8 10 Files list scrolling 13.4 / 16.5 7.8 / 8.1 4.0 / 5.9 2.1 / 2.5 Notes typing 9.8 / 11.4 6.5 / 6.9 2.9 / 3.5 1.8 / 1.9 Caret blink 1.4 / 1.5 0.5 / 0.6 0.5 / 0.6 0.3 / 0.3 The drag number varies between 5.0 and 5.6 ms from run to run (three runs of the final code); the phase split of a 5.6 ms frame is wallpaper 1.1, windows 2.7 (shadow 1.2, layer copy 1.5), copy to the card 1.5. What changed, in the order it was measured Copy32 on an unrolled 64-byte MOV loop ( KsCpu ): a 2880x1800 copy takes 15.7 ms against 52.5 ms with REP MOVSQ (the copy to the video card is 4.0 ms either way). Every wallpaper, layer and card copy uses it. Wallpaper build ( BuildWall , Up4 , BoxLow ): 1830 ms to 70 ms. The gradient and blobs are computed at a sixteenth of the native size in HolyC (20k pixels), enlarged by four in assembly ( KsLerpRow down the rows, KsUp4H along them, the same bilinear maths as before), box blurred by an assembly sliding window ( KsBox8 , eight taps each way, edges repeated), and enlarged by four again. The picture is the same to the eye (screenshots compared); the blobs are a touch smoother. Style crossfade from two snapshots : SetStyle keeps the old screen in prev , Render draws the new one once into nxt , and every crossfade frame is bb = prev*k + nxt*(1-k) in assembly plus the copy to the card, instead of a full redraw and a HolyC Mix per pixel. 277 ms to 60 ms a frame at 2x, 16 ms at 1x. The 25 ms target is missed at 2x: the blend of 5.2 million pixels is 53 ms of pure instruction count (about 11 instructions a pixel; TCG runs close to one guest instruction a nanosecond on this Mac). A four-pixel SSE2 version, byte-encoded because the TempleOS assembler has no SSE opcodes (CR4.OSFXSR set by hand), gave the right pixels but took 83 ms: QEMU runs the packed integer instructions through helper calls. Dropped. Icon masks in integer arithmetic ( SegMask , DistTab ): the stroke rasteriser projected each pixel onto each segment with x87 floating point and a Sqrt . It now works in sixteenths of a pixel, one division a segment, and reads the coverage from a squared-distance table per icon size. Eleven dock icons at 64 px: 2.8 ms, against about 11 ms each before, so a dock size seen for the first time no longer hitches (cold sweep worst 117 ms to 5 ms). Retained window layers with damage ( LayerBuild , Composite , Damage* ): each open window keeps its chrome and body in a bitmap and is rebuilt only inside its damage rectangle; content changes call Damage (whole window), DamageL (a rectangle: hover highlights, the Viewport animation, the Notes text area, the Files list, the title bar on a focus change), while moving, raising and shadow animation only expose ( DirtyWin ) and copy the layer. Hit regions are stored per window and replayed each frame. The corners blend through the corner coverage table so they stay transparent over the shadow. Drag 7.9 to 5.1 ms, drag small 9.9 to 3.4, open and close 7.8 to 5.8, focus change 15.0 to 9.1, full redraw 25.5 to 19.0. Opaque hole : the topmost window shown from an opaque layer overwrites its inner rectangle, so the wallpaper and the layers under it are not copied there (the opaque-region idea of Weston and wlroots). Small on its own (wallpaper 1.3 to 1.0 ms in a drag) but free. Cached shadow tiles and corner tables : ShadowTile kept one (radius, blur) tile and CornerTab one radius, both built with a Sqrt per pixel; a frame that drew the dock and a window rebuilt both, and the magnified dock asked for a dozen radii. Four tiles and one table per radius are cached: dock sweep 12.3 to 2.7 ms, full redraw 19.7 to 14.0. ToFront dirties the raised window and the two title bars instead of every window: open and close worst frame 23 to 9 ms. Merged with the boot splash work: its KsMix3 blend was the same two-pixel loop as KsLerpRow (same maths, same instruction count), so one copy was kept, KsLerpRow , because the self-test checks it and Up4 uses it; SplashFade calls LerpRow . Its BoxLow , Up4 and BuildWall progress hooks ( SplashTick ) were carried into the new assembly-based versions. Tried and dropped: SSE2 (above). Not done: -smp with worker tasks (not measured; the remaining per-frame cost is copies and blends that would need the work split by row band, and TempleOS task switching under MTTCG is untested); a real backdrop blur for the glass style; pixman's exact divide-by-255 in the blend routines (our alpha runs 0 to 256, so 256 is exactly opaque and coverage 255 lands 0.4 percent short, which is below what the eye sees; the fix costs two instructions a lane). Idle: with the default desktop (Projects and the animated Viewport open, nothing else happening) QEMU uses about 36 percent of one core after this pass against 38 to 49 percent before, and 8 percent at the bare TempleOS prompt; the Viewport redraws its scene 30 times a second (about 3 ms each at 2x) and the loop wakes every 5 ms to poll the mouse and keyboard. Near zero was not reached; closing the Viewport, or sleeping longer when no window animates, is the next step. The main loop sleeps 5 ms when nothing is dirty and otherwise paces to the frame cap (60, or 30 in Settings, Display; QEMU refreshes its window about every 30 ms, so 30 is enough for a shown frame). Ideas read in compositor sources (MIT, ideas only, no code copied): the per-node damage of wlroots wlr_scene (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wlroots/wlroots, types/scene/wlr_scene.c) and the opaque regions and damage merging of Weston (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/weston, libweston/compositor.c) are what the layers, Damage* and the hole implement; pixman (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pixman/pixman, pixman-combine32.h) for the divide-by-255 note above. Hyprland (GPL-3) was not read. HolyC traps met in this pass: global arrays without an initialiser are not zeroed (a cache of pointers held garbage), a new global pointer must be nulled before its first Free , ks_hx0 was already the hit-region array (name clash gives "Invalid lval"), and anything printed from inside the renderer has to go out on COM1 because the screen is in VBE mode. Scripts: KS_TVM (state directory, default /tmp/tvm ) and KS_SERIAL_PORT (default 4555) let two VMs run side by side; boot-vm.sh records its pid in $KS_TVM/qemu.pid , stop-vm.sh kills only that one, shot.sh NAME screenshots to $KS_TVM/NAME.png . Renderer performance pass (2026-10-27) Dragging the Projects window at 2880x1800 (press b in the desktop; the Monitor app shows the result) went from 72.1 ms to 9.5 ms a frame . Measured in QEMU on an Apple Silicon Mac, 40 drag steps, redraw rectangles merged as in normal use: Phase (ms a frame) Before After Wallpaper copy 12.7 2.0 Windows (shadows, chrome, app bodies) 46.3 5.7 Copy to the video card 12.9 1.6 Total 72.1 9.5 What changed, each measured first ( spike/KsBench.HC , spike/KsBlend.HC , run with KS_MODE=bench or KS_MODE=blend ): - TempleOS MemCpy is REP MOVSB : 2392 ms for 168 MB. REP MOVSQ takes 321 ms (7.5x). MemSetU32 is REP STOSD (62 ms); an unrolled store loop takes 12 ms (5x). Copy32 and Fill32 in desk3/01-core.HC use them. - Blending in HolyC costs about 31 ns a pixel because of the code the compiler emits; the same maths in assembly, two pixels a pass, costs under 1 ns a pixel (0 mismatches against the HolyC formula). KsBlendRow , KsBlendCol , KsBlendA and KsBlendA2D do constant-alpha spans and columns, per-pixel alpha rows, and 2D alpha blocks. - Shadows were 42 of the 46 ms: a per-pixel function-call loop. They are now constant-alpha rows and columns plus a cached corner tile (2.8 ms). - Glyphs, Lucide icons, disks and rounded corners use the 2D alpha blit, so no function call per pixel. - Windows that miss a redraw rectangle are skipped after the first pass of a frame. Remaining cost is mostly app bodies (2.5 ms), window chrome (3 ms) and the two copies (3.6 ms). Next candidates: retained window layers with tile damage, and -smp with worker tasks. Kosmos Temple Desktop 3 (retina, Settings and more apps) desk3/*.HC is the current desktop. It draws in logical units (1440x900) at a scale of 1 or 2, so retina is a real 2880x1800 framebuffer with every shape and glyph rasterised natively (Inter atlases for both scales in assets/KSFONT.BIN ). Only the rectangles that changed are redrawn and copied to the card, so an idle desktop costs nothing and a moving window costs about 25 ms at 2880x1800. Window corners and shadows are anti-aliased and the shadow follows the rounded shape, so corners are truly transparent; the glass style clips its blurred backdrop to the same shape. Icons are Lucide (ISC, notice in assets/LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt ): scripts/gen-icons.py flattens the SVGs to strokes in assets/KSICONS.BIN , and the desktop rasterises them as anti-aliased strokes at any size, cached per size. Plan for the rest of the OS apps: docs/core-apps-plan.md . The TempleOS app mirrors the real TempleOS screen (its 640x480 gr.dc2 buffer) into a window, so any TempleOS program runs for real: in Files, select a .HC file and press Run, or click it twice (other files open in Notes). The program runs in its own terminal task; while the window is in front the keyboard goes to it and the pointer is mapped into 640x480. Close the window to stop it. Apps: Files (browses the real TempleOS drives and Demo, Apps and Doc folders), Projects, Notes (a text editor that saves to B:/NOTES.TXT), Calculator, Monitor (frame times and redraw cost), Viewport, Palette, Scene and Settings. Settings: Appearance (five themes with previews, accent colour, wallpaper), Display (resolution, 1x or 2x retina, frame cap; Apply switches the running desktop), Dock (icon size, magnification, indicators, translucency), About (system info, animations, frame time, corner radius, restart). Settings are not saved: the live CD has no writable disk. Run it (about two minutes; pass the TempleOS V5.03 ISO): scripts/run.sh /path/to/TempleOS.ISO Keys: 1 to 9 and 0 open apps in dock order, Tab brings the back window forward, s cycles the style, r toggles retina, p the next Settings page, b runs the benchmark suite, t the renderer self-test, f forces a full redraw, Esc reboots. Notes and Calculator take typing when in front. Mouse: click, drag title bars. The QEMU window is 2880 points wide at 2x; resize it (zoom-to-fit) so each guest pixel lands on a screen pixel. Measured in QEMU on an Apple Silicon Mac (x86 emulated): 7 ms per redraw at 1440x900 for the animated Viewport, about 25 ms at 2880x1800; the first switch to a theme at 2x pauses about 0.3 s while its wallpaper is built. Quick edit and test: scripts/snap.sh saves a booted snapshot with the font in it, then KS_S=2 KS_MODE=desk3 KS_RESTORE=1 scripts/send-to-vm.sh loads new code in about 20 seconds. Port research for running kosmos-app inside this desktop: docs/kosmos-app-port-research.md . Kosmos Temple Desktop 2 (1440x900, 32-bit colour) KsDesk2.HC is the version that matches apps/os-styles : Inter text, anti-aliased rounded windows, soft shadows, a blurred wallpaper behind a translucent menubar and floating dock, five styles, window open and close animations, a dock that magnifies icons toward the cursor, and a crossfade when the style changes. Screenshots: shots/desk2-*.png . How it works, with no kernel patch: QEMU standard VGA is switched to a linear 1440x900x32 framebuffer through its Bochs VBE ports (0x1CE and 0x1CF), the framebuffer address comes from PCI BAR0, and the desktop keeps its own back buffer, draws everything itself in HolyC and copies the frame to the card each time (the VGA bank register is moved past the visible memory so the TempleOS text compositor cannot scribble on the picture). TempleOS stays underneath as the runtime for HolyC, timers, files and input. The mouse is read as relative motion, because the system mouse is clamped to 640x480. Esc reboots. Run it (about two minutes; pass the TempleOS V5.03 ISO): text Copy scripts/run.sh /path/to/TempleOS.ISO Keys: 1 to 4 open an app, s cycles the style, Esc quits. Click the dock to open, focus or close an app, drag title bars. Apps: Projects (click a row), Viewport, Palette, Scene. Styles: Longformer light and dark, macOS, Windows 11, Kosmica glass. Measured in QEMU on an Apple Silicon Mac (x86 emulated): about 30 to 40 ms per frame at 1440x900 with four windows, so 25 to 30 frames per second. A full-screen copy is about 7 ms and a 64000 pixel HolyC loop about 1 ms ( spike/KsSpike.HC ). 2560x1600 works (KS_W, KS_H and KS_VGAMEM=32, see scripts/run.sh ) but frames take about three times as long. Limits: only works on the QEMU standard VGA card; the glass style blurs the wallpaper, not the windows underneath; the text atlas is Inter (SIL Open Font License) at four fixed sizes, rasterised by scripts/gen-font.py into assets/KSFONT.BIN ; rebuilding it needs Pillow and the Inter TTFs. For quick edit and test cycles, scripts/snap.sh boots once and saves a VM snapshot, then KS_MODE=desk2 KS_RESTORE=1 scripts/send-to-vm.sh reloads in about 40 seconds. Kosmos Temple Desktop (custom drawn) KsDesk.HC is a desktop that paints itself, to match apps/os-styles : menubar with a clock and a style pill, windows with title bars and rounded cards, and a floating dock with running dots and hover labels. One full-screen TempleOS window draws everything from a draw_it callback and reads the mouse ( ms.pos , ms.lb ) and keyboard in its own loop, so Esc, mouse clicks and dragging all work. Five styles reprogram the 16-colour palette and pick a window chrome: Longformer light and dark, macOS (traffic lights), Windows 11 (caption buttons), Kosmica glass. Apps: Projects (click a row), Viewport, Palette, Scene. Run it (about four minutes, the files go in over the serial port; pass the TempleOS V5.03 ISO): text Copy scripts/run.sh /path/to/TempleOS.ISO Keys: 1 to 4 open an app, s cycles the style, Esc quits. Click the dock to open, focus or close an app; drag title bars. Screenshots: shots/desktop-*.png . Limits: 640x480 and 16 colours, an 8x8 bitmap font, no anti-aliasing; the TempleOS title bar and border still frame the screen. The older tiled-window shell ( KosmosShell.HC , KsLib.HC ) loads with KS_MODE=shell scripts/send-to-vm.sh . Kosmos Temple Shell (HolyC, runs inside real TempleOS) Tiled app windows above a persistent launcher bar, written in HolyC against the official TempleOS V5.03 sources ( Adam/Win.HC for WinHorz / WinVert / WinToTop / WinMax , Demo/DolDoc/MenuBttn.HC , Demo/Graphics/Life.HC for the draw_it idiom). Tested in QEMU on this Mac. See shots/ . File What KosmosShell.HC loader. #include "KosmosShell.HC"; loads the library into the Adam task, then starts the bar KsLib.HC the shell: four apps, the tiler, the bar ProjectsData.HC generated from ../os-styles/projects.json by scripts/gen-projects.py (17 kamiji projects) scripts/boot-vm.sh boots the TempleOS ISO headless in QEMU and answers the two start-up questions scripts/send-to-vm.sh copies the three files into the running VM over the serial port and starts the shell scripts/vmkeys.py types text into the VM through the QEMU monitor What it does The terminal you start it from becomes the bar , pinned to the bottom 4 text rows: Projects Viewport Palette Scene | Tile Close Quit . A star marks an open app. Each app opens in its own terminal window and the tiler re-flows all open apps into a grid above the bar (1 app full, 2 side by side, 3 and 4 in a 2x2, the last row stretches). Projects : the 17 kamiji projects as a menu, green for available and brown for prototype, with a popup per project. Viewport : the box-drop scene as spinning wire cubes, drawn into an off-screen buffer that the window blits, so it stays inside its tile. Palette : the 16 VGA colours. Scene : the box-drop entities with a live jiffies counter. Tile re-flows, Close closes the most recently opened app, Quit kills every app and restores the terminal. Keys inside TempleOS Arrow keys move, Space presses a button (Enter is right-click), Shift-Esc closes a popup. A new app takes keyboard focus; click the bar to give it back, then use the arrow keys and Space. Run it scripts/boot-vm.sh /path/to/TempleOS.ISO (ISO from templeos.org, 17,350,656 bytes; needs qemu-system-x86_64 and nc ). scripts/send-to-vm.sh (about a minute). Things learned the hard way Only Core0 tasks get a window, and a bare Spawn task has no document or key input. Apps run in User terminals instead, with the command typed in by XTalk . Functions defined in one terminal are private to it, so the library is loaded with AdamFile to make them global. The compiler reads one token ahead, so AdamFile(...); KosmosShell; fails: the second name is looked up before the first line has run. The loader types the call with XTalk . A dollar sign or apostrophe in a comment is still parsed as a DolDoc command or a character constant. DCFill on a window alias fills the whole screen. Draw into your own DCNew buffer and blit it from Fs->draw_it . The QEMU mouse is relative and scales by about 0.48, so mouse tests slam to the corner first. Mouse clicks on bar buttons worked in some runs and missed in others; the keyboard path is the verified one. The ISO9660 route for getting files in failed ( ISOInit exception); the serial route works. Not done Runs on the live CD, so nothing is saved across reboots. The bar does not refresh when an app is closed by other means (it redraws on the next click), and Close only closes the most recent app. The Viewport is a wireframe, not the engine.

t: Kosmos OS foundation: apps that run normally, no capture
h: Kosmos OS foundation: apps that run normally, no capture
x: Kosmos OS foundation: apps that run normally, no capture Written 2026-10-27 after the Electron and Tauri research. Facts marked (verify) are from memory or docs and have not been tried here. The principle Electron and Tauri apps do not need pixels forwarded; they need an operating system that provides the contracts they were built for: a Linux kernel interface, a C library, a Wayland display server, D-Bus, an audio server, XDG portals, and a package and sandbox format. So the foundation is a real OS that provides those contracts, with our shell as its desktop environment . We implement the platform instead of imitating an app's output. TempleOS cannot provide these contracts (no libc, threads, network stack, GPU or audio), so it stops being the base. Everything we have built for look and feel carries over. Options considered Base Runs Electron and Tauri natively Cost of the contracts Verdict TempleOS plus our own drivers no years: TCP, TLS, USB, virtio, libc, threads, a browser engine rejected Redox OS (Rust) no, Chromium is not ported (verify) high rejected Android or Fuchsia not Electron or Tauri high, and a different app model rejected A shell app on macOS (Electron or Tauri itself) yes, but it is not an OS low a useful stepping stone for UI work, not the foundation Linux with our own Wayland compositor and shell yes, unmodified apps low: the contracts already exist chosen Build on an existing distribution (Debian, Fedora, Arch or NixOS on arm64 and x86-64) and replace only the desktop layer. Do not build a distribution from scratch: security updates and hardware support are a full-time job. Layers text Copy apps Flatpak apps (Electron, Tauri, GTK, Qt), first-party Tauri apps with Kamiji components portals xdg-desktop-portal backend (file chooser, screenshot, notifications, settings, screencast) shell kosmos-shell: Wayland compositor, menubar, dock, launcher, settings, notifications, lock screen services systemd, D-Bus, PipeWire, NetworkManager, seatd or logind, greetd, polkit, Flatpak base Linux kernel and a standard userland (glibc), image built reproducibly (mkosi, Nix or Buildroot) platform virtio devices in a VM first; real hardware later The shell Recommended: a compositor on Smithay (Rust, MIT (verify)), which matches the Rust stack in this repo. Alternatives: wlroots (C, MIT), forking COSMIC (Rust, GPL-3.0, so a licence decision (verify)), or a GNOME Shell or KDE plugin (least control). Rendering must work without a GPU, because VMs on this Mac have no usable GL (see below): use Smithay's software and GLES renderers over llvmpipe (verify), and keep the shell UI cheap. Our UI layer options: the engine's wgpu renderer, a Rust toolkit (iced or Slint), or HTML through a system web view. Pick by a small spike (the shell needs a menubar, dock, launcher, settings and notifications, not a general toolkit). Protocols the compositor must implement for apps to behave normally: xdg-shell (windows), xdg-decoration (our server-side titlebars), layer-shell (menubar and dock), wl-seat with pointer, keyboard, touch, relative-pointer and pointer-constraints, fractional-scale and viewporter (retina), linux-dmabuf and wp-presentation-time, data-device and primary-selection (clipboard, drag and drop), text-input-v3 and input-method (IME), xdg-activation, idle-inhibit, screencopy or image-capture for screenshots, XWayland for legacy apps. The app platform Flatpak plus portals. One sandboxed packaging format gives access to Flathub's Electron and Tauri apps (VS Code, Obsidian, Slack, Discord, Signal, Element and more are published there (verify each)), with permissions that match our approval model. Electron runs on Wayland through Ozone (verify the flags and version). Tauri uses WebKitGTK on Linux (verify Tauri 2 packages). First-party apps are Tauri apps built with the Kamiji (Longformer) components and tokens, so system apps and the shell share one design language. Settings, Files, Notes, Terminal and the store are the first ones. Security: every app is sandboxed by default; credentials live in a system keyring; outward actions (sending mail or messages, purchases) always need an explicit user prompt. What carries over from the HolyC desktop Design tokens and the five styles, the Inter and Lucide assets, the window chrome kinds (traffic lights, caption buttons, glass), the dock and menubar behaviour, the Settings structure, the core-apps list, and the animation timings. The HolyC desktop stays as the "Temple" skin reference and as a TempleOS app (TempleOS runs in a QEMU window as one app, with HolyC available as a feature), not as the foundation. This Mac as the development host Checked on 2026-10-27: Apple Silicon (arm64, macOS 27), Homebrew qemu-system-aarch64 with HVF acceleration (guest runs at native speed), Lima and Docker present, 41 GB free. This QEMU build lists virtio-gpu-pci but no GL variant, so a Linux guest would render in software (llvmpipe), which is fine for a shell and for Electron and Tauri apps at normal speed (verify the frame rates in M0). Apple's Virtualization.framework through Lima is the quickest start; a QEMU HVF image is the more controllable one. The real target hardware (an Apple Silicon Mac with Asahi, a PC, a Pi, a VM product) is a decision for the user and affects GPU and driver work. Milestones, each with a pass or fail gate M What Gate Time box M0 A Linux arm64 VM (Lima or QEMU HVF) running a stock Wayland compositor (sway or cage) with one Electron app and one Tauri app launched natively. Needs downloads: a distro image of a few hundred MB and the apps. both apps run as real windows, typing and scrolling feel normal, 30 fps or better scrolling in software rendering 2 days M1 kosmos-shell v0: a Smithay compositor with xdg-shell, layer-shell menubar and dock placeholders, our server-side titlebars, pointer and keyboard, and the same two apps same apps, same gates, windows drag and resize, our chrome 1 week M2 fractional-scale (retina), clipboard and drag and drop, IME, dmabuf, activation, XWayland copy and paste between apps, crisp text at 2x 1 week M3 Portals backend (file chooser, notifications, screenshots), PipeWire audio, NetworkManager panel a Flatpak app opens files and plays sound 1 to 2 weeks M4 Flatpak store UI, first-party Tauri apps with Kamiji (Settings, Files), launcher install and run an app from the store inside our shell 2 weeks M5 Reproducible image build, installer, updates boots from a clean image; update works 2 weeks Risks and decisions for the user Target hardware and GPU: software rendering is acceptable in a VM, real hardware needs a driver story. Licence: COSMIC is GPL-3.0; Smithay and wlroots are MIT (verify). Decide before forking anything. Scope and ownership: a desktop environment is a long project; the repo rules (CLAUDE.md) and plan section 8.6 apply, and starting new phase work needs the user's go. Maintenance: a distribution base means tracking its security updates. Where this lives in the repo: a new directory (for example apps/kosmos-os/ ) once approved. What we stop doing No more screen capture or pixel streaming into TempleOS as the app route, no shared-RAM bridge spike, no further HolyC apps beyond the reference skin. The two research reports remain as the record of why.

t: Kosmos Temple Desktop: core apps and how to build them
h: Kosmos Temple Desktop: core apps and how to build them
x: Kosmos Temple Desktop: core apps and how to build them Status on 2026-10-27. "Built" means running in the desktop today ( desk3/ ). Everything is HolyC inside TempleOS V5.03, drawn by our own renderer, so each app is a function that draws into a window body in logical pixels and registers hit regions. API names marked (verify) are from memory of the TempleOS source and have not been tried yet. What the platform gives and takes away Gives: HolyC compiled at run time (so a code editor with a Run button is cheap), raw hardware access, the TempleOS file system (RedSea on the CD and RAM drive B:), FileRead and FileWrite , FilesFind , timers, PC speaker sound, multicore. Takes away: no network, no writable disk on the live CD (nothing survives a reboot), about 15 ns per simple pixel operation, 25 to 30 fps at retina size, single font atlas, no clipboard or drag and drop yet, one mouse and keyboard path of our own. A host bridge changes the last two points: the QEMU serial port already carries our files in, so a small Mac-side daemon can add persistence (settings, notes), a clipboard, screenshots out, and real network or kosmos-app data in. The serial loader is lockstep (about 1.4 KB/s measured, with 32 byte acknowledgements); a streaming drain loop could be much faster (unmeasured). Core apps Effort: S about a day, M about three days, L about a week. Order is the build order. Tier 0: the shell itself (needed before more apps are worth building) App State How to build it Effort App framework missing Replace the if (a==...) chains with an app table: name, icon, default size, and four functions (draw, click, key, close). New apps become one file. Add per-window minimise, maximise and resize with edge hit regions, and a focus and keyboard-routing rule that every app uses. M Widget kit v2 partial (button, toggle, radio, slider) Add text field (caret, selection, copy and paste), list and table with scrolling, tabs, dropdown, dialog and sheet, tooltip, context menu, scroll view with wheel. Immediate mode with hit regions is already proven, so extend it. Put it in its own file so the Kamiji component names map one to one. M Launcher (Cmd-Space) missing A popup with a text field that fuzzy-matches app names, recent files and commands (Files and Projects already give the data). One window, keyboard first. S Notifications and toasts missing A queue drawn in a corner above everything, auto-dismiss, optional actions. Apps call Notify(text) . Needed by Files, the bridge and Terminal. S Host bridge missing A Python daemon on the Mac that owns the QEMU serial port after boot. Line protocol: get / put file, clip , shot , tree (see kosmos-app). Guest side is one HolyC task that polls COM1 with the acknowledged scheme. Gives persistence, clipboard and screenshots. Measure the streaming rate first (gate: 20 KB/s). M Settings built (themes, accent, wallpaper, display, dock, about) Add: save and load through the bridge, keyboard shortcuts page, sound volume, date and time, default apps. Drop the pending/apply split once resolution changes are instant. S Tier 1: everyday apps App State How to build it Effort Files built (browse, open in Notes) Add: new folder, rename, copy, move, delete with confirmation ( FileWrite , Copy , Del (verify)), a search box over the current tree, list and icon views, image and text preview in a side pane, breadcrumbs, open-with. M Notes / text editor built (plain, save to B:) Multi-document tabs, open and save any path, undo, selection and clipboard (needs the text field widget), find and replace, line numbers. Keep it the single text engine: Code and Terminal reuse it. M Code editor missing Notes plus HolyC syntax colouring (keywords, strings, comments, numbers as a small state machine per line) and a Run button that does ExeFile (verify) on the buffer and shows errors in a panel. This is the best demonstration of TempleOS, since compiling is instant. M Terminal missing A scrolling text view plus an input line. Commands go to ExePrint (verify); capture output by pointing the task's put-doc at our own buffer (the approach PopUp uses, verify) or by running the command in a child task with its own CDoc and copying the text out. Include history, tab completion for paths, and a few built-ins ( ls , cd , cat ). M Calculator built (basic) Scientific mode (sin, cos, log, powers, constants), history tape, keyboard entry already works. Sin , Cos , Log10 , Pow exist in HolyC. S Activity monitor built (frame time graph) Add the task list (walk the task ring from Fs , verify), per-task name, memory and core, memory totals, and a Kill button ( Kill ). Pair frame time with the per-phase timers already collected. S Calendar and clock missing A menubar popover with the month grid ( Now , Date2Struct (verify)), world clocks, timer and stopwatch tabs. The live CD has no real time zone, so show the VM clock and allow an offset in Settings. S Image viewer missing Host converts PNG or JPEG to a raw 32-bit file with a tiny header; guest FileRead s and blits with scaling (nearest then bilinear). Works for screenshots and wallpapers too. Bridge needed for new images. S Paint missing A bitmap canvas in guest memory with pencil, line, rectangle, ellipse, fill, eraser, colour palette from the theme tokens, undo ring, save raw and PNG through the bridge. The renderer already has anti-aliased primitives. M Docs viewer missing Render the TempleOS ::/Doc DolDoc files: parse $ commands (colour, links, centre) into styled lines with our font. Makes the OS self-documenting and Help searchable from the launcher. M Tier 2: media and fun App State How to build it Effort Music missing TempleOS plays through the PC speaker ( Play , Snd ) and its Hymns are in ::/Apps . A player UI over those: list, play, pause, a spectrum from the note stream. QEMU needs -audiodev and a speaker device to be audible (unverified). M Games missing TempleOS ships games in ::/Demo/Games and ::/Apps . Ours: a launcher tile that runs them in a window by redirecting their draw to our back buffer (they use GrBlot and GrLine on a CDC, which we can point at a window-sized CDC and blit). Start with one simple game. M Screenshot missing Copy the framebuffer to a file on B: and ship it through the bridge (PNG on the host). Hot key plus a toast. S Tier 3: Kosmos apps App State How to build it Effort Projects built (17 kamiji projects) Generate from the kamiji site list at build time (already done), add status filters and open-in-browser through the bridge. S Kosmos Editor (kosmos-app mirror) missing Per docs/kosmos-app-port-research.md : run kosmos-app on the Mac, send its editor.tree as deltas over the bridge, draw it with our widget kit by role, return editor.event lines. First proof: one tree snapshot drawn as labelled boxes. Needs the user's go; no protected files touched by the demo. L Viewport placeholder (wireframe cubes) After the bridge exists, stream a 4 or 8 bit quantised engine frame into the window, or render scene data natively. Decide after measuring the channel. L Scene inspector and Palette built (static) Drive them from the same tree data as the Kosmos Editor so they become real. S Component gallery missing One window that shows every widget in every style with the token palette live; doubles as our visual regression page and as documentation for the Kamiji mapping. S Build order App framework and Widget kit v2 (everything else depends on them). Host bridge with streaming-rate spike, then persistence and clipboard. Launcher, Notifications, Text field powered Notes, Terminal, Code editor (the TempleOS-native showpieces). Files completion, Image viewer, Paint, Screenshot. Calendar, Docs viewer, Activity monitor completion, Music, Games. Kosmos Editor and Viewport, after the user approves the kosmos-app bridge. Risks Frame budget: eleven or more windows with text in each cost real time at 2880x1800. Keep the dirty-rectangle rule and give each app its own cheap invalidation (as Viewport and Scene do) rather than redrawing whole windows. Text editing at scale (selection, wrapping, undo) is where HolyC speed and our proportional font hurt: cap buffer sizes, cache line layouts, and invalidate only changed lines. TempleOS API details marked (verify) can differ from memory. Each tier starts with a half-day spike that proves the API in the VM. Nothing persists without the bridge. Until it exists, say so in Settings and Notes. Licences: Inter (OFL) and Lucide (ISC) are attributed in assets/ ; the vendored kamiji kit in apps/os-styles is not cleared for publishing. Addendum: the six big apps and porting open-source software Wanted: text editor, web browser, music player, code editor with AI, email, text messenger. Three ways to bring open-source software in, from least to most effort per app: Host service plus native UI (recommended for most). The Mac runs the real open-source engine; our desktop draws a themed, retina UI and talks to it over the host bridge. Credentials, network and heavy code stay on the Mac. Remote app window. The Mac (or a Linux VM or container) runs the unmodified app and streams its pixels into a desktop window; input flows back. Anything open source works, at the cost of looking foreign and of bandwidth. True source port into HolyC. Only small, self-contained C code (an editor like kilo, Lua, an image or MP3 decoder). TempleOS has no libc, threads or network stack and HolyC is not C, so this is translation with a small shim ( memcpy , malloc onto MAlloc , printf onto Print ), done per library, not for applications. App Approach Open-source pieces Notes Text editor native (finish Notes) kilo (about 1000 lines of C) as a reference to translate; gap buffer or rope no bridge needed except save to host Code editor and AI IDE native editor plus host agent host side: an agent like Claude Code over the bridge, language servers, git files live on the Mac and are edited by the guest through the bridge; the guest runs HolyC itself; chat, diff and tool-approval panels are native Web browser host renders, guest shows headless Chromium or WebKit through the DevTools screencast, or Servo; reader mode via Readability native chrome (tabs, URL bar, bookmarks); page pixels streamed; a cheap reader mode sends styled text instead Email host service plus native UI Himalaya (Rust, JSON output), or isync with notmuch or mblaze native list, reader and compose; HTML mail reduced to styled text; OAuth tokens never enter the guest Text messenger host service plus native UI Matrix with matrix-nio, mautrix bridges (Signal, WhatsApp, iMessage), signal-cli, IRC conversation list, bubbles, composer, toasts; each account needs explicit user approval, and sending is always a user action Music player host plays, guest controls mpd or mpv (or afplay), ffmpeg for metadata and art TempleOS has only a PC speaker driver, so audio cannot come from the guest without writing an HDA or AC97 driver; native UI over mpd gives library, queue, art and a spectrum The channel decides everything Correction, 2026-10-27: the ivshmem idea below does not work on this Mac. Homebrew QEMU 11.0.2 has no ivshmem-plain device (checked with qemu-system-x86_64 -device help ). memory-backend-file , memory-backend-shm and memory-backend-ram do exist, so the candidate is guest RAM backed by a shared file that the host also maps. Unproven under TCG on macOS. See electron-tauri-support-research.md . The serial port is too slow for pixels (about 1.4 KB/s lockstep, unmeasured when streamed). The best candidate is shared memory: QEMU ivshmem-plain backed by a file the host also maps. The guest already reads a PCI BAR (the VGA framebuffer), so mapping another is the same code, and a ring buffer in HolyC is a few dozen lines. A 1440x900 frame is 5 MB, a full copy measured about 7 ms in the VM, so 30 fps of streamed pixels is plausible. Unverified: ivshmem on macOS QEMU, the guest page mapping of that BAR, and host capture of other apps' windows (easiest from a Linux container running Xvfb or from Playwright for the browser). Spikes, in order (each a half day, each with a pass or fail gate) ivshmem ring: gate 20 MB/s guest to host and host to guest. Pixel window: stream a Playwright-driven Chromium viewport into a desktop window at 15 fps or better, with click and key back. Himalaya or Matrix over the same channel: list messages or rooms in a native list. mpd: play, pause, queue and album art from a native player. Agent panel: a chat view backed by a host process with approval prompts for every file write and command. Rule for all of them: nothing is sent, deleted or purchased on the user's behalf without an explicit prompt in the UI.

t: HolyC-native apps, including a web browser
h: HolyC-native apps, including a web browser
x: HolyC-native apps, including a web browser Written 2026-10-27, after choosing TempleOS as the base. This replaces the screen-capture route in the earlier research and supersedes os-foundation-plan.md for this direction. Facts marked (verify) are from memory and untested here. What "native" means here An app is HolyC code that draws with our renderer ( desk3/ ), receives our input, and gets anything the guest cannot do (network, TLS, audio, persistence, an AI model) from a small number of well-defined services. No pixels are captured from another program. The honest limit is that the guest has no network stack, no TLS, no image or font libraries and no JavaScript engine; each is either built in HolyC or provided by a host service behind a clean protocol. Anything that needs a modern JavaScript web platform (Gmail, YouTube, Slack, VS Code) is out of reach for a native browser, whatever we do. The browser targets the document web : articles, docs, wikis, blogs, search results, forums, repos, feeds. Foundation before the browser Piece Why Options Size A fast channel A page is tens to hundreds of KB; the lockstep serial loader moves about 1.4 to 2.7 KB/s, so one page would take a minute (a) streaming serial with the 16550 FIFO and no per-chunk acknowledgement: unmeasured, gate 50 KB/s; (b) a second IDE disk used as a mailbox the host and guest both read and write (TempleOS has an ATA driver; verify raw block access to an unformatted drive); (c) a native NIC driver (see below) spike, 1 to 2 days App framework Remove the fixed app arrays; one file per app; shared keyboard and focus rules app table with draw, click, key, close; resizable windows M Widget kit v2 Browser chrome, forms and editors need text fields, lists, tabs, menus, dialogs, scroll views extend 02-ui.HC M Font and glyph service A browser needs many sizes, bold, italic, monospace and non-Latin text rasterise TrueType in HolyC (a port of stb_truetype, about 5k lines of C) with a glyph cache; or keep atlases built on the host for a fixed set of sizes M to L Image decoding Pages contain images a PNG and JPEG decoder in HolyC (stb_image style), or a host service that returns resized raw pixels M Persistence History, bookmarks, settings and notes must survive the live CD host file service over the channel S Two ways to get bytes from the web Host fetch service (first). The Mac fetches the page (HTTP, TLS, redirects, cookies, compression), and the guest asks for it by URL. Small, fast to build, and TLS and certificate handling stay on the host. The guest never sees credentials or TLS keys. Native network stack (long term, optional). A driver for a QEMU NIC (RTL8139 or E1000, a few hundred to a thousand lines), then ARP, IP, UDP, DHCP, DNS, TCP, and TLS 1.3 (X25519, AES-GCM or ChaCha20, SHA-256, certificate chain checks with a bundled root store). TempleOS has none of it, and its original charter rejects networking, so this is new ground; plain HTTP is the achievable first milestone, TLS is several weeks on its own (verify speed under emulation: a handshake is millions of 64-bit multiplications). It would make the OS genuinely self-contained and give every app sockets. Recommendation: build the host fetch service first so the browser exists soon, with the browser written against an internal "fetch(url)" interface so the native stack can replace the host later without touching the engine. The browser, in layers Layer What it does Notes Size Chrome tabs, URL and search bar, back and forward, reload, bookmarks, history, find in page, downloads, reader mode toggle uses widget kit v2 M HTML tokenizer and a simplified tree builder, entities, a decent subset of elements, forgiving of bad markup no need for the full HTML5 error-recovery tables at first M CSS parser, selectors (type, class, id, descendant, child, attribute, common pseudo-classes), cascade and specificity, inheritance, the common properties (display, color, background, font, margin, padding, border, width, height, text-align, line-height, overflow, position basics, list-style) the most work per feature L Layout block and inline formatting, line breaking, lists, tables, floats, simple flexbox, images, forms a faithful box model L Paint our renderer: anti-aliased rounded borders, backgrounds, shadows, text with the glyph service, images, links with hover already largely exists M Interaction links, scrolling, text selection and copy, find, form fields and submit needs the text field widget M Reader mode extract the main content (Readability-like heuristics, in HolyC or on the host), render with our typography gives the best result on article pages with the least code, so build it first S to M Other protocols Gemini, Gopher, RSS and Atom, Markdown and our own docs, TempleOS DolDoc small, native, fit the OS S each JavaScript none at first; later a small ES5-class interpreter (port mujs-sized code, about 20k lines of C, or write one) with a minimal DOM even then, most modern sites break; decide only after the document web works L to XL Expected coverage with no JavaScript: Wikipedia, documentation sites, blogs, news articles (often via reader mode), Hacker News, most forums' HTML versions, GitHub README pages, search engines' lightweight pages, feeds. Not covered: web apps and anything that renders client side. If broader coverage is ever required, the clean fallback is a host-side headless browser that sends a display list (positioned text runs, boxes and images) for the guest to paint natively and crisply, with events sent back. That is rendering, not screen capture, but it reintroduces a host dependency, so treat it as an optional mode. The other apps, in the same style App Native part Service part Text editor and code editor gap buffer, selection, undo, syntax colouring, run HolyC with errors, find and replace file service for saves Terminal HolyC REPL, history, completion none Email list, reader, compose, HTML-to-text host IMAP and SMTP service (Himalaya or similar), tokens kept on the host Messenger conversation list, bubbles, composer, toasts host Matrix or Signal bridge Music player library, queue, art, visualiser host playback (mpd or mpv); TempleOS cannot play real audio without a sound driver AI IDE native editor, diff, chat and approval panels host agent with explicit approval for every write and command Files, Notes, Calculator, Monitor, Settings, Paint, Image viewer, Docs viewer, Calendar all native file service for persistence Rule for every service-backed app: nothing is sent, deleted or purchased without an explicit prompt in the UI. Order of work and gates Channel spike (2 days). Gate: at least 50 KB/s sustained from host to guest and 20 KB/s back, no corruption over 10 MB. Framework and widget kit v2 (about 2 weeks). Gate: a text field, list and tab strip used by at least two apps. Host services v0 : file, fetch. (3 days). Gate: the guest saves a note and fetches a page. Browser B0 : chrome plus reader mode on the fetch service. (1 week). Gate: five chosen article URLs render legibly at 2x. Browser B1 : native HTML and CSS subset, images, fonts. (3 to 5 weeks). Gate: a fixed set of 20 pages (Wikipedia, MDN, a blog, HN, a GitHub README) lay out without overlap and with correct links. Editor, terminal, code editor in parallel with B1, then Files completion, Paint, image viewer, docs viewer. Email and messenger on the host services, after a review of accounts and approval flows with the user. Native network stack track (RTL8139 or E1000, IP, TCP, then TLS), only if self-containment is wanted; swap in behind fetch . Risks HolyC speed under emulation: layout and CSS cascade on large pages can be slow; budget parse and layout per page and stream results in. CSS volume: scope by a fixed conformance page set, not by the spec. No JavaScript is a hard ceiling on coverage; say so in the UI (a reader-mode and "open on the host" escape). The mouse, keyboard and clipboard paths are still hacks in the guest (relative-mouse workaround, no key-up, no non-ASCII); fix them in the framework step. Persistence depends on the channel spike.

t: KSFONT2.BIN, font file format v2 (2026-10-27)
h: KSFONT2.BIN, font file format v2 (2026-10-27)
x: KSFONT2.BIN, font file format v2 (2026-10-27) Host side done, guest side is phase 2. Files: scripts/gen-font2.py (writer), scripts/font2_ref.py (reader and specimen renderer), scripts/ks-utf8.py (text to literal), tests/fonts/test_font2.py , assets/fonts/ (sources and OFL text), shots/fonts-*.png . v1 ( KSFONT.BIN , gen-font.py ) is untouched and stays the file the desk loads until phase 2. File layout (little endian, every table 4-byte aligned, offsets from the start of the file) Part Bytes Content Header 32 "KSF2" , U16 major (2), U16 minor (0), U32 file size, U32 face count, U32 face dir offset (32), U32 face entry size (64), U32 flags (bit n set = tier n present), U32 CRC-32 of bytes 32 to the end Face dir 64 each U8 ascent, descent, line gap, line height (= sum), px size, family (0 Inter), role (0 REG, 1 BOLD, 2 SMALL, 3 BIG), scale (1 or 2); U16 weight, U16 flags (bit0 has kerning); U32 range table offset, range count, record offset, record count, pixel blob offset, pixel blob length, kern offset, kern count, expanded bytes (2 x pixel length); char[16] name Range table 24 each U32 first code point, count, glyph index base, pixel offset of the slice (in the face blob), slice length, tier Glyph records 12 each U16 advance (1/16 px), U8 w, U8 h, I8 bearing x, I8 bearing y (up from the baseline), U16 flags (bit0: this character has kerning pairs as the left one), U32 pixel offset (bytes, from the face blob start) Kern pairs 4 each U16 key = (left << 8) or right, I16 value (1/16 px), sorted by key; code points below 256 only Pixels per face 4-bit alpha, two per byte, high nibble first, each glyph padded to a whole byte, rows back to back (exactly the v1 data) Rules. The face index is role + (scale - 1) * 4 , so the eight faces are v1's, in v1's order (Regular 13, Bold 13, Regular 11, Bold 22, then at scale 2 Regular 26, Bold 26, Regular 22, Bold 44); more faces append (a reader sizes its arrays from the count, 16 is plenty). Range 0 is U+0020 to U+007E (base 0), range 1 is U+00A0 to U+00FF (base 95), every face has the same ranges, ranges are sorted and never overlap. A code point inside a range that the font lacks has a record with advance 0 and w 0 ("absent"); a space has advance above 0 and w 0. A new minor version only adds fields at the end of an entry (read by the entry size); a new major version changes the magic number's meaning, so refuse it. Tier: 0 resident (set A), 1 Latin Extended-A, Greek, Cyrillic (set B), 2 Vietnamese (set C). Kerning comes from the GPOS kern feature of Inter (class and pair tables), scaled to the face size, kept when it moves at least half a pixel, ASCII only ( --kern latin1 adds the accented capitals and lower-case letters: B grows to 677,080 bytes, 40,556 more, for pairs their base letters mostly already have). No kern in v1 means v1 text is a little wider than v2 text. Lookup (the exact algorithm, Font2.lookup in font2_ref.py) text Copy cp 32..126 -> glyph index cp-32 (1 compare, the common case) cp 160..255 -> 95 + cp - 160 (2 compares) else binary search ranges 2..n-1 on first / first+count: at most 6 steps for 41 ranges (each: one U32 load, two compares) glyph index g -> record at rec_off + 12*g; advance 0 and w 0, or no range -> use the record of U+FFFD pixels of the glyph: gpx(face, range) + off * 2 + row * w + col (off is in packed bytes, so x2 in expanded bytes) kerning: only when the previous record has flag bit0 and both code points are below 256: binary search 4-byte pairs (about 10 steps) Guest read procedure for phase 2 (replaces FontLoad ) text Copy b = FileRead("B:/KSFONT2.BIN") // keep it: records, ranges and kern pairs are read in place, no copy check b[0..3]=="KSF2" and U16 at 4 == 2; nf = U32 at 12; ents = b + U32 at 16; esz = U32 at 20 for f < nf: e = ents + f*esz; ks_fa[f]=e[0]; ks_fdesc[f]=e[1]; ks_flh[f]=e[3]; ks_frng[f]=b+U32(e+12); ks_fnr[f]=U32(e+16); ks_frec[f]=b+U32(e+20); ks_fpix[f]=b+U32(e+28); len=U32(e+32); ks_fkern[f]=b+U32(e+36); ks_fnk[f]=U32(e+40) ks_gpx[f]=MAlloc(len*2+2); expand: gpx[2i]=(p[i]>>4)*17; gpx[2i+1]=(p[i]&15)*17 (the v1 loop, unchanged) The pixel offsets already include the range slice, so one gpx per face is enough (the lazy variant keeps one per range, see below). Read the U32 fields with MemCpy on Aiwnios (as v1 does for len ) or use the aligned (b+off)(U32*)[i] ; every offset is 4-aligned. Initialise len=0 (Aiwnios). Sizes (bytes; faces in file order; kerning on) Face A B C B expanded (ks_gpx) Regular 13 14,268 30,087 36,286 41,726 Bold 13 15,148 32,591 39,201 46,774 Regular 11 11,855 24,708 29,621 31,472 Bold 22 31,242 69,866 85,136 119,596 Regular 26 37,596 84,738 103,670 148,820 Bold 26 40,887 93,142 113,800 165,516 Regular 22 29,136 64,523 78,591 108,718 Bold 44 100,367 236,314 290,569 451,164 File 281,048 636,524 777,432 1,113,786 A has 258 glyph slots a face (33 ranges), B 559 (37 ranges), C 654 (41 ranges). C is measured, not estimated. Without kerning the files are 18,308 bytes smaller each (2.9 percent of B); kerning is in (407 to 784 pairs a face, 1.6 to 3.1 KB). v1 for comparison: 85,701 bytes, 159 KB expanded. Expanded totals: A 462,174, B 1,113,786, C 1,375,820. Largest face (Bold 44) pixel data: 225,582 packed bytes in B, which is why v1's U16 offsets cannot hold it. Guest memory: the VM has 1024 MB and the prompt shows about 799 MiB free; the desk at scale 2 holds up to 5 styles of 2 wallpapers at 20.7 MB (about 207 MB). Set B expanded is 1.1 MB, 0.14 percent of the free heap, so it fits with no lazy loading. Expansion costs 3 ms for 556 KB packed on the x86 VM (the tS clock) and under 1 ms on Aiwnios. The serial copy of the file into the RAM drive ( serial-send.py ) took 29 s for all 636,524 bytes of set B including 7 s of fixed waits, about 29 KB/s, against about 3 s for v1: a one-off cost per image build. Tiers are in the file so a later change can keep tier 0 resident (462 KB expanded) and expand tiers 1 and 2 on first use: allocate gpx per range, point it at expanded - slice_offset * 2 , so gpx + off * 2 is unchanged. Fonts and licences Sources are assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf and Inter-Bold.ttf (Inter 3.019, the two files gen-font.py used from the puter-ui checkout, byte identical: md5 ea587988... and ba74cc32...) with OFL-Inter.txt (SIL OFL 1.1, copyright 2020 The Inter Project Authors; copied from the Inter licence file in the cosmic-text 0.19.0 crate in the cargo registry). Inter is unmodified; the atlas is a rendering of it. Coverage: every code point of the three sets except U+2714 and U+2718 (heavy check and X), which gen-font2.py draws as strokes ( VECTOR ), U+0149 and U+03A2 (deprecated, unassigned; stored as absent). Inter has U+2713 and U+2717 itself. System fonts with these two glyphs on this Mac (Menlo, Arial Unicode, Zapf Dingbats) are not OFL and were not used. UTF-8 in HolyC source (tested on TempleOS V5.03 in QEMU and on Aiwnios, same results) Source stays ASCII; text is UTF-8 bytes; a literal writes each byte as \xHH : "LiberOS \xCE\xB1" . Tool: python3 scripts/ks-utf8.py -s 'LiberOS α' --name PRODUCT --check . | Case | Both builds | | "\xCE\xB1" | 2 bytes CE B1, StrLen 2 | | \x length | at most two digits: "\xB1A" is B1 41, "\xCEabc" is CE 61 62 63 | | adjacent literals "\xCE\xB1" "x" | joined, 3 bytes | | \d or \x24 | the dollar sign (needed for DolDoc safety) | | octal "\316\261" and "\u03B1" | not escapes, no error : the text stays as backslash and digits (8 and 6 bytes). Never use them | | StrLen, StrCpy, MemCpy, StrNew, StrPrint %s | bytes above 0x7F survive; StrCmp is unsigned | | raw UTF-8 in source (comment or literal) | compiles and survives, but keep it out: editors and DolDoc may rewrite it | | loader: Rx over COM1 | all 256 byte values arrive intact (checked, 0 differences), so the loader does not alter bytes | A DolDoc code does not carry bytes, so it is not used. Traps: U+0000 cannot be in a string; % needs %% when the literal is a Print format ( --fmt ); a literal in "..." lines, not char constants ( 'a' ); never cut a string inside a sequence (Wrap does, see below). Decoder contract for Txt, TW, Wrap (phase 2) Decode UTF-8 from the U8 string; ASCII (below 0x80) is one byte as today. Lead bytes C2 to DF, E0 to EF, F0 to F4 with 1, 2, 3 continuation bytes; overlong forms, surrogates (U+D800 to DFFF) and values above U+10FFFF are invalid. The reference is utf8_decode in font2_ref.py, tested against Python's errors='replace' on 4,000 random byte strings. Each invalid or truncated sequence draws one U+FFFD and resumes at the byte that broke it (it consumes the valid prefix, at least one byte). Code points below U+0020 and U+007F to U+009F draw nothing and have no advance (as v1 skips them). A code point without a glyph draws U+FFFD. Combining marks (U+0300 block) are out of scope: they have no glyph and draw U+FFFD, so text must be NFC (the host does unicodedata.normalize ). Pen position in 1/16 px; TW runs the same decode and kerning as Txt , so widths match. Wrap breaks only at a space byte and must never cut inside a sequence: where it limits a line to 190 bytes, step back over bytes 0x80 to 0xBF and the lead byte. CW takes a code point. Notes keeps bytes; caret and delete step over a whole sequence (optional in phase 2).

Follows kamiji-on-templeos.md (route R2, host-baked sprites; it is the permanent fallback there). Differences from that study: it did not find the creator (below); sprites are RGB565 with keyed transparency, not 16-colour KSCHAR.BIN ; they are rendered with the browser engine and three.js from the kamiji repo, not Blender; they cross the hub in base64 chunks instead of a file push (thumbnails are small). Licence: characters are CC BY-NC 4.0 with unresolved provenance rows, so this stays local use. What the Kamiji are (all under /Users/paulbloch/Documents/github/kamiji ) 31 characters, GLB only: the Kamiji hand assets/kamiji.glb , 14 Kamikin assets/mochi/*.glb (index.json: id, name, species, persona, clips; six face PNGs each in *.faces/ ), 16 Rubbernose assets/rubbernose/*.glb . No standing portrait, turntable or thumbnail image exists for any of them (checked kamiji, kamae art-source, kosmos-engine/assets/kamikin = baked source folders, not images). kamiji-demo , kamiji-game , kamiji-rig , kechimyaku-lineage-nexus hold no creator and no character files of this family. No LFS: the GLBs are real files on disk; nothing was pulled. The creator tool The Studio , kamiji/site/studio/ (README there): a no-build static page, prototype status. Parts, 35 morph sliders, colours, accessories, expressions, poses, roster, JSON and GLB export, all 31 bases. It needs three.js 0.186.1, which its import map takes from jsdelivr; kamiji/node_modules/three (same version) is on disk, so no download is needed. It has no URL parameter for a character and no host save: it keeps the current character in localStorage key kamiji.studio.current.v1 and its roster in ...roster.v1 , and exports by download. The hub makes it work without editing the kamiji repo: svc_kamiji.py runs a read-only loopback server (thread, 127.0.0.1, free port; serves only site/ , assets/ , node_modules/three/ ), rewrites the import map to the local copy, injects a script that seeds the chosen character and posts every change to /__kamiji/save (per-start token, Host check, 256 KB cap), which writes <work>/chars/<id>.json . Verified in headless Chrome: Pip opens in the Studio with its 3D view, offline ( shots/kamiji-creator-1.png ; first paint is slow under software WebGL). Saving does not re-bake the sprite in v1 (a card keeps its template sprite until kamiji_bake.py runs again; the creator JSON is kept). Launch: the guest shows the URL in its own Browser app ( edit reply, mode browser ). Fallback edit ID window : the hub runs open URL after a second approval. No child process is started for the server; Chrome is started only by bake , through browser/host/engine.py (throwaway profile, pipe, no debugging port, stopped by its own pid). Gate if three.js is missing: cd /Users/paulbloch/Documents/github/kamiji && npm ci (about 228 MB, downloads from npm; never run by the service, it answers ERR with that text). Files apps-host/hub/svc_kamiji.py (service, one edit in hostd.py build_hub : import svc_kamiji and hub.reg.add(svc_kamiji.Kamiji(cfg)) ), kamiji_bake.py , tests/test_kamiji.py (20 tests, python3 -I apps-host/hub/tests/test_kamiji.py ). Config (all optional): kamiji_repo , kamiji_work (default ~/.cache/kosmos-hostd/kamiji : sprites/ , chars/ , user.json ; git-ignored by location). Bake: python3 -I apps-host/hub/kamiji_bake.py [--sheet shots/kamiji-grid-1.png] (about 3 s for 31). Protocol (hub wire: REQ id kamiji token op args ; records TAB text, ASCII) op args reply list [offset [count<=24]] KH total offset n creator_ready baked , then K id name species family pose kind baked edited persona (kind builtin or user) info id KI id name species family persona pose kind baked edited thumb id S\|M\|L [offset] [fmt] SPR id size fmt w h total crc offset n base64 (6000 raw bytes per reply; ask offset += n until total) path id size PATH id size abs_path bytes (Aiwnios reads the file, no chunks) edit id [window] EDIT id mode url port , or APPROVE new name [template] [window] NEW id name template then EDIT ... ; the id is u-<slug> ; APPROVE comes before anything is created status , bake , studio_stop STAT repo creator n baked port saves bake_running done/total note ; BAKE started 0/31 (APPROVE first); STOPPED No delete in v1. Approval scopes (token goes in the retry): exec:kamiji-studio:<repo> (server start, kept for the session), exec:open:<url> (window, used once), exec:kamiji-bake:<repo> (used once). The sentence in the APPROVE record names exactly what starts. hello stops the server and clears grants. The server also stops after 30 minutes idle. Sprite record KSPR v1, little endian, 16-byte header: "KSPR" , u8 ver 1, u8 fmt, u16 w, u16 h, u16 flags 0, u32 crc32 of payload. fmt 2 (default, all sizes): u16 words, row-major; 0xF81F is followed by a u16 count of transparent pixels, any other word is an RGB565 pixel (alpha cut at 128). fmt 1 (on request): alpha plane (4 bits, even pixel in the low nibble) then w*h RGB565, 115 KB at L. Sizes S 64x80, M 128x160, L 192x240 (hero). Standing pose: the idle clip at t=0, front, 14 degree turn, transparent canvas. Guest decode: loop over words, ks_fb write per pixel or skip the run. Pipeline numbers (31 characters, measured) size min / avg / max bytes all 31 avg on the wire (base64) at 16 KB/s S 2,490 / 3,810 / 4,944 118 KB 5.1 KB 0.31 s each, 9.6 s all M 9,100 / 14,346 / 19,090 445 KB 19.1 KB 1.2 s each, 36 s all L 20,000 / 31,587 / 42,476 979 KB 42.1 KB 2.6 s each (detail only) Native Aiwnios: path plus a file read, under 1 ms each. Use S for the grid cards (lazy, visible ones first, about 10 s for a full grid), M for 2x screens and the selected card, L for a detail view. Contact sheet: shots/kamiji-grid-1.png . PHASE B plan (applied after the merge; shared files) Page and tab. AppSettings ( desk3/03-apps.HC , tab names ks_sp_name[5] at line 96, now Appearance, Display, Dock, About, Menu bar): add "Kamiji" as page 5 and raise the count; add KamijiPage(x,y,w,h) in a new desk3/03q-kamiji.HC (loaded before the apps) so 03-apps changes stay at three lines (name, count, dispatch). Header and cards. Title, a New button (plus icon) at the right. Scroll with the page; 24 per page of list . Icons. Add pencil and plus (and user-plus optional) to scripts/gen-icons.py , regenerate KSICONS.BIN , add ids to the icon enum; follow the Icon Style editor rules. Hub calls through HostCall("kamiji",op,args,owner,tok) ( 03h-hostlink.HC ), results read in the owner's tick via HlDeliver . One reader rule: HostPoll reads the port only while a call is pending and the v1 browser reads whenever it is open: open the Browser tab first, then Kamiji calls and the Browser must not poll at once; keep one call in flight, thumbnail chunks queued from the page's Tick. The reply is capped at HL_MAXRX 12000: chunks of 6000 raw bytes fit. Lazy load. On page open: list ; queue thumb id S 0 for visible cards; assemble chunks into a malloc'd buffer per card (CRC check, KSPR decode into a 64x80 U16 plus a key); cache in memory for the session; progress ring on a card until it is decoded. Placeholder: a grey silhouette. Edit and New. Edit sends edit id ; New opens a one-field name prompt, then new name template (template = the selected card, else kamikin-kon ). On APPROVE show the guest prompt with the hub's sentence and Allow/Cancel, retry with the token. On EDIT open the URL in the Browser app (new tab, docs/web-apps.md ); if it fails offer "Open in a window" ( edit id window , second approval). States. Error: creator_ready 0 or ERR text: "Creator not available: see docs/kamiji-tab.md" with the ERR note below. Hub down: the existing hub-offline state. Aiwnios parity. hostlink-aiw.HC runs the request through hostd.py --call --rec , so the page code is shared; for thumb use path and read the file with the platform file read instead of chunks. The decoder is integer only (RGB565), identical on both builds. Gates. kslint.py clean; x86 and Aiwnios first-frame shots of the Settings Kamiji page with 31 cards ( shots/kamiji-settings-x86.png , ...-aiw.png ); hash equal for the grid with fixture sprites; Edit opens the Studio in the Browser with the right character; New creates u-... and shows a card; approval prompts shown and refused cleanly; full grid loads in under 15 s on serial; no frame stalls while thumbnails stream.
