P1. - Drag and drop. P2; menus cover v1. - Unicode. The guest font is ASCII-only Inter bitmaps. Mail names and bodies are often non-ASCII. Plan: transliterate on the host for display, keep full UTF-8 in the host cache, mark lossy spots. Real fix: the glyph service in the browser plan. 9. Shared data with Contacts Completion. Compose To, Cc and Bcc call the contacts search with the typed prefix (limit 8). Only name and address come back. Sender card. "Show contact" in the reader fetches the card for the exact normalised address. "Add to contacts" is a prompt that opens the editor pre-filled. Contracts. The Kosmos OS repo puts OS-owned PIM data behind typed intents ( docs/app-platform-plan.md , principle 4), with os.contacts@1 first and os.mail@1 after (Phase 4). Mail calls the contact contract, never the store. The HolyC build uses the same message shapes over the channel until an intent bus exists. Only shared key: the lower-cased, trimmed email address. 10. Optional AI features (host, separate) Thread summaries and draft replies, off by default, in a separate host process. A draft is inserted into compose only and never sent. The model sees only the text the user selects. Nothing is logged. Milestone M9, optional. 11. Milestones and gates Test setup, no real account: aiosmtpd (Apache-2.0) on 127.0.0.1:1025 recording messages, and GreenMail (Apache-2.0, needs Java) or a small Python IMAP fixture on 127.0.0.1:1143. Fixture mailbox: 2,000 synthetic messages with UTF-8 names, attachments, HTML-only bodies, quoted replies, a tracking pixel, a phishing mismatch and a 10 MB attachment. ID Scope Gate (pass or fail) Effort M0 Host skeleton, framing, fixtures, CI job Pass: 100 round trips of MAIL_ACCOUNTS and MAIL_FOLDERS with injected CRC errors, zero corruption; fixtures start with one command S M1 Read-only IMAP: folders, headers, bodies to text Pass: 2,000 headers listed in under 2 s on host; text blocks match goldens for 20 messages; Himalaya agrees on subjects and flags M M2 Guest reader and list on the framework Pass: first 200 headers shown and any message opened in under 1 s at channel rate; no clipped text at 2x; scripted keyboard drive passes M M3 Compose and SMTP send behind the prompt Pass: message with attachment arrives at aiosmtpd with correct MIME; a send with a forged token is refused; Undo cancels inside the window M M4 Actions and bulk prompts, sync-back Pass: each action changes fixture state; bulk over one message always prompts; replayed token refused; UIDVALIDITY change clears cache M M5 Search, cache, offline view, outbox Pass: 100 SEARCH queries match a local filter; with the host stopped, cached lists and bodies open; outbox sends after restart M M6 Real provider (user-run): OAuth 2 or app password, keychain Pass: connect, list, and send one message to the user's own address after an explicit yes; log grep finds no token. Needs the user's go. M M7 HTML safety, remote-content block, phishing lines, attachment prompts Pass: 50-message HTML corpus (script, form, remote image, tracker) makes zero outbound connections in a recording proxy and emits no script M M8 JMAP spike (Fastmail), optional Pass: same list and send gates pass over JMAP; decision recorded M M9 AI summaries (optional) Pass: off by default; stubbed model output only enters compose; no mail text in logs S Plan of record: M0 to M5 and M7 on fixtures; M6 needs the user's approval; M8 and M9 optional. Each gate runs on the x86 (QEMU) and Apple Silicon (Aiwnios) builds. 12. Risks HolyC speed. Long folders under emulation. Mitigation: pages of 50, frame budget, measured at M2. Non-ASCII. Transliteration loses names. Mitigation: host keeps full text; glyph service is the real fix. Provider drift (OAuth and IMAP behaviour changes). Mitigation: M6 re-run before release; pinned libraries. Channel rate for header listings. Mitigation: compact binary records. Scope creep into HTML mail. Mitigation: section 6 rules; no HTML rendering. Licences of mail-parser and mblaze unconfirmed. Mitigation: not used until checked. 13. Effort M0 to M5 about 6 to 8 engineer-weeks, after the framework work (text field, list view, split view, dialogs) lands; M6 1 to 2 weeks with the user; M7 one week; M8 and M9 about a week together. The framework prerequisites dominate the schedule. 14. Verified versus memory Verified in this pass: GitHub licences and latest tags for Himalaya, neomutt, aerc, mblaze, Stalwart, imap-codec, mailparse, mail-parser, jmap-client, aiosmtpd, GreenMail; RFC 9051 title and status (rfc-editor); Fastmail IMAP, SMTP, CardDAV and JMAP availability (Fastmail help pages, via search); Gmail undo and scheduled send (third-party guides only). From memory, not re-checked: RFC numbers other than 9051 (5321, 6409, 6154, 5256, 7162, 8314, 8621, 6749, 8601, 2045 to 2049, 5322); Hey's screener behaviour; Gmail OAuth scope names; Thunderbird's MPL-2.0 licence; the PSF licence of the stdlib; the keyring package.

t: Font Manager: plan
h: Font Manager: plan
x: Font Manager: plan Status: plan, not code. Branch task/templeos-shell. Written 2026-10-27. Read with docs/browser-architecture.md section h5a (the font stages A to D) and h6 (non-Latin runs), docs/apps/music.md (channel families), and docs/apps/00-kosmos-os-primitives.md (no os.fonts@1 contract exists yet). Tags: [V] checked in a repo or on this Mac, file named. [R] from a web search this session (snippets, URL given). [M] from memory, to verify. 1. Purpose A desk app that lists the fonts the user chooses, previews any text in any of them at any size, and activates a font for the desk's own apps (Notes, the browser, slides). The guest never parses a font file. The host scans, validates and rasterises. The guest receives bitmaps, metrics and coverage tables. "Activate" means: the desk's font table gains a family the apps can request by name. It does not install a font into macOS. 2. Features Reference set: Font Book, FontBase, Typeface. Priority Feature Reference P0 List families and styles from chosen folders and the system font folders (read-only) FontBase keeps files where they are and shows them without a system install [R] (fontba.se/learn/font-activation) P0 Activate and deactivate per font; active set survives restart FontBase: new fonts start inactive, active ones return at launch [R] (fontba.se/learn/font-activation) P0 Preview: editable sample text, size slider, weight picker Typeface preview settings [R] (thesweetbits.com/tools/typeface/) P0 Metadata: name, version, licence name, weight, glyph count Font Book info panel (not fetched) P1 Charset grid: glyphs by Unicode block, with coverage Typeface organisation [R] P1 Collections, tags, search FontBase free tier includes collections and watched folders [R] (fontba.se/learn/font-activation) P1 Variable fonts: axis sliders, named instances Typeface (variable fonts not checked) [M] P1 Compare two fonts side by side Typeface Compare [R] (thesweetbits.com/tools/typeface/) P2 OpenType features (stylistic sets, figures) FontBase shows features, free tier [R] P2 Google Fonts catalogue, downloads from the host FontBase and Typeface both integrate Google Fonts [R]; a download is a PROMPT (section 9) Out Cloud sync, auto-activate for other apps Typeface's auto-activation and paid tiers [R]: not in scope Typeface is Mac-only and paid [R]. FontBase is cross-platform with a paid tier [R]. Font Book is free and built in, and reviewers call it basic [R] (thesweetbits.com), but we did not open Apple's guide. Pricing and tiers change, so none of them is a dependency. 3. Architecture text Copy TempleOS guest (HolyC) Mac host (Python font service, sandboxed workers) FontApp: list, preview, activate font index: SQLite (path hash, metadata, licence) active-font table, atlas cache (RAM) scan: user folders, /System/Library/Fonts (read-only) <-- channel --> validate (worker process, limits, timeout) render: Pillow/FreeType atlases; CoreText runs (RUNIMG) variable instances: fontTools instancer [M] Rules: Parsing happens on the host only , in a worker process with CPU time, memory and file-size limits. The guest never receives a font file for a user or system font. Rendering is the host's job. The host draws text in a font at a size and weight, and sends a bitmap atlas or a run image. Only validated results reach the guest. A failed font shows a reason ("table glyf truncated") and is never rendered. 3.1 Host tools Installed [V]: Python 3.13, fontTools (MIT [R], pypi.org/project/fonttools), Pillow (its ImageFont uses FreeType [M]). Not installed [V]: the Python freetype binding. Not checked: CoreText via PyObjC, HarfBuzz. CoreText covers macOS runs, so HarfBuzz is needed only for our own rasteriser, which we do not plan to build. 4. Three ways to get glyphs to the guest Option How Cost Verdict A. Build-time atlases (the current pipeline) scripts/gen-font.py rasterises Inter into assets/KSFONT.BIN at 4 sizes and 2 scales, ASCII only [V] zero at run time; fixed set; baked into the boot image keep for built-in faces B. Host atlases per request the host rasterises a family at a size, weight and range, sends it over the channel, and the guest caches it by hash link time per new size; needs a cache use for user and system fonts C. Port stb_truetype to HolyC and ship TTF bytes the guest parses fonts and draws any size a port of about 5,000 lines of C (brief figure, [M]; check the header); font bytes in guest RAM; untrusted parsing in the guest breaks rule 1; no shaping defer , only for trusted built-in OFL fonts at M6 (browser h5a stage D) stb_truetype is a single-file library, public domain or MIT, dual licensed per file [R] (github.com/nothings/stb). That makes option C legally clean; the problem is safety and size, not licence. 4.1 Atlas format Current format [V: scripts/gen-font.py docstring]: per face, one byte ascent, one byte line height, then 95 records of U16 advance (1/16 px), U8 w, U8 h, I8 bearing x, I8 bearing y, U16 offset , then U32 data length and 4-bit alpha pixels. The U16 offset is a limit. Measured on this machine with the current script [V: run in a scratch folder]: the eight ASCII faces hold 3.0, 3.4, 2.3, 8.6, 10.5, 11.8, 7.7 and 32.2 KB of pixel data. The largest face is 32,237 bytes, half the 65,535-byte offset range. Browser stage B (about 350 glyphs, roughly 3.7 times the ASCII set [browser-architecture h5a]) would take the 44 px face to about 120 KB [estimate], and the offsets would wrap silently. Format v2 (proposal): U32 offsets, one page per 64 KB, and a family header with the Unicode ranges present. Every guest atlas carries its own version byte, so the v1 faces keep working during migration. 4.2 Atlas cache Key: SHA-256 over (font file hash, face index, variation axes, size, weight, scale, code range, renderer version). Host cache under the user's cache folder. Guest RAM cache with a budget (browser budget reused, section d3 in browser-architecture). The guest sends HAVE with the hashes it holds, so a reconnect costs nothing. Cost check with the measured numbers: an ASCII atlas for one family at four sizes is about 20 to 60 KB [estimate, from the table above]. At the reported 47 KB/s serial rate that is about 1 s. At the old 1.4 to 2.7 KB/s lockstep rate it is 10 to 40 s. So the channel spike gate (50 KB/s) decides whether option B is interactive. Without the gate it is a background fetch with a placeholder face. 5. Non-Latin text and emoji Latin, Greek, Cyrillic (stage B): atlases in format v2 from Inter, which covers them [V: browser h5a; coverage to confirm in the font file]. Everything else (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai, any font the user adds): a run image (RUNIMG, browser 0x09 and h6). The host shapes and draws the run in the font with CoreText, sends an alpha mask and the colour token, and the guest caches it by hash. Cost estimate from h6: a 20-character CJK run is about 8 KB compressed. Emoji : Apple Color Emoji ships with macOS and its font terms restrict redistribution [M]. We render emoji on the host only and send RUNIMG RGBA. We never bundle it. Noto Color Emoji is an open alternative, licence to be checked [M]. Encoding : the guest is 8-bit HolyC text. The font manager shows UTF-8 names by sending them as a pre-rendered label or a transliterated ASCII name. Typed input in the preview field is ASCII in v1. 6. Variable fonts The host reads the fvar table and its named instances. For a requested axis set (for example wght 620 and wdth 100), it makes a static instance with fontTools' instancer [M: fontTools.varLib.instancer ], then rasterises that. The guest sees each instance as an ordinary face, with a name like "Family Bold 620". Slider changes are debounced to 150 ms so the link is not flooded while dragging. 7. System fonts and redistribution macOS system fonts (in /System/Library/Fonts and /Library/Fonts ) are listed and previewed on the host only. Their licence terms restrict redistribution and extraction [M, Apple's font terms not checked]. Rule: the host may render a system font for the local user's preview. It must not write those glyphs into the repo, the boot image, the test fixtures or any shared file. The boot image stamp in scripts/image-path.sh lists its inputs explicitly [V]; system-font atlases are excluded from it. User-added fonts follow their own licence. The index stores the licence name from the font's name table (nameID 13 and 14) [M] and shows it. ls of /System/Library/Fonts and /Library/Fonts gives about 134 entries together [V; includes folder headers, so approximate]. Design the list for hundreds of files. 8. Licence hygiene in the repo assets/ holds KSFONT.BIN , KSICONS.BIN and LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt [V]. No OFL text is in the repo. The Inter licence the atlas uses is required by OFL 1.1 to travel with the font. Add assets/licenses/OFL-Inter.txt before the next image build. scripts/gen-font.py reads Inter from an absolute path outside the repo, /Users/paulbloch/Documents/github/puter-ui/src/gui/src/fonts [V]. Vendor the two files it uses, or record their checksums and source in a README, so the build does not depend on another checkout. That folder holds nine Inter weights (Black, Bold, ExtraBold, ExtraLight, Light, Medium, Regular, SemiBold, Thin) [V]. The generator uses two. Record which weights are intended. OFL reserved font names: Inter's name is not reserved in what we checked [M]; any modified Inter must be renamed if it is distributed. We do not modify it. 9. Activation, consent and the channel Message family 0x30 to 0x3F (proposal; the browser uses 0x01 to 0x14 and music uses 0x20 to 0x2F). Code Name Payload 0x30 FONT_LIST (H to G) font id, family, style, weight, width, source (system, user, google), glyph count, licence name. No bytes 0x31 FONT_QUERY (G to H) view, filter, sort, offset, count 0x32 PREVIEW (G to H) font id, axes, text (ASCII, up to 256 bytes), size, scale, colour token 0x33 ATLAS (H to G) hash, font id, size, weight, scale, range, format v2 data 0x34 ACTIVATE (G to H) font id, on or off; the host stores the active set 0x35 COVERAGE (H to G) code ranges present, for the charset grid 0x36 VALIDATE (H to G) ok, or a reason string, and the table that failed 0x37 ADD_FOLDER (G to H) a path chosen in a host dialog; the guest only asks, the host shows the dialog 0x2C, 0x0D, 0x0E PROMPT and answer shared with music and the browser Activation is local, and it changes what the desk's apps see, so it needs no PROMPT. Adding a Google Fonts download, a folder outside the user's home, or any write outside the cache is a PROMPT showing the file name, size and source, with the default "no". Install of a font into macOS is never done. Apps consume families by name: FontFace(family, weight, size, scale) returns a face id from the active table, or falls back to the built-in Inter face and records the miss. Browser pages use the same table. Slides ( DeckDoc fontFamily ) and Notes do the same [V: primitives 3, DeckDoc schema]. 10. UI mockup (window about 900 by 560) text Copy | Font Manager [ search families ] | | COLLECTIONS | Inter OFL 1.1 active [x]| | All (412) | Regular Medium SemiBold Bold Black | | Active (6) | | | Serif | Preview text: [The quick brown fox 0123 ] | | Mono | | | SOURCE | Size [ o ] 24 Weight [ Regular v ] | | System (371) | | | User (38) | The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. | | Google (3) | ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ | | | abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz 0123456789 !?@#$% | | | | | | Glyphs: 384 (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic) [ Charset ] [ Compare ]| | Active: Inter, IBM Plex Sans, Source Serif 4 Adds folder ... | Example names are placeholders for the mockup. The active toggle is the [x] control; a non-Latin sample shows a run image with a "rendered on host" label. 11. Framework needs Virtual list with family rows, search field, collections sidebar, slider (exists [V: Slider in 02-ui.HC]), toggle, a segmented control for weight, a text field with caret for preview input. A glyph grid (charset) with block headers, drawn from COVERAGE. An atlas blit with scale 1 or 2 [V: the desk draws at 1 or 2 with ks_s ]. The channel client and the PROMPT dialog shared with Music. 12. Milestones and gates Milestone Work Gate F0 atlas format spike format v2 writer on host, reader in HolyC; one family, four sizes guest atlas matches the host render within one level per pixel, on x86 and Aiwnios (golden method in aiwnios/README.md ) F1 host index and validation scan, SQLite index, sandbox worker 500 fonts indexed; 2,000 corrupted copies of Inter (byte flips, truncation) give no crash and no hang, each with a reason F2 guest Font Manager list, search, preview, activate activating a font makes it selectable in Notes F3 user fonts and variable instances ATLAS for user fonts, instancer, charset grid wght 400 and 700 instances render, with distinct atlas hashes F4 browser stage B Latin-1, Ext-A, Greek, Cyrillic in format v2 the German and Russian article gate in browser h5a F5 run images CoreText runs for CJK, Arabic, emoji one CJK run and one emoji run legible at 2x F6 Google Fonts catalogue fetch on the host, OFL only, PROMPT for each download a download prompt shows name and size before any byte moves Every phase needs the owner's go. F0 is the cheapest decision: it proves or kills option B before any UI is built. 13. Test plan Golden atlases. For each built-in face and two user fonts, the atlas hash is stored; a change needs a reason. Metadata golden. The index output for a fixed folder (the Inter set and two Google fonts we vendor) as JSON, compared on each run. Fuzz. Byte flips and truncations of Inter in the scratch folder (never committed), with a 10 s timeout and 256 MB memory cap per worker. Pass: no crash, no hang, a reason for each failure. Licence check. A script fails the build if any bundled font lacks its OFL text in assets/licenses/ . Boot. KS-READY stays in the 0.5 to 0.7 s range recorded for Aiwnios [V: aiwnios/README.md] after each stage. Parity. golden.py on x86 and Aiwnios for the Font Manager window, once it exists. 14. Risks Parsing risk. FreeType and fontTools are C and Python code that parse hostile input [M]. Mitigation: worker sandbox, limits, no guest parsing, patch the library as CVEs appear. Redistribution. System fonts and Apple Color Emoji. Mitigation: host-only rendering, exclusion from the image stamp and repo (section 7). Link cost. A family at four sizes can be tens of KB. Mitigation: the F0 gate decides; placeholders while atlases stream. Offset wrap (section 4.1). Mitigation: format v2 with a version byte, tested with a 44 px stress face. Font count. Hundreds of families can overwhelm the guest's RAM. Mitigation: the active set is capped (16 faces, a number to check) and atlases are evicted by LRU. Text encoding. 8-bit guest text. Mitigation: names transliterated, non-ASCII shown as run images. Stale boot image. New font assets not in scripts/image-path.sh leave an old image in use. Mitigation: add them to the stamp in the same change. 15. Verified and from memory Verified here: the desk3 font loader and constants ( desk3/01-core.HC lines 1007 to 1060, FontLoad , TW , Txt ); scripts/gen-font.py record format and its external Inter path; the atlas sizes (measured by running the generator in a scratch folder); the assets folder contents; the image stamp inputs ( scripts/image-path.sh ); the nine Inter files; the Python tool presence (fontTools, Pillow; no freetype); the Kosmos OS primitives (no os.fonts@1 , shell font presets); the browser h5a and h6 plans. From web searches (snippets only): FontBase (fontba.se/learn/font-activation), Typeface (thesweetbits.com/tools/typeface/), stb_truetype licence (github.com/nothings/stb), fontTools licence (pypi.org/project/fonttools). From memory, not checked: Font Book's features; Apple's font licence; Apple Color Emoji and Noto Color Emoji licences; the fontTools instancer API name; FreeType and fontTools CVE history; the 5,000-line stb_truetype size; the active-set cap of 16. Not run: any rasterised atlas for the guest, any worker sandbox, the VM with the font manager.

t: Icon Style Editor (app "Icons", desk3/03c-iconstyle.HC)
h: Icon Style Editor (app "Icons", desk3/03c-iconstyle.HC)
x: Icon Style Editor (app "Icons", desk3/03c-iconstyle.HC) Open it with the dock icon (paintbrush) or the i key. Left: every app icon at Large (56), Dock (the Settings icon size, at most 56) and Small (24) on a light and a dark backdrop. Right: presets, ten pages of controls, Reset, Export, Import. Every change reaches the preview and the real dock at once (one style, one DrawIconTile ). Controls (page: what) Shape : corner radius (0 square to 100 circle), presets Square, Round, Squircle, Circle, squircle corners toggle (superellipse, exponent 4). Fill : Solid, Linear (angle), Radial; 2 or 3 stops, each a swatch (lighter, tile colour, darker, 11 fixed colours); middle stop position. Scheme : App accents, Mono, Duo, Pastel, Vivid, Sunset, Ocean, Gold, Desktop (follows the current desktop style), Custom; a 12 by 4 hue and lightness palette picks colour A and B; "one shared colour" uses A for every tile. Tone : hue shift, saturation, brightness. Depth : bevel strength and size, gloss band, inner shadow, "preview all pressed". Shadow : drop shadow opacity, offset, blur; tilt (vertical squash) and reflection. Glyph : stroke weight, filled shapes (0 is outline), size, offset x and y, colour (auto contrast, white, dark, tint). Border : ring width, colour, opacity; glass tile (see-through, the dock pill and its blurred backdrop show through) and its opacity. Extras : outer glow and radius, grain, fade when the app is closed, hover lift, glyph shadow, glyph glow. Layout : dock tile size (Settings value), gap between tiles, name label on hover, "Time rebuild". Presets: Default, Flat, Glass, Soft (neumorphic), Pop (gradient), 3D (skeuomorphic), Mono (line), Temple. Reset returns style and layout to the defaults. Keyboard: Tab or Down next control, Up previous, Left and Right adjust (or choose), Space or Enter toggles and presses, Page Up and Down change page, m times a rebuild. Hover a preview tile for lift and its name; press on it for the pressed look. Style string KSI1 followed by every parameter that differs from its default, as a two letter key and a number: KSI1 rd50 sq1 fl2 sc7 bv40 gl25 sd40 so3 sb6 gc2 rw1 rk1 ra50 ow30 or5 gn15 . Export writes it into Notes (and opens Notes); Import finds the first KSI1 in Notes, resets the style and applies the line. A preset is the same kind of line. Keys are in is_k (03c), ranges in is_lo and is_hi . Architecture is_v[] (the IconStyle) holds every parameter as an I64; the dock size, gap and label live in ks_dsize , ks_dgap , ks_ilabel . is_sig hashes the tile parameters; is_def says all are default. DrawIconTile(x,y,size,app,state) (state: 1 pressed, 2 inactive, 4 hover). Default style: the old direct draw (RRFill and LIcon), so the dock costs what it did. Otherwise: colour tile per (app, size, signature, state) in a 256 slot two-way cache; shared planes per size (shape alpha, bevel bands, gloss, inner shadow, ring, grain, shadow and glow with a margin, radial index, row spans) built once per shape; glyph masks cached per (icon, size, weight, fill). A tile is built from Fill32 , a 64 entry ramp stepped in 16.16 fixed point (two pixels a store), and KsBlendA2D through the planes. A frame blits: shadow and glow planes, per row the soft edge pixels, then Copy32 (or LerpRow for glass) of the opaque run. Nothing is rebuilt while the signature is unchanged. Sizes are quantised to multiples of 4 native pixels so a magnifying dock reuses tiles. The dock reaches DrawIconTile through the pointer ks_ictile (a call through a forward declaration does not reach a later definition on either HolyC). Aiwnios: same file, no asm, integer paths; see aiwnios/drive-icons.HC for the headless driver. Numbers QEMU x86 at 2880x1800 (ms a frame, average, before with 11 apps and after with 12 apps and the Icons app, default style): dock sweep warm 3.2 and 3.7, cold 4.0 and 5.0, drag large 6.5 and 6.6, drag small 4.7 and 4.7, full redraw 17.8 and 19.0. The default style takes the old direct path, so the rise is the twelfth icon and the wider dock. Rebuilding the 12 dock tiles (Glass preset, 104 px tiles): 2.5 ms with the planes and glyph masks cached, 4.8 ms with every plane and mask rebuilt (Layout page, "Time rebuild", or key m ; also a serial line icons|rebuild|... ). Aiwnios on Apple Silicon: 0.1 to 0.9 ms and 0.2 to 1.6 ms depending on the preset. Nothing is built while the style is unchanged; a frame only blits. Limits Tilt is a vertical squash with a reflection, not a perspective. Glass uses the dock pill, so it shows blur only where the dock is translucent. Import reads Notes, not a file. Colours of Desktop scheme and tiles follow the desktop style; the default style in a dark desktop style keeps the old dark glyph. Weights above 100 percent use a blurred dilation. The Quit button is not an app tile and is unchanged.

t: Maps app: plan
h: Maps app: plan
x: Maps app: plan Status: plan only, no code. Written 2026-10-27 on task/templeos-shell . Read with docs/holyc-native-apps-plan.md and docs/browser-architecture.md sections a to d. Evidence tags: [verified] opened or run in this pass; [reported] from a search snippet or secondary source; [memory] unchecked; [estimate] our arithmetic, for the gates to confirm. 1. Purpose and users A map for the TempleOS desk that works offline once a region is loaded and draws with our own renderer. Three jobs: look at a place, find a place by name or address, and drive from A to B with a line and a turn list. Users: the desk owner, on the QEMU guest (slow, ASCII text) or Aiwnios. Offline use is the main case because the guest has no network. Not in v1: transit, live traffic, street imagery, satellite. 2. Platform facts Renderer [verified, desk3/01-core.HC ]: anti-aliased rounded rectangles ( RRFillN ), discs, one-pixel anti-aliased lines ( LineN ), shadows, a clip rectangle, and blended blits. There is no general polygon fill and no stroke wider than one pixel . Text [verified, Txt , TW ]: four Inter bitmap faces at two scales, 95 ASCII glyphs (codes 32 to 126). No glyph for ° or accented letters, so the host folds names to ASCII and the UI writes deg . Icons [verified, LIcon ]: Lucide strokes from KSICONS.BIN , usable for pins. App model [verified, 02-ui.HC , 03-apps.HC ]: apps draw in logical units, register hit regions, and use AID . The Browser ( 03b-browser.HC ) already follows it. There is no Contacts app and no map app yet. Channel [reported, browser doc b4]: about 47 KB/s on QEMU serial, to re-measure at M2; Aiwnios sockets are effectively unlimited. First paint is capped at 120 KB. Host [verified locally]: Python 3 with PIL, rsvg-convert and ImageMagick. Kosmos OS [verified, /Users/paulbloch/kosmos-os-frame ]: src/apps/maps/ uses Leaflet. MapCanvas.tsx loads tile.openstreetmap.org directly; server/services/mapsService.ts uses the public Nominatim and the OSRM demo server. Those data paths break the policies in section 6, so we keep the feature intent and not the endpoints. docs/apps/00-kosmos-os-primitives.md does not exist in this repo, so the desk tokens from browser h1 are used; re-check when it appears. 3. Feature inventory P0 needed for a usable first version; P1 next; P2 later. Effort S (days), M (one to two weeks), L (several weeks), one developer. Competitors: Apple Maps (apple.com/maps) and Google Maps (maps.google.com) [memory]; OsmAnd (osmand.net) [reported, GPL]; Organic Maps (organicmaps.app/terms) and CoMaps (github.com/comaps/comaps) [verified licences, section 8]. Features listed are what those apps are known for [memory]; we copy only the offline subset. Feature P Effort Notes Pan (drag, arrows), zoom (keys, wheel), zoom steps 1 to 17 P0 M Base map: land, water, roads by class, parks, buildings at high zoom P0 L Styled on the host (section 4) Road and place labels, ASCII-folded P0 M Collision in section 7 Attribution footer P0 S Legal requirement, section 6 Search by name or address in the loaded region P0 M Local geocoder, section 5 Drop pin with name and coordinates P0 S Driving route A to B: line, distance, time, turn list P0 M Local router One bundled offline region P0 S PMTiles extract built on the host Inertial pan, animated zoom P1 M Several regions, choose and remove P1 M Host manages files Saved places and recent searches P1 S Host store Reverse geocode under the pointer P1 M Local geocoder Walking and cycling routes P1 M Valhalla costing Text along roads P1 M Section 7 Rotate, compass, dash patterns P2 M Satellite imagery P2 L Raster only; licence and size Share a place, Contacts link P2 S No other app exists yet Transit (GTFS), live traffic P2 XL Not in our data Elevation profile, isochrones P2 L Valhalla features [reported] 4. Architecture (a) Host-rasterised raster tiles. The Mac draws 256 px tiles at device scale and sends them. A raw RGB565 tile is 256 x 256 x 2 = 131 KB; a 1440 x 900 view needs 24 to 30 tiles, so 3 to 4 MB, about 85 s at 47 KB/s. Run-length coding helps flat colour, not antialiased text [estimate: 10 to 30 KB per tile]. Guest CPU is tiny and fidelity is best, but text is baked in and each restyle is a full tile set. Five styles means five data sets. (b) Vector tiles drawn natively. The host sends geometry; the guest fills, strokes and labels it. A dense urban MVT tile is about 20 to 60 KB gzipped [estimate]; a compact form after zoom filtering and quantising should be 5 to 15 KB [estimate, M1 gate]. Guest CPU is the cost: protobuf decode, thousands of fills, labels. Restyling is free. (c) Hybrid (recommended). The host reads a PMTiles file (section 6) and writes our compact tile form per tile: features filtered by zoom, clipped to the tile plus a 16 px buffer, polygons pre-triangulated (earcut, section 8), and labels pre-shaped as ASCII with anchors and priorities. The guest does what is view-dependent: transform, scan triangles, stroke, cull labels, and apply one of five palettes. Raster appears only for satellite (P2) and host-side previews. Criterion (a) raster (b) vector (c) hybrid Channel per view 3 to 4 MB [estimate] 0.2 to 0.5 MB [estimate] 0.2 to 0.5 MB Guest CPU very low high medium Fidelity fixed, best crisp, restylable crisp, restylable Five styles five data sets free free (palette) Renderer work blits polygons, strokes, labels triangle scan, strokes, labels Biggest risk channel guest speed host writer complexity Recommendation: (c) . If the guest misses 200 ms per view at M3, fall back to a raster base layer with vector labels on top. Cache: the guest keeps about 64 parsed tiles (a guess to measure); the host keeps compact tiles keyed by PMTiles hash, tile id and format version. 5. Routing and geocoding All run on the Mac, reached on 127.0.0.1 by the host bridge. Nothing goes to a public server. Engine Licence Notes Valhalla MIT [reported, official repo] Routing; car, bike, foot; isochrones [reported]. First choice OSRM BSD-2 [memory] Fast car routing; keeps graph in memory [reported]. Fallback GraphHopper Apache-2.0 core [reported] Hosted API is paid and keyed; not needed Photon Apache-2.0 [verified, LICENSE] Geocoder with typeahead; needs an index built from OSM. First choice Pelias MIT [memory] Heavier Elasticsearch stack. Skip for v1 Nominatim GPL-2.0 [memory] Self-hosted only, as a separate service; fallback search Each region's routing graph and search index come from the same extract, built on the Mac. Build times and sizes are unmeasured; M0 measures them. 6. Data licences and tile policy OSM data is ODbL [reported]. Show "© OpenStreetMap contributors" on the map. Offline packs are for the owner's personal use; sharing a derived database triggers share-alike, so the about box says so. Public raster tiles at tile.openstreetmap.org [verified, operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles]: heavy use needs Operations Working Group permission; "Offline use is not permitted"; bulk prefetching is banned; access "may be blocked without prior notice"; apps must send a unique User-Agent. Not allowed. Public Nominatim [verified, operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim]: an "absolute maximum of 1 request per second"; results "must be cached on your side"; heavy users should self-host. Not allowed for search. Public OSRM demo [memory]: no service level. Not allowed. Protomaps daily builds [reported, docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads]: ODbL data, BSD-3 code, CC0 design; attribution required. A planet file is reported at about 120 GB, and sizes vary by date. pmtiles extract with a bounding box makes a regional file [reported]. Check each build's BLAKE3 hash. OpenMapTiles [reported]: BSD schema with CC BY design; credit "© MapTiler © OpenStreetMap contributors". Its layer names serve as reference. Result: the app reads only local files and local services. The footer attribution is the only visible legal item. 7. Renderer features needed Feature Today Plan Effort Anti-aliased polygon fill, triangle scan, non-zero and even-odd No ( RRFillN is a rounded rectangle) Scan host-triangulated triangles M Wide strokes (1 to 12 px), round and bevel joins, caps No ( LineN is one pixel) Discs and quads along the path, cached M Clip to tile and view Yes done Label collision: grid bins, priority, box test No M Text halo No Eight offset blits in halo colour, then the fill S Text along a path No Per-glyph placement on a polyline M, P1 Zoom animation Partial: style crossfade in 06-run.HC Show the parent tile scaled, then crossfade S Inertial pan Drag exists Velocity decay per frame S POI icons Yes ( LIcon ) done Labels are ASCII and small at scale 1, so the first version uses scale 2 labels and fewer of them. 8. Open-source reuse Project Licence Verdict and reason Protomaps PMTiles BSD-3 [verified, LICENSE] Reuse on the host: single-file tiles and extracts Protomaps basemap data ODbL data, BSD-3 code, CC0 design [reported] Reuse data with attribution earcut ISC [verified, mapbox/earcut LICENSE] Port to the host first; to HolyC only if needed; keep the notice MapLibre Native BSD-2 [reported] Reference : GL engine, cannot run in HolyC MapLibre GL JS BSD-3 [memory] Reference : style spec semantics tippecanoe not verified (memory: BSD-2) Optional for our own tile sets; check LICENSE first Organic Maps Apache-2.0 app [verified]; map data under a custom licence [reported] Reference for label logic; do not use its data CoMaps Apache-2.0 [verified]; AGPL-3.0 proposal from May 2025 [reported] Reference ; recheck the licence before copying anything OsmAnd GPL [reported] Reference only ; no code copied Valhalla, Photon MIT [reported], Apache-2.0 [verified] Use as local services OSRM, Nominatim BSD-2 [memory], GPL-2.0 [memory] Option for routing; Nominatim as a separate service only Lucide ISC [verified, assets/LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt ] Use (in the desk already) No copyleft code is ported. Apache and MIT code keeps its notice. 9. Security and privacy Location is sensitive. The guest has none. If "here" is wanted, the host reads CoreLocation only after the Mac's prompt and an in-app approval. A plain Python process may not get the prompt [memory]; test with a signed helper at M5. Remote calls : none in v1. If a later version adds one, settings name the service and the exact fields it receives. Searches, saved places and history stay on the host store (browser e4 style). Outward actions (share, open in another app) need a UI prompt. Logs record request paths and counts, never search coordinates, unless debug logging is on. 10. UI specification Tokens from browser h1: C_INK , C_ACC , C_CARD , C_BRD , C_PAGE , C_MUT ; title bar 44, toolbar 44, footer 22; F_REG and F_SMALL faces. text Copy | Maps _ [] x | <- title bar 44 | [ Search places or addresses ] (Go) [Route] [Pin] | <- toolbar 44 | | | (street and water map in our palette) | | o Pin: Harbour Cafe | | Route 4.2 km, 11 min | | [+] zoom 14 | | [-] | | (c) OpenStreetMap contributors offline: Harbour region 32.71 N 117.16 W | <- footer 22 Directions panel (left third, 320 wide): | From [Current place ] | | To [Harbour Cafe ] | | (Car) (Walk) (Bike) P1 | | 4.2 km 11 min | | 1. Head north on Pier St 0.4 km | | 2. Turn right, Bay Road 1.8 km | | 3. Arrive, on the left 4.2 km | Rules: plus and minus, arrows and Page Up and Down zoom and pan (P0); the wheel and drag too. Escape clears search, then closes directions. Search results are a list of up to eight; Enter takes the first. The attribution footer is never hidden. No ° : coordinates are written with N, S, E, W. 11. Framework needs Text field, list and toggle widgets from widget kit v2 (not built). A host map service on the browser frame format ( browser-architecture.md b1, b2) with new message types: tile, search, route. The browser's list has none of them yet. A host file service for offline packs and saved places (P1). Renderer work in section 7. 12. Milestones, gates and tests Milestone Work Gate (pass or fail) M0 Fixtures Extract a 10 km square from a Protomaps build (hash checked); record Photon results for 30 queries and Valhalla routes for 5 pairs; store under tests/fixtures/maps/ Pass: replay reproduces stored outputs; total under 60 MB M1 Tile writer Host PMTiles reader, compact form, zoom filters, triangulation Pass: 20 tiles at zoom 12 to 15: median under 10 KB, max under 40 KB; geometry within 1 device px M2 Channel 1 MB host to guest in the browser frame format, with CRC Pass: 0 CRC errors; throughput recorded against 47 KB/s M3 One tile Decode and draw one tile: polygons, strokes, labels Pass: 256 px tile with about 2000 features under 200 ms on QEMU; within 2 percent of host reference M4 Pan and zoom Tile cache, drag, wheel, keys, zoom animation, inertia Pass: no blank frame on zoom; pan step under 150 ms on QEMU; no requests for hidden tiles M5 Labels Collision, halo, priority; location helper test Pass: ten golden views with no overlaps; top 20 roads and cities labelled M6 Search and pins Photon via host; list; pins Pass: correct top result for 27 of 30 fixture queries, network unplugged M7 Routing Valhalla route, polyline, turn list Pass: line within 20 m of fixture; duration within 5 percent M8 Offline region Bundled region; footer; region choice (P1) Pass: full session offline with no outbound connections M9 Policy review Traffic and attribution audit Pass: an hour of use makes no request to tile.openstreetmap.org or a public geocoder Test plan: offline by default (tests read fixtures; a socket open fails the test). Golden screenshots from QEMU via scripts/snap.sh , compared with host renders of the same tile. Host-side protocol tests (round trip, CRC, truncation). Parser tests with a triangulation area check (within 0.5 percent). A mutation check: break one filter rule and confirm a golden fails. A policy test counts outbound hosts and fails on any host other than 127.0.0.1. 13. Risks Guest speed under QEMU may miss M3. Fallback: raster base layer. The real channel may be slower than 47 KB/s. Mitigation: 120 KB first-paint cap, zoom-based detail limits. Small ASCII labels. Mitigation: scale 2, fewer labels. Regional extracts can be large, about 1 to 2 GB for a big metro [estimate]. The owner picks the region. Licence drift (CoMaps, Protomaps builds). Mitigation: pin builds by hash; recheck before each port. No live traffic or transit in routing. Stated in the UI. 14. Effort P0 is about L: 10 to 14 weeks for one developer, including the renderer work in section 7. M0 to M2 (host and channel) can run in parallel with the renderer. 15. Verified versus memory Verified (opened or run): desk renderer and font code, Kosmos OS maps code and endpoints, the OSM tile and Nominatim policies, licence files for PMTiles, earcut, Photon, Organic Maps, CoMaps and Lucide, the Mac's tools. Reported (search snippets): Protomaps licence split and planet size; OpenMapTiles licence; Valhalla MIT; OSRM and GraphHopper licences; MapLibre Native BSD-2; OsmAnd GPL; the CoMaps AGPL proposal; the 47 KB/s channel figure (repo notes). Memory, unchecked : Apple Maps and Google Maps features; Pelias, Nominatim, OSRM and tippecanoe licences; regional extract sizes; the CoreLocation prompt behaviour. Sources: - https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ (opened) - https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ (opened) - https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads (search) - https://github.com/protomaps/PMTiles/blob/main/LICENSE (opened) - https://github.com/mapbox/earcut/blob/main/LICENSE (opened) - https://github.com/komoot/photon/blob/master/LICENSE (opened) - https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/blob/master/LICENSE (opened) - https://github.com/comaps/comaps/blob/main/LICENSE (opened) - https://github.com/Valhalla/valhalla (search) - https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/OpenMapTiles (search)

x: Music app: plan Status: plan, not code. Branch task/templeos-shell. Written 2026-10-27. Read with docs/holyc-native-apps-plan.md , docs/core-apps-plan.md (Tier 2, Music) and docs/apps/00-kosmos-os-primitives.md (the os.music@1 contract). Registration follows docs/apps/applications-folder.md . Tags: [V] checked in a repo or on this Mac, file named. [R] from a web search this session (snippets, URL given; pages were not opened). [M] from memory, to verify. 1. Purpose A native TempleOS player: browse by artist, album and folder, build a queue, show art, watch a spectrum. The Mac plays the audio, because TempleOS has no usable audio output (section 7). The guest draws everything. A separate, optional retro module plays HolyC sequences on the PC speaker (section 8). 2. Features and priorities Reference set: Apple Music, Spotify, Swinsian, Doppler, foobar2000, Navidrome and Subsonic clients, Koel. Priority Feature Reference P0 Local library from chosen folders: scan, tags, art, duplicate finder Swinsian: folder watching, tag editing, duplicates [R] (swinsian.com/support/about) P0 Formats: MP3, AAC/M4A, ALAC, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, Ogg Vorbis Doppler plays FLAC, ALAC and WAV without conversion [R] (brushedtype.co/blog/doppler-for-mac); foobar2000 format list [R] (neowin.net/amp/foobar2000-v20/) P0 Play, pause, next, previous, seek, shuffle, repeat, volume, mute all references P0 Queue: add, remove, reorder, play next, clear foobar2000 playlist model [R] P0 Now playing: art, title, artist, album, elapsed and remaining Apple Music, Spotify P0 Keyboard first; / focuses search foobar2000 P1 Smart playlists (rules on tags, play count, last played), M3U import Swinsian smart playlists [R] P1 Spectrum visualiser, bars with peak dots cava [R] (reference for band layout) P1 Gapless playback, ReplayGain foobar2000 [R] P1 Streaming from Subsonic servers (Navidrome) Navidrome implements Subsonic API v1.16.1 with exceptions [R] (navidrome.org/docs/developers/subsonic-api) P1 Internet radio (stream URL list) Apple Music and Spotify radio P2 Podcasts from RSS Kosmos musicRssService [V] P2 Lyrics from tags or LRC files Koel Player lists lyrics [R] (apps.apple.com/app/id1576886982) P2 Scrobbling Koel's listed integrations [R] (selfhostedworld.com, unverified) Out Paid-catalogue playback (Apple Music, Spotify), DRM, store purchases, sync between devices Apple Music Sync Library needs a subscription [R] (support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/music/musa3dd5209/mac). Excluded: no accounts or sync in v1 Kosmos OS's os.music@1 contract [V: primitives 1.5] means the same library can later be read by the Kosmos app. 3. Architecture The guest owns UI and state. The host owns files, scanning, decoding and output. text Copy TempleOS guest (HolyC) Mac host (Python daemon + player helper) MusicApp: library, queue, now playing, music-host.py (owns the channel, tab 0) art, spectrum; client of section 4.2 scanner (ffprobe JSON), SQLite library art cache (resized, RGB565) <-- channel --> streaming adapters, Keychain secrets player helper: audio out, position, FFT Rules: Playback is on the host. A guest crash does not stop audio, and the guest never holds a stream URL with a token. Scanning is on the host. ffprobe -v error -show_format -show_streams -of json gives duration, codec, rate, channels and tags [V: /opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe ]. Koel uses getID3 for the same job [V: app/Services/Scanners/FileScanner.php ]. mutagen is GPL-2.0-or-later [R] (pypi.org/project/mutagen) and is not installed [V], so it waits for a licence decision. Art is resized on the host to paint size. 64 by 64 RGB565 is 8,192 bytes; 96 by 96 is 18,432 bytes [estimate]. At the reported 47 KB/s serial rate that is 0.2 to 0.4 s; at the old 1.4 to 2.7 KB/s lockstep rate it is 3 to 13 s, so the art cache is required. Lists are paged. The guest asks for 32 rows at a time. The host never sends a whole library. Library model (host SQLite, stdlib sqlite3 ): track , album , artist , playlist . Track ids are a hash of path and size, so a moved file keeps its play count after a rescan. Folders are chosen in a native host dialog. 4. Playback and control protocol 4.1 Player helper Option Gets us Lacks Verdict afplay [V: /usr/bin/afplay ] play to end, volume pause, seek, state too thin ffplay [V: /opt/homebrew/bin/ffplay ] most formats window only, no IPC not headless mpv [V: not installed] JSON IPC over a Unix socket: loadfile , pause , volume , time-pos , events [R] (mintlify.com/mpv-player/mpv/scripting/ipc-protocol) install; no spectrum over IPC; GPL build options [R] good P1 option Swift helper on AVAudioEngine pause, seek, volume, installTap for FFT (Accelerate) Xcode CLT not checked; AVFoundation lacks Ogg Vorbis and Opus [M] recommended P0 Recommendation: a small Swift helper for P0. Formats AVFoundation cannot play are transcoded to a temporary WAV by ffmpeg on the host. mpv can replace the helper in P1 behind the same protocol. The helper speaks JSON lines on a local Unix socket, so it can be tested with nc -U . 4.2 Messages (new family 0x20 to 0x2F) The browser uses 0x01 to 0x14 and 0x7E/0x7F [V: browser-architecture b2]. This family is a proposal to reconcile with that table. Code Name Payload 0x20 LIB_QUERY (G to H) view (songs, artists, albums, folders, playlists, radio, podcasts), filter, sort, offset, count 0x21 LIB_PAGE (H to G) total, rows: id, title, subtitle, duration, art hash 0x22 PLAY queue position or track id, start ms 0x23 TRANSPORT play, pause, toggle, next, prev, stop, seek ms, shuffle, repeat 0x24 VOLUME level 0 to 100, mute (host output only, not the Mac system volume) 0x25 QUEUE_EDIT add, remove, move, clear, play-next 0x26 STATE (H to G, at most 10 a second on change) status, track id, position ms, duration, queue length, volume 0x27 SPECTRUM (H to G) 16 bands of 1 byte at 10 frames a second 0x28 ART (H to G) hash, size, RGB565 (RLE optional), only if the guest lacks it 0x29 HAVE art hashes the guest holds 0x2A SCAN add root, remove root, rescan, status 0x2B SOURCE add or remove a stream source; the secret never travels 0x2C PROMPT, PROMPT-ANS reuse browser 0x0D and 0x0E Spectrum budget: 16 bytes of bands plus a 16-byte header, 10 times a second, is about 320 bytes a second [estimate]. That fits even the lockstep rate. The spectrum is not sent while the window is hidden. Position: the helper reports position every 100 ms while playing. The guest interpolates for the clock, so the link carries no 30 Hz timer. Gapless: the helper schedules the next file when the current one has 5 s left. 5. Streaming sources Source Auth Work on the host Priority Local folders none scan, play P0 Subsonic (Navidrome and others) user and password or token in the macOS Keychain getIndexes , getAlbumList2 , stream , getCoverArt ; guest sees track ids only P1 Internet radio none the helper plays the stream and reads ICY metadata P1 Podcasts (RSS) none fetch feed and enclosures on demand P2 Koel account on its server Koel has no Subsonic API [V: no "subsonic" in Koel's app/ ]; a separate adapter P2 Apple Music, Spotify paid account, DRM, closed APIs not supported out Navidrome does not mark a song played on stream , only on scrobble with submission [R] (navidrome.org/docs/developers/subsonic-api). The adapter sends scrobble at the play threshold. Account rule: adding a service is an explicit PROMPT (section 9) that names the host, the account and the data read. Tokens stay in the Keychain. The guest gets a track id and a proxy URL on 127.0.0.1. 6. Visualiser and reuse The helper runs the FFT on its output tap and sends 16 bands. The guest draws bars with theme colours and peak dots. A scope view would need raw samples, which the link cannot carry, so it stays in the helper's own window (P2). Candidate Licence (checked) Use mpv GPLv2+ default; LGPLv2.1+ with --enable-lgpl [R] (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mpv_(media_player)) optional helper, run as a separate process over IPC, not linked cava MIT per package indexes [R] (chimera-linux, t2linux). Gentoo lists "MIT Unlicense" for later releases band layout reference; read its LICENSE before copying projectM core LGPL-2.1-or-later [R] (MSYS2 package, 4.1.6) host-side option only mutagen GPL-2.0-or-later [R] not used until a licence decision MPD GPL [M]. Its idle command blocks until a subsystem changes and queues events [R] (git.pvv.ntnu.no mirror of doc/protocol.xml) model for STATE: push on change, not poll Koel MIT [V: LICENSE.md ]; getID3 and ffmpeg transcode [V: app/Helpers.php ] reference for the library model; MIT notice kept if code is copied Navidrome upstream licence not checked [M] test server only, never bundled lofinity-player (local) no LICENSE file [V]; README dedicates it to a teacher's work ideas only; ask the owner before any code reuse Kosmos OS music ( src/apps/music/ , server/services/musicLibraryService.ts ) has no licence [V: primitives 5], so use it as a spec of fields only. 7. TempleOS audio: what is known TempleOS has a PC speaker path (its Snd and Play routines) [M]. Not run here. This QEMU offers sb16 , AC97 , es1370 , intel-hda , hda-* , virtio-sound [V: qemu-system-x86_64 -device help ] and back-ends coreaudio , wav , dbus , none [V: -audio help ]. pc-i440fx-9.2 lists no pcspk-audiodev property [V: -machine pc-i440fx-9.2,help ]. A speaker route to the Mac therefore needs another mechanism. Unverified. A web search for a TempleOS sound-card driver found nothing usable [R, weak sources]. No SB16, AC97 or HDA driver is known in TempleOS V5.03 [M]. Assume no guest audio until the M0 spike says otherwise. The VM launch in scripts/boot-vm.sh has no -audiodev option [V]. 8. Retro module (optional) A separate window: a HolyC note sequencer with a piano roll and tempo, playing on the PC speaker only if M0 finds a route. If there is no route, it runs silently and still shows the notes. It is off the critical path. 9. Security and consent Scoped access. Only folders the user picked are scanned. Symlinks are not followed out of a root. Roots are listed in Settings and removable. No DRM circumvention. Protected files are counted as "protected, not played" and never decrypted. Outward actions prompt. A new account, a new stream host, a podcast download or a write outside the app's data raises PROMPT (browser 0x0D) with the default "no". Guest holds no secrets. Tokens, passwords and credentialed URLs stay on the host. Path checks on the host. No .. , must sit under a chosen root, length at most 1024. Untrusted media is parsed on the host only , in the helper, with a timeout. A bad file is marked failed and does not stop a scan. 10. UI mockup (desk 1440 by 900, window about 880 by 560) text Copy | Music [ / Search ] | | LIBRARY | Songs Artists Albums Folders Lists | NOW PLAYING | | All songs | | Artists | 01 Tone 440 Hz 0:05 | | art 128x128 | | | Albums | 02 Tone 1 kHz 0:05 * | | | Folders | 03 Silence 0:05 | Tone 440 Hz | | Radio | 04 Tone 20 kHz 0:05 ! | |>| 0:02 / 0:05 | | Podcasts | ... | o | | QUEUE (4) | | << || >> vol 60 | | now Tone 440 | | | | next Tone 1 kHz | | 16-band spectrum | | 1,284 tracks scanning 12 of 40 folders host: connected Shuffle Repeat | * marks a queued track; ! marks a file the helper could not decode. Rows are virtualised. 11. Framework needs An app-table entry (name, icon, size, draw, click, key, close), per the framework step [V: holyc-native-apps-plan]. Widgets: virtual list with sticky header, tab strip, search field with caret, slider [V: Slider in 02-ui.HC], progress bar, context menu. A scaled RGB565 blit, shared with the browser's IMAGE path. A 10 Hz timer for spectrum and clock; hidden windows do not redraw. A channel client with request ids. The channel spike (gate 50 KB/s) comes first. 12. Milestones and gates Milestone Work Gate M0 audio route spike (1 day, can run now) host tone through the helper; QEMU sb16 and PC speaker probe; check TempleOS drives either host tone plays; guest route yes or no written here. "No" is a valid result M1 host daemon and helper scan, DB, play, pause, seek, volume, JSON socket 1,000 generated files scanned in under 30 s [estimate]; seek error under 50 ms M2 guest UI over channel paged library, queue, transport, now playing (no art) 500-row list scrolls at 30 fps in the desk [estimate] M3 art and spectrum resize, cache, blit; spectrum at 10 fps art for 200 albums in 2 MB host cache; spectrum latency under 150 ms M4 gapless, smart playlists, ReplayGain pre-schedule; rule engine gap under 10 ms on the gapless tone set M5 Subsonic local Navidrome test server browse and play 50 tracks; no token in any captured guest message M6 radio, podcasts ICY, RSS a stream and a feed play M7 retro module PC speaker sequencer, only if M0 says yes tone audible on the VM back-end M0 and M1 are host-only and can start now. Each later phase needs the owner's go. 13. Test plan A folder of generated test tones: tests/music/fixtures/ , made by scripts/gen-test-tones.sh (to write) with ffmpeg lavfi, so it is reproducible. Tones at 440 Hz, 1 kHz and 20 kHz, 5 s, 44.1 and 48 kHz, mono and stereo. Silence, a 10 ms click track (gap detection), a 60 s sweep (seek accuracy). The same tone as MP3, M4A (AAC), ALAC, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, Ogg Vorbis. Tagged copies with embedded art at two sizes. Bad files: zero bytes, truncated FLAC, wrong extension, a tag claiming 1 GB (rejected, not read whole). A duplicate pair at two paths with equal tags. Checks: scan output against a golden JSON; seek and gap timings from the helper log; a grep of captured guest traffic for tokens and credentialed URLs; desk frame time in a scripted drive ( aiwnios/drive.HC pattern [V]). 14. Risks No guest audio (likely). The app is host-first; the retro module is optional. Codec gaps: AVFoundation lacks Ogg and Opus. Transcode on the host, measured on the fixtures. Link load from art and rows. Caching, paging, 64 px art, 10 fps spectrum. Licence creep (mutagen, mpv, projectM, unlicensed Kosmos OS code). No copying or linking without a written decision. Account services change APIs or terms. Subsonic only in P1. Large libraries on serial. Host SQLite, virtual lists, no full-library sends. 15. Verified and from memory Verified here: the QEMU device, back-end and machine lists; the host tools (afplay, ffmpeg, ffprobe, ffplay, QEMU present; mpv and mpd absent); Python 3.13 with PIL and fontTools, no mutagen; Koel's MIT licence, getID3 and ffmpeg use, and no Subsonic API; lofinity-player's missing licence; the Kosmos OS music files and missing licence. From web search snippets (URLs above; pages not opened): Swinsian, Doppler, foobar2000, Navidrome, Apple Music sync, Koel Player, cava, projectM, mpv, MPD, mutagen. Spotify: no usable source found, so its column is omitted. From memory, not checked: AVFoundation codec list; TempleOS audio routines; Navidrome's and MPD's licences; the Swift toolchain on this Mac. Not run: any audio output, the helper, or the VM with audio.

x: Podcasts: port of the Kosmos OS podcast app (phase A: host and spec; phase B: the HolyC app) Source read 2026-10-27: kosmos-os-frame src/apps/podcast/ (13 files, 3131 lines), shared/podcastDirectory.ts (221, the 108-show directory), shared/podcastFeeds.ts (59), the server services server/services/podcast*.ts (1713) and the 82 APPS$PODCAST_* copy keys in public/locales/en/arco.json . The user's own project, no licence file: behaviour, layout, data model and copy are translated; nothing is pasted. Host side is done ( apps-host/hub/svc_podcast.py , protocol in apps-host/hub/PODCAST.md , 18 offline tests pass). 1. What the source app really has (verified by reading) Shell: app id podcast ("Podcasts"), one window; a shell-level audio engine (PodcastEngine, an <audio> element) keeps playing when the window is minimised. No agent tools, intents or contracts: it only talks to the shell through the window store and /api/podcast/* . Sidebar: search box; Browse section (Main Feed, Home, Browse, Library, Downloads, Transcripts); Sources (Local library, RSS feeds, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Audible, Connect account); Manage (Settings). Home: Continue listening card (Play), Following (grid of followed shows), New in your feed (episode rows), Discover more; empty state "Your feed is empty" with Browse podcasts. Browse (directory): 12 category chips plus All, grouped sections or a Results list when searching or filtering (search matches title, publisher, description), cards with cover, publisher, blurb and Follow/Following. Directory show page: hero cover, publisher, episode count, blurb, Play latest, Follow, episode list with loading, refreshing and error states (previews a show without following). Show page (from Home/Library): back, hero, Play latest, All episodes. Episode page: About / Transcript tabs, Play, Transcribe, Save to Drive. Library: content filter chips (All, Podcasts, Audiobooks) plus Local, downloaded episodes, continue listening, your shows, episodes, "Open in provider". Downloads: locally scanned files. Transcripts: list with word counts and engine. Settings: feed manager (paste RSS URL, Add feed, list with publisher and "auto-download on", remove, sync downloads). Main Feed: full-screen vertical snap slides built from continue, up to 14 new episodes, up to 4 shows, a Discover slide; arrow/PageUp/PageDown keys; blurred cover backdrop; an unwired "Save to queue" button. Player bar (shared MediaPlayerBar): cover, title, show, previous, play/pause, next, progress seek with elapsed and duration, volume, Transcribe, Save to Drive. Previous/next cycle through the catalog of the same source, wrapping; end of episode plays the next. Cover art: server proxies the feed image; fallback is a coloured tile from one of 12 tones (sum of char codes modulo 12). NOT in the source (verified by grep): playback speed, sleep timer, chapters, a real queue, shuffle, repeat, skip 15/30 s, saved resume position (progress is in memory and resets to 0 on every play), played flags, manual download. The host service adds speed, sleep timer, resume, played, download and auto-next anyway because the brief asks for them; queue and chapters stay out (S, below). 2. Data model (types.ts and podcastStore.ts) PodcastEpisode: id, title, showTitle, host, durationLabel "m:ss", publishedAt, kind podcast|audiobook, artTone (12), source local|rss|remote, provider, streamSrc, listenUrl, coverUrl, feedUrl. Episode id for RSS = "rss-" + 16 hex of sha256(feed URL, guid). Ours: eid = 10 hex of sha1(show id, guid). PodcastShow: id, title, host, episodeCount, artTone, feedUrl. Feed subscription: id, url, label, publisher, addedAt, autoDownload. Directory entry: id, category (12), label, publisher, url, description. NowPlaying: episode, progress 0..100, elapsed, duration. Store: three catalogs (local, rss, remote), subscribed feeds, drive saves, transcripts, selection (nav section, show, episode, directory show), filters, playing , nowPlaying. Home = RSS episodes of subscribed feeds, newest first, search and kind filter; server keeps 20 episodes per feed, 30 min cache, downloads at most 5 new per feed. Ours: the same records, flattened into the S D E PS records of PODCAST.md; the guest keeps only the current page (10 rows) and the selection; the host keeps state.json (subs, progress, files, speed, autonext). 3. Mapping to desk3 (window 820 x 560 logical, body below the title bar) Colours only through P(C_*) so all five window styles work; cover tones are a 12-entry table mixed 60% into C_CARD. Widgets: Button (kind 0/1), Radio (category chips), Slider (volume and speed), Toggle, Check, RRFill/RRRing, Txt/TxtC, Hit, LIcon. (two rows of chips, 28 px) [c48] The Daily [ Follow ] <- 10 per page, 52 px rows, Prev/Next page, count "108 in directory" The New York Times - Twenty minutes on the biggest stories ... Show: < Back [cover 96] Planet Money / NPR - 12 episodes [> Play latest] [Following] About text (2 lines) Episodes: rows with [v] downloaded (.) unplayed title date dur [Download] Player: speed chip cycles 0.75 1 1.25 1.5 2; sleep chip cycles off 15 30 45 60 end; seek bar 330 px; volume slider 80 px.
