Copy: reuse the source strings ("Your feed is empty", "Follow podcasts from Browse to see new episodes from your shows here.", "Continue listening", "New in your feed", "Browse podcasts", "No podcasts found", "Try another category or search term.", "Loading episodes...", "No episodes found for this feed."). Icons (Lucide): present in KSICONS.BIN: layers, search, settings, check, play, pause, skip-back, skip-forward, volume-2, refresh-cw (spinner), moon (sleep), star, hard-drive (downloaded), clock, music, chevron-right, x. New, add to NAMES in scripts/gen-icons.py: headphones (app icon), house, book-open, library, download, chevron-left, plus, trash-2 (8). Optional: gauge (speed). 5. Host mapping Search is client side in the source; ours: directory ... QUERY on the host (108 entries) and the title filter of the page on the guest. Follow = subscribe (local) then refresh (approval naming the feed host). Episode rows come 10 at a time ( episodes FID off 10 , 658 bytes). Cover cover ID 48 per visible row, lazily, at most one call in flight (HostCall takes turns), cached by the guest per id. Progress bar and clock from status polled at 250 ms like Music. 6. Playback decision Reuse the Music service (one afplay, one spectrum, one volume). Facts tested: afplay cannot open URLs (so download first, approval each), afplay -r changes speed (measured: 3 s file, rate 2 saves 1.5 s, 0.75 adds 1 s), no pause/seek in afplay (music service uses SIGSTOP and a trimmed file, a 100 to 200 ms gap). The podcast service hands one flagged entry to the Music instance and wraps spawn / position for the rate; Music's own tracks are untouched. While a podcast plays, the Music app shows it as the current track; stop in either app stops both. S only: queue, chapters (Podcasting 2.0 JSON), transcripts, shuffle, repeat, skip 15/30 s (guest can seek pos+30 ). 7. Phase B plan (after the shared tree merge; re-check every number against the merged tree) Files: new desk3/03m-podcast.HC (after 03j and 03l, before 03k-hostpoll if HlDeliver needs the owner; check order in scripts/send-to-vm.sh and aiwnios/build.py lists); hooks in shared files, each a one-liner: 1. 01-core.HC: #define NA +1 (16 now, so the app id is NA-1; define PD_ID after the other ids in 03h-hostlink.HC or in 03m with the Clock method, PdId() looks up "Podcasts" in ks_an ); L_ icons after L_HDD (63): L_HEADPH 64 .. L_TRASH 71; NICON 64 to 72. 2. 02-ui.HC: append "Podcasts" to ks_an, ks_acol, ks_aico (L_HEADPH), ks_aw 820, ks_ah 560, ks_fx, ks_fy, ks_dord (last in the dock). 3. 06-run.HC BodyOf : else if (a==PD_ID) AppPodcast(a,x,y,ks_aw[a],ks_ah[a]); 4. 04-main.HC: AppClick else if (a==PD_ID) PodcastClick(k); ; wheel if (dz && f==PD_ID) PodcastWheel(dz); ; Keys : else if (f==PD_ID && PodcastKey(ch,sc)) {} before the Notes fallthrough (search box, Up/Down, space = play/pause). 5. 03k-hostpoll.HC HlDeliver : owner PD_OWN calls PodcastDone(st) ; HostPoll unchanged. Main loop: PodcastTick once a frame (poll status 250 ms while open, like MusicTick); close hook (Music stops on close; Podcasts keeps playing, stops only by Stop). 6. send-to-vm.sh and aiwnios/build.py file lists; gen-icons.py NAMES (8) then rebuild KSICONS.BIN. Framework needs: all listed in section 4; tab strip, text entry and cover blit are new local helpers inside 03m (no shared change). Widget ids from AID(PD_ID): 1..9 transport, 10..19 nav, 20..39 chips, 40..59 header buttons, 90/91 allow/not now, 100..109 page rows (Play), 110..119 row buttons, 200.. directory rows. Order and gates (each ends with a screenshot in all five window styles, and kslint clean): 1. Icons and hooks only, empty window opens, closes, dock tile. Gate: boots, existing apps unchanged (compare screenshot hash of Music and Weather). 2. Nav, Home empty state, Browse with directory paging and categories ( directory , offline, no approval). Gate: 108 entries, 12 chips, page 10 in under 100 ms. 3. Follow, refresh approval prompt, episodes list with paging against a localhost fixture feed ( podcast_allow_loopback ). Gate: approval text names the host; list scrolls by wheel. 4. Download, play, pause, seek, resume, player bar. Gate: fake-afplay run first ( FAKE_AFPLAY_LOG ), then one audible run on the Mac; Music app still works after. 5. Speed, sleep, autonext chips; covers (p4) on rows and hero; Settings feed manager with text entry. Gate: 48x48 cover paints in one frame; idle CPU not above Music's. 6. Main Feed (reduced), polish, Aiwnios build, docs and status note. One live feed smoke test only with the user's approval of the URL. Risks: HolyC cannot patch forward calls (define before use, follow the Clock lp_req pattern for OpenApp); one host call in flight (cover prefetch must yield to status polling); reply buffer 12000 bytes caps a 96x96 cover at 9.6 KB.

t: Slides for the TempleOS desktop (HolyC)
h: Slides for the TempleOS desktop (HolyC)
x: Slides for the TempleOS desktop (HolyC) Plan only, no code. Written 2026-10-27 on task/templeos-shell . Companion: spreadsheets.md , which owns the shared infrastructure (section 10 here summarises it). Basis: holyc-native-apps-plan.md , holyc-improvement-analysis.md , aiwnios/README.md , desk3/01-core.HC , 02-ui.HC , and the Kosmos OS sources in section 5. Labels: (V) read or fetched today, (M) from memory, not checked. 1. Purpose and users A presentation tool for the desktop: build a short talk from text, shapes, images and tables, present it full screen with speaker notes, and export it. Users: the desktop's author making talks and demos for the TempleOS showcase; people who receive a .pptx from the host and want to view and present it; later, the agent, which writes decks as JSON through a host service. Out of scope: animation timelines beyond simple builds, master editing in version one, real-time collaboration, embedded video and audio (no audio driver in the guest, per the native-apps plan), and any Unicode text beyond the ASCII fonts. 2. Feature inventory Sources: Apple Keynote (support.apple.com/keynote, V for presenter notes and controls in a separate window on Mac, during a video-call presentation; transitions, Magic Move, builds and PowerPoint import are M : that page did not list them). PowerPoint, Google Slides and LibreOffice Impress feature sets are M , not fetched. reveal.js (revealjs.com/speaker-view, V): pressing S opens notes in a second window with the next slide, an elapsed timer and an optional pacing timer. Marp (github.com/marp-team/marp, V): Markdown slides with --- separators, exported to HTML, PDF and PPTX. Feature Seen in Priority Effort Deck of slides: add, duplicate, reorder, delete; slide sorter rail all P0 M Text boxes: two sizes, bold, italic, palette colour, left, centre, right all P0 M Basic shapes: rectangle, ellipse, line, triangle, diamond (from SlideBox ) all P0 S Images placed in a box (decoded on the host, 32-bit) all P0 M Themes: the five desk3 styles as masters (palette, radius, weight) all, as themes P0 M Present mode: full screen, arrow and page keys, Esc, slide counter all P0 S Speaker notes per slide, shown only while presenting all P0 S Native save and open ( .KSD ); JSON interop all P0 M Undo and redo (shared stack) all P0 S Tables: rows and columns, cell text all P1 M Charts: a copy of a chart from the sheets app, or a simple bar or line chart all P1 M Transitions: none, fade, push, wipe; one per slide all P1 M Auto-advance per slide Keynote, PowerPoint, Slides, reveal.js P1 S Presenter view: current slide, next slide, notes, clock all P1 M Layouts: title, title and content, two columns, blank all P1 M Groups, z-order, align and distribute, snap to grid all P1 M Markdown import (Marp-style --- separators, headings, bullets, Notes: ) Marp, reveal.js P1 S PDF export (host) all P1 M PowerPoint import with positions and shapes (not text only) all P1 L Per-object entrance animation (appear, fade) and builds Keynote, PowerPoint, Slides P2 L Morph or Magic Move transitions Keynote, PowerPoint P2 L Hidden slides, slide numbers, custom slide sizes all P2 S Presenter view in a second window (Aiwnios only at first) Keynote, reveal.js P2 L Master and layout editing all P2 L Comments, live collaboration, video, audio all out n/a 3. Architecture decision Options for the slide canvas and the document: A. Native. The deck is parsed in HolyC; each slide is painted with the renderer; text is laid out with Wrap ; transitions run in HolyC over Copy32 and LerpRow . B. Host-rendered display list. The host lays out the deck and sends positioned runs, boxes and images for the guest to paint (the option the native-apps plan keeps for browsers). It gives exact text but needs a host round trip per slide change and a display-list protocol. C. Host-rendered frames. The host renders each slide to pixels and streams them. Rejected: a full 1920 by 1080 frame is about 8 MB of 32-bit data, far above the serial budget. Recommendation: A for editing and presenting; B only as an optional later path for complex PowerPoint text. A keeps the same code on the guest and on Aiwnios and needs no network. Runs natively (HolyC) Runs on the host Slide paint, shapes via RRFill , Disk , Line , text via Txt and Wrap PNG and JPEG decoding into 32-bit tiles, until a HolyC decoder exists Layout of boxes, selection, drag, resize, sorter PPTX and ODP read and write Transitions (fade, push, wipe) with LerpRow and Copy32 PDF and HTML export Presenter layout, notes, timer, key handling Markdown with the full Marp syntax Native .KSD save and open, JSON read, Markdown subset Font work: none, the guest uses ASCII fonts Presenter mode on one display: the guest has one screen and no second window. Version one shows the presenter layout (current slide, next slide, notes, timer) as a toggled split of the same window. A real second window needs the Aiwnios build and a framework change to its SDL windowing, so it is P2 (L). 4. Data model and file format Reuse. Kosmos OS already defines the deck in packages/doc-interop/src/types.ts (V): DeckDoc { version, title, width: 960, height: 540, slides: [{ id, boxes, notes }] } , where a SlideBox has kind ( text , image , shape ), a box x, y, w, h , content (TipTap JSON for text, a URL or data URL for images), fill , stroke , strokeWidth , color , textAlign , shape ( rect , ellipse , triangle , line , diamond ) and groupId . The web app ( apps/slides/src/App.tsx , V) already has groups, resize handles, slide notes, a slide rail and present mode, so the interaction model is proven. Gaps for the guest: no tables, charts, layouts or masters; no transitions; text content is a rich tree that is costly to parse in HolyC. Proposal (additive, version 2). Box kind gains table and chart ; a group lists child ids. Integer geometry in canvas units (960 by 540), so layout needs no F64 . Text as a flat list of paragraphs, each a list of runs {text, bold, italic, size: 1 or 2, color slot} . The TipTap tree is kept as an import and export form. Slide gains layout (name), transition {kind, ms} , advance (seconds or none), and notes (already present). A theme on the deck: a style index (0 to 4) that selects one of the five desk3 styles' palette, radius and weight. Guest file. .KSD , one record per line, ASCII only, generated by the host from the JSON: text Copy KSD 1 SIZE 960 540 THEME 2 SLIDE 1 LAYOUT title B text 80 200 800 120 T2 "Kosmos desktop" B shape 0 0 960 8 rect slot 3 NOTES 1 Say the one-line pitch first. Interop, realistic subset. The Kosmos OS matrix ( packages/doc-interop/FIDELITY.md , V) lists text boxes, shapes and images as supported and tables and charts as partial. Two findings from the code (V): pptx.ts exports with pptxgenjs , which works for the subset, and embeds arco-deck.json in the zip so the Kosmos OS re-import is lossless. The PPTX importer reads only text runs ( <a:t> ), and places each one at a fixed position ( x: 48 , y: 48 + i * 64 , w: 800 ). Real positions, shapes and layouts need parsing of ppt/slides/*.xml and the layout parts. This is the L item in section 2, and the host converter (python-pptx, MIT, 1.0.2 uploaded 2024-08-07 (V); its notes and chart support is M ) is the cleaner place for it. ODP follows the same route through the Kosmos OS converter. Realistic in version one: text, shapes, images, notes, slide order, and PPTX import of text and positions. Not realistic: exact master and theme fidelity, animations, morph, and embedded fonts. 5. Open-source candidates Project Licence and version Verdict reveal.js MIT (GitHub README, V); npm package not found in the registry check Reference for presenter view and notes ( <aside class="notes"> ); optional HTML export. Not run in the guest. Marp (core and CLI) MIT (V) Markdown dialect and converter for the host. Reuse the syntax; the converter runs under Node. impress.js MIT (M) Reference for 3D transitions only. Not needed. python-pptx MIT; 1.0.2, 2024-08-07 (PyPI, V) Host PPTX read and write with positions. First choice if the converter is Python. pptxgenjs Used by doc-interop (V); licence not checked (M: MIT) Keep for export; check its licence before relying on it. LibreOffice Impress MPL-2.0 (M); help version 26.8 (V) PDF of a PPTX through headless conversion, as an external program only. Typst Apache-2.0 (V) Text-only PDF typesetting option. Optional. Kosmos OS doc-interop Private workspace package (V) Reuse as the converter; its FIDELITY.md is the spec. 6. Security and privacy No macros, scripts or embedded code. Hyperlinks are shown and never followed on open or during presenting; a link opens only on an explicit click that asks first. Embedded objects, linked media and OLE data are skipped with a placeholder box. Media in PPTX is not extracted. Import caps: input size, slide count, zip entry count and uncompressed size (zip-bomb guard), and text length per box. The converter reads and writes only the guest's B: directory and a host folder the user picks, with validated arguments and no shell interpolation, and no network access. Export to a path, share, or send each need an explicit prompt. Speaker notes are exported only when the user chooses to include them, because the notes are private to the presenter. Images are decoded with size limits (pixel count and bytes) before allocation. 7. UI specification Layout follows desk3: a rounded window, a toolbar strip, the slide canvas in the middle, a slide sorter rail on the left, and an inspector on the right. text Copy | Slides Insert Slide Format Present Help [Share] [X]| | [Save] [Undo] [Redo] | [T] [Box] [Shape] [Img] [Table] | [Present] | | 1 [ ] | | Inspector | | | | | | Box: text | | 2 [ ] | | Kosmos desktop | | Size: 2 (v) | | | | | | Bold [x] | | 3 [ ] | | Built in HolyC | | Colour: slot3| | | | | | Transition | | [+ slide] | | fade 800ms | | Slide 2 of 3 . Notes: Say the one-line pitch first. | Presenter layout (Present, then P for the presenter split): text Copy | [ current slide ] | Next slide | | | [ thumbnail ] | | | | | Notes | Elapsed 04:12 Clock 14:05 | | Say the one-line pitch first. | Pace: on time | | Left/Right or PgUp/PgDn: move Esc: stop B: black screen | Behaviour: the sorter rail selects slides; drag reorders. Double-click a text box to edit (the text field in section 8). Present mode fills the screen with the current slide scaled to 960 by 540, with no chrome. Transitions run only in present mode and only when the frame budget allows, otherwise they are skipped with no error. 8. Framework needs and gaps Present (V): the window, layer and dirty-rectangle system; hit regions; the Button , Toggle , Radio , Slider and Check widgets; Txt , Wrap , TW and LHt ; RRFill , Rect , Disk , Line ; Copy32 , LerpRow , Fill32 , BlendSpan ; and the Frame and Menubar chrome. The Calculator and Notes apps show the single-buffer text path. Missing: A rich text field: caret, selection, bold and size toggles, paragraph breaks, a word-wrapped layout that updates while typing. Shared with the sheets formula bar and cell editor. Box selection, multi-select, drag and resize with handles, snapping. Only window dragging exists. A slide sorter: a virtualised vertical list of thumbnails, each a cached paint of a slide. A full-screen mode and a mode-specific key map that does not fight the desktop's keys (the desktop uses Esc). An undo stack shared with sheets. Key-up and modifiers, for Shift-click and held-arrow presenting; see the spreadsheets plan. A thumbnail cache with invalidation on edit. Unicode: none in the guest. Smart quotes and dashes must be written as ASCII on import. 9. Shared infrastructure Built once and used by spreadsheets.md : Charts: one module for line, bar, pie and scatter, fed by data arrays. Slides store a chart object with a copied data block, not a link. Tables: the same cell model as the grid. Text: the rich text field, Wrap and a width cache. Undo: a bounded command queue. File and converter: one KsExec protocol for import, export and PDF. Palette and styles: the five desk3 styles' 16-slot palettes, used as themes. Image cache: 32-bit tiles decoded on the host. 10. Milestones and gates Milestone Work Gate (pass) S0 Load a .KSD and paint slides: text, shapes, images 20 golden decks render; pixel differences only where F64 differs (aiwnios README rule) S1 Edit boxes: select, move, resize, text field, sorter, undo scripted drive of 100 edits; no fault, undo returns to the start state S2 Present mode, keys, notes hidden from the audience key test: 50 page moves in both directions; notes never painted in present mode S3 Transitions (fade, push, wipe) and auto-advance each transition at 30 frames a second on Aiwnios; QEMU figure recorded S4 JSON, .KSD , Markdown subset, PPTX text and positions 10 decks round-trip; PPTX positions within 2 canvas units S5 Tables, charts, layouts, groups, align 5 table and 5 chart goldens match S6 Presenter split on one screen, then second window on Aiwnios presenter layout golden; second window opens and closes cleanly S7 PDF and HTML export through the host PDF page count and text match the deck; prompts tested Test plan. Deck render goldens: 20 decks (text sizes, shapes, images, notes, tables) rendered with golden.HC at 1440 by 900 and compared with pxdiff.py , on both targets. Known F64 differences are listed, not failed. Round trips: JSON, .KSD , PPTX (python-pptx read-back of text and positions), Markdown corpus of 20 files. Input: scripted runs of drive.HC for edits, page keys and present mode. Timing: transitions and sorter scroll measured with the improvement analysis benchmark set. 11. Risks PPTX fidelity: the current Kosmos OS importer is text-only (V). Realistic for version one: text and positions. Mitigation: the host converter with real XML parsing (S4). Transition cost under QEMU: a full-slide crossfade touches about 2 million pixels at 1920 by 1080. Mitigation: transitions at half resolution in the guest, and a measured budget before any promise. Presenter on one screen: the second window is Aiwnios-only at first; a user on the guest gets a split layout. ASCII only: most real talks use non-ASCII text. Accept for version one. Scope: animations and masters are where tools spend their effort. Mitigation: they are P2 and out of the first release. 12. Effort Estimate, not measured: S0 to S2 about 4 to 6 weeks of focused HolyC work, dependent on the shared text field and undo from the sheets plan; S3 to S7 about 6 to 8 weeks. Total about 3 to 4 months for one developer. The shared work (text field, undo, charts, converter) is counted in the sheets plan, so the slides increment is smaller if the sheets milestones land first. 13. Verified and from memory Verified (V): packages/doc-interop/src/types.ts , slides/pptx.ts , FIDELITY.md , office-format-interop.md , apps/slides/src/App.tsx (groups, notes, present mode); reveal.js speaker view; Marp's MIT licence and output formats; Keynote's presenter display and notes; the licences and versions in section 5; the desk3 function names and the aiwnios notes. From memory (M): PowerPoint, Google Slides and Impress feature lists; Keynote transitions and Magic Move; impress.js licence; python-pptx notes and chart support; pptxgenjs licence. Not checked: reveal.js's current version (npm lookup failed); LibreOffice's function and slide feature pages (the fetch returned the Writer welcome page).

h: Spreadsheets for the TempleOS desktop (HolyC)
x: Spreadsheets for the TempleOS desktop (HolyC) Plan only, no code. Written 2026-10-27 on task/templeos-shell . Companion: slides.md . Basis: holyc-native-apps-plan.md , holyc-improvement-analysis.md , aiwnios/README.md , desk3/01-core.HC , 02-ui.HC , 03-apps.HC , and the Kosmos OS sources in section 5. Verification labels: (V) read or fetched today, (M) from memory, not checked. 1. Purpose and users A calculator-grade sheet for one user on the desktop: budgets, lists, small models, teaching examples, and quick checks of numbers that arrive from the host. It must run identically on the x86 guest (QEMU) and on Aiwnios (native arm64, see aiwnios/README.md ), so the formula engine lives in HolyC, not on the host. Sizing target: 10,000 rows by 52 columns, sparse; about 5,000 populated cells and 2,000 formulas in a typical file. Out of scope: pivot tables, macros or scripts, real-time collaboration, data sets above one million cells, external data connections. 2. Feature inventory Sources: Microsoft's Excel function list (support.microsoft.com, about 514 entries, approximate); Google's Sheets function reference (support.google.com/docs/table/25273, about 520 functions in 17 categories, approximate); Apple's Numbers support page (support.apple.com/numbers: "hundreds of built-in functions", export to Excel, CSV and PDF); LibreOffice Calc (the Calc function list did not load; Calc details are from memory (M) ). Effort: S under a day, M one to three days, L a week or more. Feature Seen in Priority Effort Grid, A1 references, selection, keyboard movement all P0 M Cell values: number, text, boolean, error all P0 S Formulas: arithmetic, comparison, & , A1 refs, ranges all P0 M Function set tier 1 (40 functions, section 4) all P0 L Recalculation on edit with dependency tracking and cycle errors all P0 M Number formats: General, fixed decimals, thousands, percent, ISO date all P0 S Copy and fill with relative references all P0 M Undo and redo (50 steps) all P0 S Cut, copy and paste inside the app all P0 S Several sheets: add, rename, delete; cross-sheet references all P1 M Column width, row height, freeze top row all P1 S Bold, italic, alignment, fill from the style palette all P1 S Charts: column, bar, line, pie all P1 L Find and replace; sort a range by one column all P1 S Function set tier 2 (25 functions) all P1 M Named ranges Excel, Sheets, Calc P2 S Conditional formatting (one rule: value above or below a limit) all P2 M Data validation (list) and autofilter all P2 M Printing and PDF export all P2 M Function set tier 3 (15 functions) all P2 M Pivot tables, macros, scripts, comments, live collaboration Excel, Sheets, Numbers out n/a 3. Architecture decision Options: A. Native engine. Grid, editing, parser, dependency graph, recalculation, number formatting and chart drawing in HolyC. B. Host engine. Every edit goes to a host service (IronCalc, HyperFormula, LibreOffice). Rejected for interactive use: each edit crosses the serial channel, whose speed the native-apps plan gates at 50 KB/s but whose round-trip latency is unmeasured. C. Hybrid. Native editing and recalculation; the host does file conversion, PDF output, and acts as the test oracle. Recommendation: C. It is the only option that works offline, under QEMU and on Aiwnios with the same code. Runs natively (HolyC) Runs on the host Grid painting with dirty rectangles, scroll, selection, cell editing XLSX and ODS read and write Formula tokeniser, parser, evaluator, dependency graph PDF output Recalculation, error values, number formatting to text Large-file conversion and bulk checks Chart drawing (lines via LineN , pie via DiskN , rectangles, text) Golden oracle runs (LibreOffice headless, IronCalc) Undo stack, native .KSS file read and write, CSV and TSV Font work: none needed, the guest uses ASCII fonts 4. Formula engine Parser. A tokeniser (numbers, strings in double quotes, references with $ , ranges, names, function calls, operators) feeds a Pratt parser with Excel precedence. Excel binds unary minus tighter than ^ , so -2^2 is 4; the test set checks this. Each formula compiles to a flat postfix array of opcodes stored with the cell. Evaluation walks that array with a pointer, with no recursion for ordinary formulas. Values. One struct per value: type tag, an F64 number, a string pointer into a small string pool, and an error code ( #DIV/0! , #VALUE! , #REF! , #NAME? , #N/A , #NUM! , #CYCLE! ). Dependencies and recalculation. Each cell keeps its precedents. Ranges are stored as rectangles, and a reverse index maps a rectangle to the formulas that read it. An edit marks the forward closure dirty and evaluates it in topological order with a depth-first walk and an on-stack flag; a cell reached again while on the stack gives #CYCLE! . Budget: full recalculation of 2,000 formulas under 30 ms on Aiwnios; under QEMU the first measured figure sets the gate, with a fail threshold at 10 times the Aiwnios figure. Numbers. Values are F64 (IEEE double), as Excel and Google Sheets are. Reasons: - the goldens can match a Python reference computed in double; - the performance concern is per-frame float, which the grid avoids by caching formatted text; per-cell float work is cheap (the benchmark set in the improvement analysis measures about 67 ns per float multiply-add under TCG, so 20,000 operations is about 1.3 ms); - an integer fast path handles SUM and COUNT when all operands are whole numbers. Decimal fixed point (I64 scaled by 10^6) was rejected for the main path: it overflows at about 9.2 trillion and cannot represent division. It is kept as a P2 option for a currency-only mode. Display rounds to 15 significant digits with integer digit extraction, not PrintF . Known parity risk. TempleOS evaluates F64 in 80-bit x87; Aiwnios uses IEEE double. The aiwnios README records this as the reason some F64-derived pixels differ. Spreadsheet goldens therefore compare with a relative tolerance of 1e-12, and any value that differs at 1e-15 is reported, not failed. Function tiers (80 in total). P0 (40): SUM AVERAGE MIN MAX COUNT COUNTA COUNTBLANK PRODUCT ROUND ROUNDUP ROUNDDOWN ABS INT MOD POWER SQRT IF IFERROR AND OR NOT ISBLANK ISNUMBER ISTEXT ISERROR CONCAT LEN LEFT RIGHT MID UPPER LOWER TRIM TEXT VLOOKUP HLOOKUP INDEX MATCH SUMIF COUNTIF. P1 (25): AVERAGEIF SUMIFS COUNTIFS IFS SWITCH TODAY NOW DATE YEAR MONTH DAY WEEKDAY EDATE PMT PV FV MEDIAN STDEV LN EXP LOG SUBSTITUTE FIND VALUE SUMPRODUCT. P2 (15): XLOOKUP FILTER SORT UNIQUE SEQUENCE RANDBETWEEN LET MAXIFS MINIFS TEXTJOIN CHOOSE OFFSET INDIRECT NETWORKDAYS REPT. Semantics to match: ROUND rounds halves away from zero; dates use Excel's 1900 serial system, including its false 29 February 1900 (M, from Excel's documented behaviour); text comparison is case-insensitive. Excluded everywhere: WEBSERVICE , IMPORTDATA , GOOGLEFINANCE , and any function that reads a file or the network. OFFSET and INDIRECT are volatile and stay P2. Charts. Column, bar, line, pie in P1; scatter and area in P2. They read a range and draw with the existing primitives: Rect , RRFill , Line / LineN for series lines, DiskN for pie slices (angles need trig, once per slice, acceptable). Labels use the 8-pixel and 16-pixel fonts already loaded ( F_SMALL , F_REG ). 5. Data model and file format Reuse. Kosmos OS already defines a workbook: packages/doc-interop/src/types.ts (V) gives WorkbookDoc { version, title, sheets: [{ id, name, cells: { "A1": { value, formula, format } } }] } , with format covering bold, italic, strikethrough, alignment, a three-value number format ( plain , currency , percent ) and a fill. shared/sheetFormula.ts (V) is a small TypeScript evaluator covering SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT and IF; it is useful as a behavioural reference, not as the engine. Gaps versus this plan: no column widths, row heights, merged cells, freeze panes, charts, named ranges, validation or conditional formats, and a number format too coarse for decimals or dates. Proposal. Version 2 of WorkbookDoc , additive only: cols , rows , freeze , charts , names , and numberFormat accepting an Excel-style format code, with the old enum kept as an alias. Version 1 files keep loading in both apps. The Kosmos OS importers and the TempleOS app read the same JSON on the host side. Guest file. .KSS , one record per line, ASCII only, written by the host converter from WorkbookDoc : text Copy KSS 1 SHEET Sheet1 W A 14 C A1 S Item C B1 S Amount C B2 N 1200 C B3 F =SUM(B2:B2)*1.25 FMT B2 #,##0.00 Non-ASCII text is written as \uXXXX escapes and shown as ? on the guest. CSV and TSV are read and written natively, but only the ASCII subset is round-tripped, and a leading = in imported text stays text. Interop. The host converter reuses packages/doc-interop (V: CSV, TSV, ODS and XLSX, ESM TypeScript, runs under Node). The guest reaches it through the KsExec pattern in 03b-browser (V: the bridge reads a request line and replies OK n c ). Realistic subset: values, formulas as text, multiple sheets, bold, italic, alignment, column widths, common number formats. Dropped with a warning: charts, pivot caches, conditional formats, macros, external links (cached values kept). PDF: HTML rendered by LibreOffice headless (M) or Typst (M), in M7. 6. Open-source candidates Licences and versions checked today on GitHub, npm, crates.io and PyPI (V unless marked). Project Licence and version Verdict IronCalc MIT OR Apache-2.0; ironcalc 0.9.1 (crates.io, 2026-10-21); @ironcalc/wasm 0.9.1; README says "work in progress" and xlsx only Use as a host oracle for function results. Not in the guest. Young; do not depend on it for runtime. HyperFormula GPLv3 or a paid proprietary licence (README (V)); npm 3.5.0 is GPL-3.0-only (V) Semantics reference only. Do not link: GPL, or buy a licence. Blocked by default. formula.js ( @formulajs/formulajs ) MIT; 4.6.1 (V) Reference for each function's edge cases and test vectors. JavaScript, not portable to HolyC. calamine MIT; 0.37.0 (crates.io, 2026-10-18); reads xls, xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, ods; read-only (V) Host reader if the converter is Rust. SheetJS CE ( xlsx ) Apache-2.0 (README (V)); npm 0.18.5 (V). Newer versions are on sheetjs.com, not checked Second choice for a JavaScript host converter. Pro features are paid; CE is enough for this subset. openpyxl MIT; 3.1.5, uploaded 2024-06-28 (PyPI, V) Python host writer for XLSX if the converter is Python. LibreOffice Calc MPL-2.0 (M); help version 26.8 (V) Oracle for recalculation and PDF rendering, run as an external program, never linked. Typst Apache-2.0, Rust (V) PDF typesetting option for printed sheets. Optional. doc-interop (Kosmos OS) Private package in this workspace; depends on exceljs, jszip, pptxgenjs (V) Reuse as the host converter. Its FIDELITY matrix is the spec. 7. Security and privacy No macros, scripts or plug-ins. The formula language cannot reach the network or the file system. Opening a file never fetches anything. External links are shown as text. Embedded objects and OLE data are skipped. Imports are capped: 5 MB of input, 1,000,000 cell records, a limit on zip entries and on uncompressed size (a zip-bomb guard before any parsing). The converter reads and writes only the guest's B: directory and a folder the host picks; arguments are validated and never interpolated into a shell line. It has no network access. Export to a path, share, or send each need an explicit prompt in the UI. CSV formula injection: a leading = in imported text is text. Export writes formulas as text and warns. 8. UI specification Layout follows the desk3 style: rounded window, toolbar strip with RRFill buttons, one line for the formula bar, a grid with a fixed header row and column, sheet tabs at the bottom, an inspector on the right that opens with a key. text Copy | Sheet Edit Insert Format Data Help [Share] [X] | | [Save] [Undo] [Redo] | [B] [I] | [0.00] [%] [$] | [Chart] [fx] | | B4 | =SUM(B2:B3) | | | A | B | C | D | | 1 | Item | Amount | Tax | Total | | 2 | Rent | 1,200.00 | 0.00 | 1,200.00 | | 3 | Food | 310.50 | 0.00 | 310.50 | | 4 | | [1,510.50]| | | | [Sheet1] [Sheet2] [+] | Inspector: Format | | | Number: 0.00 (v) | | | Bold [x] Fill: [16 swatches]| Behaviour: arrows move the selection, Enter commits and moves down, Tab moves right, F2 edits in place, Esc cancels, a drag on the corner fills. Chart panel opens over the grid on request, and a chart is a movable object with a title. Text: two sizes plus bold, the ASCII fonts already loaded ( F_REG , F_BOLD , F_SMALL , F_BIG ). Colours: the 16-slot palette of the active style ( ks_pal ), not free colour, so the five styles stay consistent. 9. Framework needs and gaps Present (V): Button , Toggle , Radio , Slider , Check , hit regions per window and the Hit / HitAt routing, per-window layers and dirty rectangles, Txt , TxtR , Wrap and TW , RRFill , Line , Disk , and IconLoad . The Notes app is a single text buffer with insert and delete ( NotesInsert , NotesDelete in 03-apps.HC ): no selection, no caret movement, no undo. Missing, in order of need: A text field with a caret, selection, and home, end and word movement. A virtualised grid scroll view with a fixed header, drawing only visible cells. An undo stack built on commands, shared with slides. An internal clipboard (cells and text); the guest has no system clipboard. The host clipboard is a P2 service. Key-up and modifier state. Aiwnios reports these; the x86 path needs checking before relying on Shift-click range selection. A context menu. The desktop has only the Kosmos menu. A number input for the inspector. Unicode: none in the guest. Non-ASCII renders as ? . 10. Shared infrastructure Shared with slides.md , built once: a chart module (sheets use it for ranges, slides for chart objects); the cell model as the slide table model; Wrap and a width cache for text; a bounded undo queue; one KsExec converter protocol; the five styles' 16-slot palette ( ks_pal ); and a 32-bit image cache, with PNG and JPEG decoded on the host until a HolyC decoder exists. 11. Milestones and gates Milestone Work Gate (pass) M0 Grid paint, scroll, selection, cell store on both targets 10,000-row sheet scrolls at 16 ms a frame on Aiwnios; QEMU figure recorded M1 Editing, tokeniser and parser for operators and refs 40 parser cases pass; -2^2 = 4 M2 Dependency graph, recalculation, 40 P0 functions, cycles 100 golden formula cases pass (below); recalc budget met M3 Native .KSS , CSV and TSV; host XLSX and ODS round trip 10 sample workbooks round-trip with identical values M4 Charts (column, bar, line, pie) 5 chart goldens match within the render tolerance M5 25 P1 functions, sheets, freeze panes, sort, find 100 further cases pass M6 Undo, paste, fill, number formats, column widths scripted drive of 200 edits leaves no residue M7 PDF export, sharing and export prompts PDF of a 3-page workbook matches the grid; prompt tests pass Test plan. Golden workbooks: 20 small workbooks; expected values from a Python reference ( decimal and fractions for exactness, float for IEEE). LibreOffice headless recalculation is a second oracle, IronCalc a third where it implements the function. Tolerance 1e-12 relative. 100 formula cases as the M2 gate, a table of formula, inputs and expected value, generated and checked by the Python reference. Differential fuzzing: 10,000 random expressions compared between the HolyC engine and the Python reference. Render goldens: grid screenshots at 1440 by 900 with golden.HC and pxdiff.py , on both targets. Performance: the benchmark set in the improvement analysis (section 11), reported as median of three runs. 12. Risks F64 cost under QEMU: a large recalculation may be slow. Mitigation: integer fast path, dirty-only recalculation, and a measured gate. Excel compatibility: function edge cases (ROUND, the 1900 date bug, text comparison) are where spreadsheet tools disagree. Mitigation: the golden cases encode the Excel answer and the LibreOffice answer is recorded separately. Scope creep: pivots and charts of every kind. Mitigation: the P-levels in section 2 are the cut line. ASCII only: non-English sheets display badly. Accept for version one; a Unicode font path is a separate project. Converter drift: the Kosmos OS model changes. Mitigation: the version 2 proposal is additive, and the converter has golden round trips. 13. Effort Estimate, not measured: M0 to M2 about 6 to 8 weeks of focused HolyC work; M3 to M7 about 6 weeks; total about 3 to 4 months for one developer, with the framework items in section 9 counted in M0 to M2. Lower bound if charts are cut to column and pie only. 14. Verified and from memory Verified (V): the Kosmos OS sources in sections 5 and 6, the desk3 names, the aiwnios notes, the benchmark figures, the licences and versions in section 6, the Numbers summary, and the approximate Excel and Sheets counts. From memory (M): LibreOffice's licence and function list, Excel's 1900 date rule, ROUND's mode, Excel's unary-minus precedence, exceljs and pptxgenjs licences. Not checked: IronCalc's function coverage, calamine's Python bindings, SheetJS versions after 0.18.5.

t: Weather and Music prototype: design notes
h: Weather and Music prototype: design notes
x: Weather and Music prototype: design notes Hub: apps-host/hub/hostd.py owns the one VM serial connection, routes by service (echo, time, weather, music, sys), forwards GET lines to scripts/browser-bridge.py (imported, not edited). Guest: desk3/03h-hostlink.HC (transport, HostCall), 03k-hostpoll.HC (HostPoll, after the apps because HolyC does not reliably resolve calls to later-defined functions), 03i-weather.HC, 03j-music.HC. afplay limits (honest) No seek, no pause, no live volume. We use SIGSTOP/SIGCONT on our own pid for pause (queued audio drains, so sound can trail by a fraction of a second); seek and volume change restart afplay on a trimmed temp WAV (python wave or ffmpeg), with a 100 to 200 ms gap. Position is a host clock, not the device clock; spectrum is computed from the file at that position, not captured. Next step: Swift AVAudioEngine helper A small Swift binary the hub starts and talks to over a Unix socket in JSON lines: load, play, pause, seek, volume, state at 10 Hz, 16 FFT bands from an output tap (Accelerate). Gapless by scheduling the next file with 5 s left; formats AVFoundation lacks go through ffmpeg to a temp WAV. The service keeps its op names, so the guest does not change.

x: Weather app: plan Status: plan only, no code. Written 2026-10-27 on task/templeos-shell . Read with docs/holyc-native-apps-plan.md and docs/apps/maps.md (same host-service pattern and renderer gaps). Evidence tags: [verified] opened or run in this pass; [reported] from a search snippet or secondary source; [memory] unchecked; [estimate] our arithmetic, for the gates to confirm. 1. Purpose and users A forecast app for the TempleOS desk: current conditions, the next 48 hours, 10 days, rain timing, alerts, and later radar. It works from a cache with no network. Users: the desk owner with a few saved places. Not in v1: air quality, pollen, history, notifications. 2. Platform facts No network in the guest [verified, holyc-native-apps-plan]. A host service fetches, caches and normalises; the guest reads a compact record. ASCII text only [verified, Txt and TW , desk3/01-core.HC ]. No glyph for ° . Write C or F after the number; draw a ring with RRRing if a symbol is needed. Place names are folded to ASCII on the host. Renderer [verified]: rounded rectangles, one-pixel lines ( LineN ), discs, shadows, Lucide icons ( LIcon ). A temperature curve needs strokes wider than one pixel, which do not exist (same gap as maps, section 7 there). Icons : Lucide is ISC [verified, assets/LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt ]. Host [verified locally]: Python 3 with PIL, rsvg-convert , ImageMagick. Kosmos OS [verified, /Users/paulbloch/kosmos-os-frame ]: src/os/bento/BentoWeatherWidget.tsx calls api.open-meteo.com from the browser for a fixed city list. No weather app or design exists there. We avoid the direct client call: our data goes through the host with caching, rounding and rate rules. Desk : no weather or Contacts app exists yet [verified]. 3. Feature inventory P0 first usable version; P1 next; P2 later. Effort S (days), M (one to two weeks), L (several weeks). Competitors: Carrot Weather (apps.apple.com/DE/app/id961390574) and Windy (apps.apple.com/it/app/windy-com-weather-radar/id1161387262) [reported, search]; Apple Weather (apple.com/weather) and Weather Underground (wunderground.com) [memory]. Features listed are what reports say each app does. Feature P Effort Notes Current conditions: temperature, feels-like, condition, wind P0 S Next 48 hours: temperature curve and rain chance P0 M Needs strokes (section 7) 10-day list: high, low, condition, rain chance P0 S Sunrise and sunset P0 S Provider daily data [memory] Rain timing: "rain starts in 25 min" P0 S Carrot does precipitation alerts [reported] Units: C or F, km/h, mph, hPa, 12 or 24 h P0 S Unit change never refetches Up to five saved places; typed city search P0 M Geocoder (section 5) Provider attribution P0 S Required (section 4) Background refresh and offline cache P0 M Host service (section 6) Alerts (severe weather) P1 M NWS for the US; MET MetAlerts elsewhere [reported] Radar, one-hour animation P1 L Windy and WU have it [reported]; sources in section 4 Desk widget: temperature and condition P1 M Reads cache only Current location from the Mac, with approval P1 M Section 8 Pressure, humidity, UV charts P1 M Depends on provider Lightning, storm cells P2 L Windy has it [reported]; data licence unknown Rain notifications P2 M No notification path on the desk 4. Data sources and terms Source Verified terms Verdict MET Norway (api.met.no) Open data under CC BY 4.0 , attribution required [verified]. An identifying User-Agent with app name and contact; generic library strings are blocked [verified]. Cache responses and honour Expires ; use If-Modified-Since [verified]. Coordinates at most 4 decimals [verified]. Poll no more than every 10 minutes [verified]. Above 20 requests per second total needs an agreement [verified]. No SLA [verified]. Do not use "Yr", "NRK" or the logo in a service name [verified]. Large animations should be hosted by the site itself [verified] Default global provider. The page we read has no non-commercial clause Open-Meteo Data CC BY 4.0 [reported]. Free API non-commercial only ; under 10,000 calls a day, 5,000 an hour, 600 a minute [reported, official terms, not opened] Personal builds , and the geocoder . Commercial use needs a paid plan or self-hosting NWS (api.weather.gov) User-Agent required [reported, official page]; an API key is planned to replace it [reported]. Public-domain status not verified US alerts and US detail. Contact value comes from owner settings Apple WeatherKit 500,000 calls a month per developer membership; paid tiers from US$49.99 for 1 million [reported, developer.apple.com/weatherkit/get-started]. Attribution rules not retrieved Opt-in , for an owner with a membership. Key stays on the host RainViewer Free API for personal and educational use [reported, rainviewer.com/api.html]. Zoom and rate limits reported inconsistently Personal dev test only NOAA radar (MRMS, NOWCOAST) Public US data [memory]; terms not checked Radar candidate (P1); check terms at W6 Recommendation: MET Norway as the default, NWS for US alerts and detail, Open-Meteo for the geocoder and personal fallback, WeatherKit opt-in. Each provider is a host adapter with its own rules. The host applies the strictest rule of each: lowest rate, longest cache, and rounding. Coordinates sent to a provider are rounded to 2 decimals (about 1 km), inside MET's 4-decimal limit. The cache key is the rounded point. Attribution appears in the footer; full credit text goes in the about box. 5. Location and places Typed city (P0): the host geocodes the text (Open-Meteo's geocoder [memory, check at W4]; Photon from the maps plan offline). The result is a rounded point and an ASCII name. Saved places (P0): up to five, in the host store. Current location (P1): read on the Mac with CoreLocation, after the Mac's prompt and an in-app approval. A plain Python process may not get the prompt [memory]; test with a signed helper at W7. IP location is not used : it is inaccurate and sends the address to a third party. 6. Architecture Options: (1) the guest fetches directly, impossible without a network; (2) host service with cache, guest reads a compact record (recommended) ; (3) host pushes on a timer, which wastes channel time on data nobody asked for. Rejected. Compact record [estimate, to measure at W1]: current about 16 bytes; 48 hourly entries at about 8 bytes (about 380 bytes); 10 daily entries at about 14 bytes (about 140 bytes); strings about 80 bytes. Total about 0.6 KB, about 13 ms on the 47 KB/s channel [reported figure]. The forecast is cheap; radar is not. Condition codes map on the host to 12 conditions (clear, mostly clear, cloud, fog, drizzle, rain, sleet, snow, thunder, wind, hail, unknown). Providers differ: Open-Meteo uses WMO codes, MET uses symbol names, NWS uses icon URLs [memory]. The mapping table is tested against fixtures. Radar: a 128 x 128 mosaic of intensity at 4 bits per cell, 12 frames, run-length coded per row: about 2 to 4 KB per frame, 25 to 50 KB an hour [estimate]. Frames are built on the host from the source, never fetched per user. Refresh and cache: - Foreground open: cache is used while younger than the provider's Expires (MET) or 15 minutes (others, to check per provider). - Background: the host refreshes saved places at most every 60 minutes while the Mac is awake, within each provider's rules. - Offline: the last record shows with its age ("updated 3 h ago"). - The host counts requests per provider and stops at 80 percent of the lowest documented cap. 7. Renderer and framework needs Need Today Plan Stroke 2 to 3 px for the temperature curve LineN is one pixel Discs or quads along the path (as maps) Filled area under the curve No Column fills with the rectangle primitive Condition icons LIcon (Lucide) Lucide static icons; a few animated (falling drops, drifting cloud) by frame counter Degree and unit No ° C , F , ring from RRRing Text sizes Four faces, two scales Large face for current temperature Scrollable 10-day list, tabs Not built Widget kit v2 Units are stored as tokens and converted in the guest, so a switch never refetches. Dates use English day names, ASCII only, dot as decimal separator. 8. Security and privacy Location is sensitive. The host asks macOS first; the owner approves in the app second. Nothing is stored before approval. What goes where : settings list, for each provider, the exact rounded coordinates and request type it gets ("MET Norway: 51.51, -0.13, forecast"). Shown before a provider is enabled. Never more precision than the provider allows; never to a provider not enabled. Keys (WeatherKit, any future key) live in a host file with owner-only permissions; the guest never gets them. User-Agent contact comes from owner settings, not hard-coded personal data. Logs hold provider, status and timing; never coordinates unless debug logging is on. Sharing a forecast or forwarding an alert needs a UI prompt. 9. UI specification Tokens from browser h1: C_INK , C_MUT , C_CARD , C_BRD , C_ACC for the current value, C_TEAL for rain, C_AMB for sun, C_BAD for alerts. Kosmos OS tokens are not used (primitives file absent). text Copy | Weather _ [] x | <- title bar 44 | [Now] [Hour] [Week] [Radar P1] Places: [London v] [+] C | F | <- tabs 32 | London updated 12 min ago | | 14 C feels 12 C (cloud) Mostly cloudy | | Wind 18 km/h SW Humidity 72% Pressure 1012 hPa | | | | Rain starts in 40 min, light, 2 mm | <- C_TEAL | | | temperature curve across 48 hours, rain bars along the bottom | | .--. | | / \__.--. .-. | | 14 16 17 16 | | Forecast: MET Norway (CC BY 4.0) Alerts: none cache 12 min | <- footer 22 Week tab: | Mon 27 Oct cloud 14 / 9 C rain 20 % sun 06:58 / 17:22 | | Tue 28 Oct rain 12 / 8 C rain 80 % | Rules: keys 1 to 4 switch tabs; C and F switch units. Enter or click a day to show its hours. Alerts sit in a red bar ( C_BAD ) with event name, end time and "Details" (scrollable full text). Cache older than 6 hours shows its age and a Refresh button, which asks the host and obeys rate rules. Nothing appears that the owner did not ask for. 10. Milestones, gates and tests Milestone Work Gate (pass or fail) W0 Fixtures Record JSON from MET, Open-Meteo and NWS for five places (London, Oslo, Miami, a US place with an alert, a clear-sky place) with headers and times; store under tests/fixtures/weather/ Pass: replay reproduces normalised records byte for byte W1 Host service Fetch, normalise, cache, rate counter, Expires , condition mapping Pass: three providers normalised; a simulated day stays under each documented cap; 0 network calls in tests W2 Current card Guest parses record, draws current card Pass: five places render; no non-ASCII byte in output; golden matches W3 Hourly and daily Stroked curve, rain bars, 10-day list Pass: within 2 percent of host reference; 48-hour view first paint under 1 s on QEMU (target; if missed, ship the list only) W4 Places and units Typed city, five saved places, unit switch Pass: 10 typed queries resolve from fixture; unit switch sends 0 requests W5 Alerts NWS and MET alert fixtures Pass: alert shown with severity colour; clear fixture shows none; text fits W6 Radar (P1) 12 host-built frames; guest animates; attribution Pass: under 60 KB per hour; frame step under 100 ms; terms checked first W7 Widget and location (P1) Desk widget from cache; location via signed helper Pass: widget updates after fixture change; 24-hour simulation respects rules; a test fails if location is sent without approval Test plan: offline by default (a socket open fails the test). Provider contract tests: a changed field in recorded JSON fails the parser. Rate and cache tests with a simulated clock. Privacy test: outbound coordinates must not exceed the allowed decimals. Golden screenshots from QEMU via scripts/snap.sh at W2, W3 and W5, compared with host renders. Mutation check: change one condition mapping and confirm an icon golden fails. 11. Risks Terms conflict: Open-Meteo is non-commercial, RainViewer personal, WeatherKit attribution unread. Mitigation: per-provider rules and separate personal and shipped defaults. Quality varies by region (MET strong in Europe, NWS in the US). Mitigation: provider shown per place; owner chooses. QEMU speed on the curve. Mitigation: fewer points; 24-hour default.
