I did not run a benchmark here (no VM may be started without approval). From sources: HVF and the VZ driver give near-native CPU in the guest [M]; QEMU with TCG is software emulation and is slow (the TempleOS processes above run on TCG [V]). Colima's own config says virtiofs "is the fastest of the options" for vz and 9p is recommended for qemu [V colima.yaml comments]. Lima 1.0 made 9p the QEMU default, virtiofs the VZ default [W]. The ratio virtiofs versus 9p versus sshfs is therefore to be measured : gate G7 runs git status and npm install on a fixed repo under each mount type and records seconds. Do not quote a multiplier until then. Cost on this Mac. RAM: default 6 GiB reserved while running, none when stopped (16 percent of 36 GiB). Disk: base Debian image about 0.3 to 0.5 GB plus tools 1 to 3 GB [M]; with 24 GiB free, a 16 GiB cap is the sane limit. Docker Desktop's 24 GB already held would be freed only if the user removes it, which is the user's choice. 11. What HolyC land would still lack (question 8) GUI debugging and visual tools: a Linux GUI app inside the box cannot be shown (no X/Wayland path to the 16 KB/s link) beyond screenshots; browser devtools for a web app run in the host Chromium, not in the desktop (browser plan DevTools mapping). Mobile emulators: the Android emulator and iOS Simulator are macOS-host programs with their own windows; not in a HolyC window. Command-line control ( xcrun simctl ) is possible through exec with approval; display is not. GPU work (CUDA, Metal, WebGPU): the VM sees at most a virtio GPU in software [V os-foundation-plan.md line 71 says the QEMU build has no GL]; run GPU jobs on the host. Rich editor features (refactors, extension marketplace, notebooks) need work in HolyC or are out of scope. Large-output tools (full docker build logs, huge test runs) are bound by 16 KB/s unless summarised on the host. Latency: every keystroke is a hub round trip; fine for typing, felt in vim at 20 ms [M]. 12. Linux as the base OS instead (question 9) os-foundation-plan.md weighs a Linux base for the whole desktop (Wayland compositor, Electron and Tauri apps). If Linux were the base, containers, ptys, LSP and the GUI toolchain are all native, the serial bottleneck disappears and 16 KB/s stops mattering. The cost is the HolyC desktop's identity: TempleOS would become one app. The Dev Box gets about 80 percent of that value for the apps that matter to developers (terminal, files, git, containers, LSP) and keeps the HolyC desktop as the product. It does not give a GPU, a real browser engine in the guest, or a high-bandwidth display. Recommendation. Take R1 as the product: a Lima arm64 VM (VZ driver, virtiofs, workspace-only mount, Docker or Podman inside), the Docker panel reading the Engine API from it. Use R2 only as a fallback backend when the user already runs Docker Desktop or OrbStack (read-only by default, explicit mounts), R3 as the same term service with an ssh target, and R4 unchanged for HolyC projects. Do not make Linux the base OS for this goal: decide that on the other merits in os-foundation-plan.md . If the Aiwnios build becomes the main path, add the native pty route (KsExec) for the terminal and keep the hub for everything else. 13. Kosmos OS ( /Users/paulbloch/kosmos-os-frame ) has no licence file: its shapes are cited as spec, nothing is copied. 1. Answer Build one app contract and three renderers behind it . Contract (build first, shared): a kind: "web" manifest, a default-deny window.kosmos API, theme tokens, one permission store on the host. This is almost the Kosmos OS "Tier 3 code app" (sandboxed iframe, postMessage SDK, --os-* tokens) [S: app-platform-plan.md, AppHost.tsx, packages/app-sdk], so web apps written for Kosmos OS port with a thin shim. A, host Chromium (first, for compatibility): the existing browser/appd route. Any framework works. Content apps get display-list bands, creative apps and games get tiles. C, host-side JS plus declarative tree (second, for system apps): JS runs in Node or a worker on the host; the guest interprets an indented-record tree. This is the native-feeling, cheap-in-memory track, and the right target for OpenUI Lang apps. B, JS in the guest, Aiwnios only, last, and narrowed: link QuickJS to run the reconciler for C in-process. Do not build a native HTML/CSS engine. The evidence below overturns that half of B. D (compile to HolyC): rejected, except "D-lite": JSX compiled to static tree literals. Caveat: os-foundation-plan.md [S] proposes Linux with our own compositor as the base. If that wins, A's host pieces (runner, manifest, permissions, kit) carry over and the guest-painting parts fall away. 2. What exists today (read, not assumed) Piece State Source Host Chrome 156 over --remote-debugging-pipe , throwaway profile, contexts, tabs, input, snapshots built, M1 passed 24/25 sites browser/host/engine.py, tests/browser/results/m1-summary.md [S] DLIST encoder (DOMSnapshot to 256-px bands), reference painter, format spec built (host); guest painter desk3/browser/paint.HC partial browser/host/dlist.py, dlist-format.md [S] Electron runner (install, sha256, supervisor, CDP, approvals, optional sandbox-exec, tile stream), manifest kind electron , host hub with REQ/RES/APPROVE built; tiles are the labelled "fallback path" apps-host/appd.py, perms.py, stream.py, manifest.py, hub/hostd.py [S] Applications folder: manifest and registry plan, kinds holyc , templeos , host plan docs/apps/applications-folder.md [S] Retained tree interpreter ( desk3/ui/tree.HC , 512-node pool) not built ; spec only docs/apps/01-porting-method.md 4.1-4.3 [S] Aiwnios: natives registered with PrsBindCSymbol("Name", fn(int64_t *stk), arity) ; set today: KsOpen, KsPresent(Rect), KsPoll, KsInject, KsExec. No sockets. built aiwnios/aiwnios-sdl32.patch, platform.HC [S] 3. The shared contract text Copy app bundle (HTML/CSS/JS + manifest) --install--> host appd (grants, signature, hash) | window.kosmos <--CDP binding--> appd/hostd --records--> guest (windows, prompts, notifications) 3.1 Manifest, kind: "web" json Copy { "schema" : 1 , "id" : "user.todo" , "name" : "Todo" , "version" : "1.2.0" , "icon" : "list-checks" , "entry" : { "kind" : "web" , "root" : "dist/" , "start" : "index.html" , "spa" : true }, "render" : "auto" , // auto | dlist | tiles | tree "window" : { "w" : 900 , "h" : 600 , "min_w" : 480 , "min_h" : 320 , "resizable" : true }, "theme" : { "kit" : "kosmos-ui@1" , "follow" : true }, "permissions" : [ "storage:own" , "shell:notify" , "net:https://api.example.com" , "host:files:r" ], "tools" : [], "update" : { "channel" : "stable" , "url" : "https://..." }, "signature" : "ed25519:..." } It extends applications-folder.md section 4 (a new entry.kind next to holyc / templeos / host ) and manifest.py ( electron ). Nothing in the guest parses JSON; gen-apps.py writes the table. Field Kosmos OS manifest [S: shared/manifest.ts] PWA manifest [M] Tauri [M] id, name, version, icon same; Lucide icon name name, short_name, icons[] identifier , productName , version entry url / bundle / openui start_url , scope build.frontendDist , devUrl window not in manifest ( setWindowGeometry aspect only) display app.windows[] {title,width,height,resizable} permissions intent , contract , storage own , shell notify/windows/clipboard/agent none (browser prompts) capabilities/*.json with core:* , fs:allow-read theme --os-* tokens pushed by the host theme_color , background_color none Rule for importing: a PWA manifest becomes entry.start / window / icon ; a Tauri tauri.conf.json becomes window and a proposed permission list that the user must still approve. Permissions are never inferred silently. 3.2 window.kosmos Shape mirrors the Kosmos OS SDK [S: index.d.ts] so those apps run with a shim: intents.invoke , storage.query/execute , shell.notify/askAgent/setWindowGeometry/toolbar , events.on , theme.current/onChange . Additions for the desk: files.pick() (host dialog, returns a handle), clipboard.read/write , window.setTitle/close/requestAttention , agent.registerTool . Transport: Runtime.addBinding("__ks_send") plus a script on Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument that defines a frozen window.kosmos . The host replies by Runtime.evaluate("kosmos._done(id,ok,value)") . Identity comes from the CDP session id that carried the call, never from a field the page sets. [R] I ran this: a denied kosmos.call('fs.read') rejected with "denied: needs host:files:r", an allowed notify resolved, 51 calls were audited, in-page round trip p50 0.1 ms (Python handler, local pipe), and assigning kosmos.call = 1 did not override it. Default deny: every method maps to one permission key (same vocabulary as applications-folder.md section 7); an ungranted key returns a rejection and writes an audit line; "ask" keys open a guest prompt (Allow once / Allow / Deny) whose answer is stored only on the host. The guest never stores a grant and never sees a token. 3.3 Theme The desk has five styles and 16 palette slots ( ks_pal ) [S: 01-porting-method.md 4.5]. Three channels, all host-driven: CSS custom properties injected at document start: --ks-bg --ks-ink --ks-accent --ks-rad --ks-pad --ks-font-scale , and <html data-ks-style="macos|win11|kosmica|longformer-light|longformer-dark"> . [R] injection worked (body computed to the injected colour). Emulation.setEmulatedMedia(prefers-color-scheme) follows the desk's light/dark. [R] flipping it changed all 3 bands of the test page (checked by band hash, not by eye). kosmos-ui.css plus web components ( <ks-button> , <ks-tabs> ...) that read only those variables, so the same markup looks right in all five styles. The apps may ignore the kit; they then look foreign (the Kosmos OS plan accepts the same trade). Fidelity limit [S: browser-architecture.md c4]: in the DLIST route glyphs are the desk's bitmap faces, not the app's font. The kit should therefore set font-family to a face whose metrics the host knows, or line breaks may differ by a pixel or two. 4. Architecture A: host Chromium renders, guest paints text Copy guest window (our chrome, prompts) host input | DLIST bands / tiles | | appd: Chrome target per app | | painter, scroll, hit | | CDP: Input.*, DOMSnapshot, Fetch | bands | window.kosmos binding, perms, audit | Fidelity: layout is Chrome's (flex, grid, tables exact); glyphs, shadows, gradients and rotation are approximate or tiles [S]. React, Svelte, Preact, web components all work because Chrome runs them. Measured here [R] (Chrome 156, Python encoder, 900x600 viewport, loopback server, throwaway profile, M-series Mac): Measure Vanilla todo React 19 todo (195 KB min, 61 KB gzip) React + 200-row table Navigate to settled 0.59 s 0.60 s 0.54 s DLIST items / ops 22 22 822 (808 TEXT) DLIST bytes, all bands 931 B 745 B 27.3 KB (20 bands) First-paint bytes (visible bands) 931 B 745 B 3.6 KB Capture + encode, steady p50 0.7 + 0.5 ms 0.7 + 0.5 ms 18.6 + 21.4 ms Type text and click Add, host side, to a new DLIST: p50 17 ms , p95 21.5 ms; changed bands cost p50 1.4 KB . At the reported 47 KB/s serial [S, unreproduced] that is about 30 ms more; on an Aiwnios socket it is negligible. The guest half (paint) is not measured. Resize 900x600 to 600x400 to a new DLIST: 3.9 ms host-side. Pixels instead: screenshot 600x400 PNG 18.9 KB (35 ms), 900x600 JPEG q60 18.8 KB (28 ms) for this near-empty page; raw RGB565 900x600 is 1.08 MB, 23 s at 47 KB/s. The guest has no JPEG decoder, so tiles use the palette/RLE encodings already in stream.py , dirty rectangles only. Memory: physical footprint (macOS footprint ) of the Chrome tree rose 647 MB for 5 extra app tabs, each in its own incognito context (about 129 MB each, 16 extra processes), on top of an 810 MB tree with no app open. One shared context was not measured; it should cost less but weakens isolation. Trap found: the second tab I opened ignored input for about 5 s per click (p50 5069 ms) because it was not the front target. Calling Page.bringToFront and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled fixed it (17 ms). The runner must front the focused app's target and emulate focus on every window focus change. How the awkward cases behave (mechanisms from browser-architecture.md and CDP, [M] for the CDP method names unless noted): Area Behaviour Resize, DPI guest RESIZE (100 ms debounce) to Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride ; stream.py uses DSF 1 so surface px equal CSS px [S] Scrolling root scroll local; nested containers cost a round trip [S] Text, IME key/char events to Chrome; committed IME text via Input.insertText ; inline composition preview is a gap Clipboard kosmos.clipboard with a prompt, through the channel Drag and drop in-page drag via Input.dispatchDragEvent ; dropping a desk file needs a granted host path File pickers intercept the chooser, show the desk's picker, answer with DOM.setFileInputFiles Notifications Notification overridden to kosmos.shell.notify ; Chrome's permission stays denied [S: engine.py] Audio, video, canvas no guest audio; video and canvas as tiles (video 2-5 fps, canvas on change, ~100-200 ms, estimate) Cost: the engine is installed on the host, not bundled (licensing and size) [S]. Memory scales with Chrome, not with the guest. Idle apps should be frozen ( Page.setWebLifecycleState [M]) and their processes discarded after a timeout. 5. Architecture B: JavaScript engine inside the desktop x86 TempleOS. Not impossible, but not worth it. engine-on-templeos.md [S] proved a freestanding Rust blob loads as a .BIN and matches host hashes, so a C engine behind a libc shim (memcpy/malloc/math, the shim listed in holyc-improvement-analysis.md ) is conceivable [M]. QuickJS has no JIT, runs on TCG emulation, and is about 6x slower than V8 even natively (below); I estimate 20-100x slower than the host under TCG [M, unmeasured]. What survives on x86 is therefore: the tree interpreter (C), host-side JS, and display-list/tile rendering (A). No JS in the guest. Aiwnios. Feasible and cheap to start. Natives are registered by PrsBindCSymbol [S]. QuickJS: MIT licence [S: brew info quickjs ], version 2026-06-04 is installed here, libquickjs.a is 1.0 MB with symbols [R]. quickjs-ng, Duktape, Hermes and Boa are alternatives, also permissively licensed [M]. Speed [R], same reconciler script (render + diff, one list row changed): Node 22 0.04 / 0.55 / 2.9 ms; QuickJS 0.11 / 3.4 / 17.4 ms for 5 / 200 / 1000 rows. QuickJS is about 6x slower than V8 but is fine at 200 rows and poor at 1000. Not measured: React itself under QuickJS (needs a DOM). Native HTML/CSS subset. What a todo app needs: DOM (createElement, appendChild, attributes, classList, events with bubbling, innerHTML ), a CSS cascade (selectors, specificity, custom properties, calc ), block/inline/flex layout, text wrapping, borders/radius, images, form controls, timers, fetch . Real frameworks add MutationObserver, getBoundingClientRect , requestAnimationFrame . Ideas to borrow, not code: litehtml (BSD-3 [M]; CSS 2.1 centric, flex partial [M]), Taffy (MIT [M], Rust, flexbox/grid, layout only), Yoga (MIT [M]). Estimate [M]: 3-6 person-months to run a Preact todo app acceptably, then permanent compatibility debt. Chrome gives all of it for 0 lines; the only gain is independence from the host, which hostd already forgoes (secrets and services live there). Verdict: B-lite : QuickJS in Aiwnios running the C reconciler, so a tree app can run without the host's Node. Defer until C exists. 6. Architecture C: host JS, declarative tree text Copy JS (React/Preact/Svelte-like custom renderer, or OpenUI Lang) [host Node worker] | state -> component tree (virtual) -> keyed diff v TREE / INS / SET / DEL records EV id kind value guest: tree interpreter (512-node pool) -> Txt, Button, Toggle, RRFill... with our theme This is Elm's loop (model, view, messages) with React Native's split (JS thread builds a shadow tree, the native side renders and sends events) [M]. It differs from Flutter, which owns every pixel; our guest renders with its own widgets, so theme and accessibility come free. The wire format already exists on paper: TREE , SET , EV , NOTIFY over the hostd frame [S: 01-porting-method.md 3.3, 4.1, 4.6]. Measured [R] (scratch reconciler, one tree vocabulary row/col/text/button/check/list): Rows Nodes Full tree Patch: toggle one check Patch: append a row 5 38 564 B 20 B 95 B 200 1208 20.1 KB 20 B 107 B 1000 6008 102.5 KB 20 B 113 B Compare the same todo in A: 745 B to 27 KB per first paint and about 1.4 KB per change. C wins on bytes by 10-70x for updates, and needs no Chrome process for rendering (memory per app: a Node worker, tens of MB [M]). The limits: the pool is 512 nodes, so lists need a virtual list node (host sends only the visible window); layout is the row/col/gap/pad/fill subset, no wrap, grid or absolute positioning [S]. Relation to Kosmos OS OpenUI Lang [S: src/apps/generator, appview, node_modules/@openuidev]. Generative apps are text programs of assignments ( root = Card([hdr]) , hdr = CardHeader("Title","Sub") ) with positional component calls and actions such as @ToAssistant("Submit") . The library (react-ui genui-lib , about 40 components) includes Accordion, Button, Callout, Card, Carousel, Charts, CodeBlock, DatePicker, Form, Image, Input, Modal, Select, Slider, Stack, Steps, Table, Tabs, Tag, TextArea, TextContent. Persisted apps add $state , SQL-backed Query bindings and declared action intents (tier 1-2 in app-platform-plan.md). The packages are MIT [S]. Mapping: OpenUI is a front end that compiles to the same tree (Card to card, Stack to row/col, TextContent to text, Button to button, Form to form, Table to list/table, Charts to chart, Modal to dialog). So C has two front ends over one IR: a React-style renderer for hand-written apps and an OpenUI Lang parser for agent-made ones. Actions become EV messages, then intents through the same grant table. kosmos-ui contents (one vocabulary, two renderers: tree node in C, web component in A): layout (row, col, card, split, scroll, tabs, sidebar, grid-lite); controls (button, toggle, check, radio, slider, select, input, textarea, date); display (text, markdown-lite, image, icon, tag, progress, metric, table, virtual list, line/bar chart, code block); overlays (dialog, menu, toast, tooltip); system (menu-bar items, toolbar, file dialog, notification). Costs [M]: interpreter v0 M, v1 M (text field, scroll list), React-style custom renderer S-M (react-reconciler is MIT [M]; I did not try it), OpenUI front end M. Text fields and the font service (P2, P5 in the porting plan) gate real apps. 7. Architecture D: compile-time to HolyC Compile web components or restricted TSX to HolyC at build time. Too ambitious for general code: HolyC has no closures, no managed strings or arrays, F64 is x87 on x86 and IEEE on Aiwnios (parity differs) [S: aiwnios README], and the Aiwnios dialect has six documented traps. What is worth keeping is D-lite : JSX with static structure compiles to tree literals plus a handler table, so a purely declarative app needs no JS at runtime. That falls out of C almost free, and runs on x86 with no host JS (it still needs the host for services). 8. Hybrid by app type (section E) App type Route Why Content: docs, mail, news A with DLIST; C for first-party mail and contacts text-heavy, bands are small (3.6 KB first paint for a 200-row table), selection and find work on DLIST Dashboards, widgets C (metric, chart, list) small trees, frequent patches, low memory; maps to OpenUI Charts, Table Creative tools A with tiles; native HolyC for tight loops canvas/WebGL needs pixels; input latency is a round trip, so brushes should be local Games A tiles on Aiwnios socket, or native HolyC 100-200 ms tile latency rules out action games over serial; state it plainly IDEs A via Electron/appd tiles for existing editors (VS Code), C for our own IDE the editor surface is canvas-like text; stream.py already exists for it 10. Security Origin and storage. One Chrome context per app, a distinct origin per app id, disposed on close. Memory cost above. No ports for assets. Prefer serving the bundle through Fetch.enable / Fetch.fulfillRequest under https://<appid>.kosmos.invalid/ [M]: no listening socket, and the same hook is the network allowlist for net: permissions (everything else fails). If a loopback server is used (the day-one prototype does), bind 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, serve only the bundle, check Host , reject .. . The browser design already forbids --remote-debugging-port [S]. CSP injected by the host: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src limited to the manifest's net: list; no inline script unless the manifest asks and the user approves. Guest holds nothing. No tokens, cookies, keys, passwords [S: browser-architecture.md e2]. Grants live in approvals.json on the host [S: perms.py]; the guest only draws prompts. A hostile guest can ask for a token and replay it; the hub says so itself [S: hostd.py], so hostd, not the prompt, is the boundary. Process. appd already strips the environment, fixes profile and download dirs, and offers a sandbox-exec profile [S]. Chrome's renderer sandbox stays on ( --no-sandbox never used). Supply chain. kosmos-app pack takes a built dist/ , refuses install scripts, records SHA-256 of every file, and signs (Ed25519, per applications-folder section 8). No remote script at runtime (CSP). Lockfile and SBOM are packaged, not trusted. Unsigned apps need an explicit prompt. Agent tools bind to intents or fixed queries, never app code [S: shared/manifest.ts]. 11. Packaging, distribution, developer experience Package: a folder or .ksapp zip: manifest.json , dist/ , icons, optional sw.js . Offline: the bundle is local, so a service worker is only needed for the app's own data caching. Do not register service workers by default (they add a background process); allow offline: "sw" explicitly. Updates: compare semver, re-prompt only for new permission keys [S: applications-folder 8]. Remote start URL: allowed as entry.url , flagged "not packaged", needs net: for its origin. CLI kosmos-app : init (template for vanilla, Preact, Svelte; kosmos-ui preinstalled), dev (runs the user's Vite on loopback and opens it in a desk window with HMR; the dev server is the only time a loopback port serves app code), check (manifest and permission lint), pack , install , run . DevTools: the host already owns each app's CDP pipe. The guest DevTools app (DEVT messages, panels to CDP domains: Elements, Console, Network, Application) [S: browser-architecture.md f] attaches to the app's target, with Cookie/Authorization redacted. Developers can also use real DevTools in dev mode through a token-guarded loopback socket, off by default. 12. x: Electron apps in the HolyC desktop (prototype) Date 2026-10-27. Code: apps-host/ (host), desk3/03d-electronapp.HC (guest, off by default). Context: electron-tauri-support-research.md (why not pixel capture of the Mac screen), browser-architecture.md (CDP over a pipe, display-list bands), apps/applications-folder.md (manifest, permissions). Measured on this Mac with a VS Code OSS build (Caret 1.116, Electron 39.8.5, Chromium 142) that was already on disk. Architecture An Electron app is a Chromium renderer plus a Node main process. appd launches the app with --remote-debugging-pipe (fds 3 and 4, no port), so the desktop drives the renderer exactly like the browser engine: CDP Page , DOMSnapshot , Input , Emulation , Runtime . Electron 39 accepts the Chromium switch; only Browser.getWindowForTarget is missing (no window bounds), everything else probed ok. text Copy guest window (HolyC) <-- COM1, framed, lockstep ACK --> appd bridge <-- unix socket --> supervisor <-- CDP pipe --> Electron 03d-electronapp.HC tiles (down), input (up) stream.py appd.py BrowserWindow pages Allow/Deny sheet attach.py (throwaway profile) Two content routes, one control path: 1. Display list: attach.display_list = DOMSnapshot -> browser/host/dlist.py bands (reused, unmodified). Fits plain DOM; used for the report. 2. Pixel tiles (labelled fallback, the one wired to the guest): the page is laid out at the exact surface size ( Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride , DSF 1), screenshotted, diffed in 16-row strips, sent as RGB565 or 16-colour RLE rects. Input: guest mouse/wheel/key -> Input.dispatchMouseEvent/KeyEvent ; surface px = CSS px, so no mapping error. Focus rule: the front guest window sends focus on/off -> Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled (the app only types while the guest window is front; it never raises the Mac window). Install flow ( install.py ) text Copy fetch (https or loopback http, or a path) -> SHA-256 must equal --sha256 (required, no default) -> safe extract to a work dir -> find .app, Info.plist, Electron Framework (else refuse: Tauri/WebKit is not supported) -> read Electron fuses -> codesign: none = refuse (--allow-unsigned); ad hoc = refuse unless --allow-adhoc; developer-signed must verify -> strip com.apple.quarantine -> manifest -> move to apps/<id>/ -> registry.json (atomic) Extraction rejects absolute paths, .. , backslashes, symlinks leaving the tree, writes through symlinks, hard links, devices, duplicates, size bombs. Tested only against local archives (zip of the on-disk VS Code, 296 MB, served by python3 -m http.server on 127.0.0.1). Nothing was downloaded. The VS Code build is ad hoc signed and does not verify ( code has no resources ), so it needs --allow-adhoc . Fuses of this build: RunAsNode on, EnableNodeCliInspectArguments on, cookie encryption off, ASAR integrity off (so patching and CDP are not blocked). Measured (loopback, no QEMU UART in the path) What Result Launch to attached page (existing profile) 0.4 to 1 s; first workbench paint about 2 s Display list of VS Code, 1440x900 103 items, 3.9 KB, capture 10 ms + encode 7 ms; tile similarity 0.874 vs screenshot (mostly flat dark area, so flattering) Screenshot of the page 73 ms round trip (2880x1800 PNG 110 KB); at DSF 1, 36 ms p50 Tile stream, 1000x640 first frame 63 to 216 KB; capture 36 ms, encode 4 ms, send 2 ms (p50) Click to first tile at the guest p50 109 ms, p95 193 ms (8 clicks); settled p50 322 ms Key (editor) to first tile p50 63 ms, p95 96 ms; wheel p50 100 ms, p95 136 ms Bytes per click that opens a file about 81 KB (the whole editor area changes) Result checks typed text reached the Monaco editor, wheel scrolled 33 lines, decoded framebuffer equals a fresh screenshot (0 px differ) Results above come from a Python stand-in for the guest ( tests/stage3_fake_guest.py ). The HolyC guest was not compiled or run in a VM ; real latency adds the UART (81 KB at 100 KB/s is about 0.8 s per file open) and the guest blit. Aiwnios native I/O was not checked. Cuts if serial is the limit: 4-bit palette tiles with dithering, smaller surface, scroll copy (CopyRect) instead of resending, delta against the prior tile. What the display-list route cannot do Canvas and WebGL, the Monaco editor's glyph layers when it renders to canvas, <webview> /iframe content from other processes, native menus and title bar, OS dialogs, <select> popups, video, codicon/icon fonts (private-use glyphs, shown as boxes), SVG (grey placeholder), text shaping. Proposal: DOM-heavy shells (sidebar, tabs, settings) as display list; editor, terminal, webviews, canvas as pixel tiles, per target rectangle. The tile route covers everything a page paints but not what the OS paints around it. Security and permissions Manifest permissions : storage:own , host:files:ro|rw (one workspace folder), host:net , host:downloads , shell:clipboard|notify|agent . First launch: the bridge sends a question (what the app asks, workspace path, "not signed") to the guest sheet; Allow records approvals.json on the host. More permissions in an update invalidate it. Revoke with appd revoke . Kill switch: appd stop (Browser.close), appd kill (supervisor, else the verified process tree only; tested: 8 processes to 0). Closing the last window stops the app. Enforced by the host: profile, extensions, downloads under profiles/<id>/ ; minimal environment (no tokens, throwaway HOME and TMPDIR); --use-mock-keychain (without it Electron blocked on a Keychain prompt); workspace must be a real folder, not / , $HOME , ~/.ssh , Library , ...; network off by Chromium flags unless host:net (renderers only; the Node main process is not covered); eval only with shell:agent . Not enforced: an unsandboxed app can read anything the user can (tested: Electron as node read a decoy outside its workspace). sandbox-exec (deprecated, present): a profile denying $HOME reads and network confines the Electron runtime in node mode (workspace file read, outside read EPERM, write outside EPERM, net EPERM; tests/test_perms.py ). The full Chromium app fails under it ("sandbox initialization failed"): Chromium cannot nest its own seatbelt, and --no-sandbox would trade renderer isolation for it. App Sandbox needs a signed bundle with entitlements: not tried. A real boundary needs a container or VM (see os-foundation-plan.md ). Electron wants short profile paths (103-byte socket limit): appd aliases through /tmp/ksa-<uid>/ . Tauri and WebKit apps No CDP on macOS WKWebView (Safari inspector only, private API; tauri-driver has no macOS driver). Options: pixel capture of the window (ScreenCaptureKit) as in the research doc, or run the frontend as a page in headless Chromium with the Rust side mocked (per app, needs source). h: ArtCraft Crafting Apps on the HolyC TempleOS desktop: feasibility study
x: ArtCraft Crafting Apps on the HolyC TempleOS desktop: feasibility study Date 2026-10-27, branch task/templeos-shell . Research only: nothing was cloned, downloaded or run; everything below comes from web pages, the GitHub API and raw.githubusercontent.com files read today. Labels: [V] read or fetched today (source named). [R] measured in our repo's earlier notes (cited). [M] memory, inference or estimate, not checked. Effort sizes (S, M, L) are [M] . 1. Answer Do not run the Crafting Apps as windows in the desktop as the main plan. The best fit is R3: use the headless *-cli binaries (and their stdio MCP servers) as host services behind our hub , feeding our own HolyC UIs: GridCraft for xlsx/xlsb/ods import, export and a formula oracle; PdfCraft for page render, text and page organise; WordCraft and DeckCraft for docx/odt/pptx conversion and page PNGs. Each CLI is a single local process with no network need [V]. The second route is R2: the WebAssembly builds in headless Chrome under appd, shown as tiles . All are egui canvases, so tiles are the only route; it works with infrastructure we already have, but is slow over serial and mostly gives us the apps' own UI rather than our native look. R1 (native window streaming) is possible without Screen Recording because the apps expose ui.screenshot and input calls over a JSON channel, but it has no advantage over R2 for us. R5 (Rust staticlib inside Aiwnios) is real but later. R4 (no_std to a .BIN ) is blocked by std , alloc , chrono and regex . R6 (port to HolyC) is rejected. Handle with care: the projects are weeks old and move extremely fast (section 2.1). Pin a release by SHA-256, expect breakage, and make no plan depend on a single version. Day-one prototype: GridCraft CLI behind the hub (needs one 11.7 MB approved download). An optional hour-long R2 tile test with the 7.7 MB GridCraft web zip. 2. What they really are (question 1) 2.1 Organisation, maturity, licences Fact Value Source Org github.com/storytold ; 18 repos listed in the first 100 KB of the API reply (the reply was truncated, so more may exist) [V] API orgs/storytold/repos Apps 13 repos, all "pure Rust", engine plus swappable egui UI [V] repo descriptions and READMEs GridCraft repo created 2026-10-07, last push 2026-10-27, 6,677 stars, 3,084 forks, 1,372 open issues; Rust 8.1 MB of source, workspace version 0.12.1 [V] API PdfCraft repo created 2026-09-30, 18,235 stars, 6,925 forks, 2,356 open issues, version 0.14.0 [V] API Release cadence GridCraft v0.11.1 on 2026-10-22, v0.12.1 on 2026-10-25 [V] API releases Merge rate GridCraft PR #2704 merged 2026-10-27 [V] API commits Launcher storytold/craft-launcher , Apache-2.0, "early alpha" [V] Shared libs storytold/craft-libs (Apache-2.0, created 2026-10-09), pinned by git rev 92d392c ; egui and winit are pinned to storytold forks [V] Cargo.toml Agent files GridCraft and others carry AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md [V] contents listing How to read this: about four weeks of history, thousands of PRs, huge star and fork counts. I cannot verify what produced those numbers, so treat popularity as unverified and judge the code, not the stars. The repos are heavily agent-assisted (agent instruction files, "clean-room" framing, parity percentages), so quality is uneven. Self-reported readiness: GridCraft "about 50%" (alpha), PdfCraft 55% (alpha), WordCraft 60% (alpha), DeckCraft 55% (alpha), SoundCraft "roughly 40%" (pre-alpha), VectorCraft 65%, FilmCraft 56%, LightCraft 61%, EffectCraft 45%, FigCraft 49% (early alpha), DesignCraft "pre-alpha", CADCraft "early development", PhotoCraft "early alpha" [V] READMEs. Discrepancies found, so do not trust the marketing page alone: - getartcraft.com/apps says GridCraft is "In development" with v0.5.0; GitHub releases are at 0.12.1 [V]. - The apps page lists FilmCraft as having no web build; the FilmCraft README says a web build exists and ships as a zip [V]. - The page says "permissive licences" without naming one; the repos say MIT OR Apache-2.0 (GridCraft and PdfCraft READMEs; API reports Apache-2.0) [V]. Licences that matter. Code: MIT OR Apache-2.0. The ArtCraft name and logos are trademarks under a separate brand licence; forks and modified builds must remove them [V]. GridCraft's attribution file lists fonts under MIT, Bitstream Vera, SIL OFL 1.1 and Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0, and no GPL, LGPL or MPL [V]. FilmCraft uses symphonia (MPL-2.0, per its README) for MP3, FLAC, ALAC and Vorbis [V]. CADCraft's DWG support uses the acadrust library, whose licence I did not check [M: unknown] . Licences of egui, wgpu, hayro, lopdf, vello_cpu, krilla and skrifa are [M] (all believed MIT and/or Apache-2.0); run cargo deny before any redistribution. We would run the binaries as separate processes (R3), so even a copyleft crate would not link into our code. 2.2 Stack (GridCraft in detail, others from READMEs) Workspace layers (enforced by cargo xtask layers ) [V] architecture.md: L0 core (cell addresses up to 1,048,576 x 16,384, values, errors, date serials), numfmt ; L1 formula (tokenizer, parser, A1/R1C1), functions (513 worksheet functions listed, per the README's own caveat a parity inventory); L2 model , calc , xlsx (XLSX/CSV/TSV, XLSB and ODS import, pivot caches, DrawingML charts); pdf (small PDF 1.7 writer); L3 chart ; L5 engine ( Session , 313 commands through Session::execute(id, params) ); L6 ui-egui , mcp ; L7 gridcraft , gridcraft-cli , gridcraft-web . Nothing below L6 depends on egui, eframe, winit or rfd [V]. This is the key fact for R3. Dependencies of the core crates [V] Cargo.toml files: gridcraft-core = serde, thiserror, chrono (std), js-sys on wasm32; gridcraft-formula = core, serde, thiserror; gridcraft-functions = core, regex ; gridcraft-calc = core, formula, functions, numfmt, model, log ; gridcraft-engine = those plus serde_json, xlsx, chart, pdf, image . Workspace root also has rayon, quick-xml, zip, sha1/sha2/aes (encrypted workbooks), skrifa. unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide. Threads: calc is single-threaded (listed as a known gap) [V]. VectorCraft and DesignCraft render multithreaded on CPU (vello_cpu) [V]. UI and renderer: egui 0.37 / eframe 0.37 on wgpu (Metal, Vulkan, DX12, WebGPU), winit via a storytold fork [V]. Variations: WordCraft and DesignCraft rasterise pages with vello_cpu and use the GPU only for UI compositing [V]; PhotoCraft has a CPU reference compositor and a wgpu one [V]; FigCraft uses tiny-skia with HarfRust/skrifa [V]; PdfCraft draws pages with the third-party hayro crate while its own pdfcraft-render is built [V]; FilmCraft and LightCraft use wgpu compute with CPU fallback [V]. No Skia, no iced. File formats [V]: GridCraft xlsx r/w, xlsb/ods import, csv/tsv, json/html export. WordCraft docx/odt/rtf/html/md/tex/txt r/w, .doc read, PDF export. DeckCraft pptx r/w, PDF/PNG/JPEG/GIF export. PdfCraft PDF (own COS layer, 33 crates). PhotoCraft PSD/PSB/layered TIFF/ORA r/w and many flat formats. VectorCraft SVG, PDF/AI, EPS, DXF. CADCraft DXF and DWG, SVG/PNG/PDF out. SoundCraft WAV/AIFF/FLAC r/w, MP3/Ogg/AAC in. WebAssembly build [V]: apps/<app>-web , trunk build --release , eframe + wgpu (WebGPU with WebGL2 fallback), wasm-bindgen , web-sys , one <canvas> ; open uses the browser file picker and save downloads a file. Shipped as a static zip: GridCraft web 7,660,730 B, PdfCraft web 15,961,263 B [V]. Uncompressed .wasm sizes reported by a third-party review: PhotoCraft 24.2 MB, PdfCraft 37.9 MB [V search result, secondary source]. No hosted URL : you self-host the zip [V search result, apps page lists none]. DesignCraft's web build has no control channel [V]. Windowing/threading: winit fork, one UI thread plus app-specific workers [M]. 2.3 CLI, control channel and MCP CLI (GridCraft) [V] cli.md: info , convert (xlsx/csv/tsv/json/html by extension), eval , cat , check (accuracy and round trip, JSON schema gridcraft-check/1 ), run (repeatable --cmd 'id={json}' , scripts), commands --json , functions --json , mcp , send <port> <method> . No PNG or PDF export is documented for GridCraft headless. Other CLIs [V]: PdfCraft info text edit combine extract split run tools ui mcp ; WordCraft convert text inspect run mcp (PNG page images via convert ); DeckCraft render --all (headless slide PNGs), mcp ; SoundCraft run --bounce (WAV/AIFF/FLAC with LUFS report); VectorCraft run --export ; DesignCraft run --all-pages out/ ; FigCraft render export run ; EffectCraft render --comp Main --out main.mp4 ; CADCraft info convert run commands mcp . Control channel (desktop app only) [V] control-protocol.md: plain TCP on 127.0.0.1:<port> ( --control ), newline-delimited JSON {id, method, params} ; mandatory 256-bit token, either from GRIDCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN or a 0600 file in a 0700 directory; first line must be auth within 10 s. Methods include engine.execute , engine.commands , sheet.read , cell.get , ui.click/drag/move , ui.key/text , ui.dialog* , ui.resize , ui.screenshot (PNG, base64 or to a path, 8 s timeout, 64 MiB reply cap), app.open/save/quit . PdfCraft's variant is off by default and takes a control file with the token; it refuses symlinked or shared files [V]. MCP [V] mcp.md: hand-written JSON-RPC over stdio ; GridCraft has 22 tools ( read_range , write_range , evaluate_formula , insert_chart , sort_range , execute_command , screenshot in remote mode). Headless mode uses an in-process session with no window and no documented network use. PdfCraft MCP: render_preview(page, max_side<=4096) , text_extract , doc_combine , doc_split , page_extract , command_run , plus --root , --automation-read-root , --automation-write-root path confinement, symlinks resolved [V]. MCP stdio plus a roots flag is exactly the shape our hub wants. 3. Routes into TempleOS (question 2) Relevant measurements from our own notes [R] ( web-apps.md , electron-apps.md , browser-architecture.md ): host-side type-to-new-display-list p50 17 ms; screenshot 600x400 PNG 35 ms, 900x600 JPEG 28 ms; the guest has no JPEG decoder, so tiles use palette/RLE rects with 16-row strip diffs; raw 900x600 RGB565 is 1.08 MB (23 s at 47 KB/s); serial 16 to 47 KB/s (16.3 end to end measured, 47 reported); Aiwnios has native sockets; second-tab input needed Page.bringToFront (5 s to 17 ms); about 129 MB of Chrome per extra app tab; hub round trip 18 ms, a 20 KB reply 0.58 s at 34 KB/s [V weather-music-status.md]. R1. Native app on the Mac, stream its window. Mechanics without Screen Recording: start the app with --control <port> , read the token file, then loop ui.screenshot (PNG), diff in our 16-row strips (the apps send no dirty rects), and forward guest mouse/keys as ui.click , ui.drag , ui.key , ui.text in window points (so no coordinate mapping error), with ui.resize to match the guest window. Costs: a real window on the user's Mac that must stay visible (minimised windows queue captures) [V] ; each frame is a full render plus GPU readback plus PNG plus base64 over JSON, which I estimate at 50 to 150 ms [M] ; a visible GUI process outside appd's CDP controls; sandbox-exec around a GUI app is awkward [M] . Effort M. Verdict: works, but strictly dominated by R2 for apps that have a web build. R2. WASM build in headless Chrome under appd, tiles. Fit: the egui canvas is pixels, so display lists cannot express it; tiles are the only route [V: egui draws one canvas; R: tiles are the labelled fallback]. Plan: appd serves the zip on loopback, kind web , render: "tiles" , the existing stream.py strip diff and RLE, input via Input.dispatchMouseEvent/KeyEvent with CSS px = surface px (DSF 1), focus emulation fix from the Electron work. Unknowns [M] : whether headless Chrome 156 on this Mac gives eframe a WebGPU or WebGL2 context (both are claimed fallbacks [V], not tested); egui IME and clipboard through its hidden text input; wasm load time (PdfCraft 38 MB uncompressed). Latency estimate: host side 50 to 150 ms; over serial a full first frame may be 30 to 120 KB of RLE (about 1 to 3 s at 47 KB/s) and later deltas a few KB (about 100 to 300 ms); over an Aiwnios socket close to host cost. Good for demos and for tools whose value is the UI itself (PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FigCraft, PdfCraft). Effort S to M, since appd and stream.py exist. Canvas apps are the only kind that have no alternative. R3. Core as host service behind the hub. The hub already does REQ/RES/APPROVE with a 20 KB reply in 0.58 s [R]. Each service is a child process of the CLI. Two protocols are available: one-shot CLI commands with --json (GridCraft eval --json , info --json , convert ), or a long-lived stdio MCP session (GridCraft 22 tools, PdfCraft render_preview ) confined with --root . Separability from the UI is verified in the manifests for GridCraft, PdfCraft and the layering claims of WordCraft, SoundCraft, VectorCraft, DesignCraft, CADCraft, FigCraft, FilmCraft [V]. Cost: start-up per call for one-shots (not measured [M] ), process memory, a JSON-RPC client in hostd.py (about 150 lines [M] ). Effort S per service. Caveat: payloads are PNG or text, and the guest cannot decode PNG, so page images must be re-encoded on the host into our RLE/RGB565 image path (the browser already does this for IMAGE ops [S: browser-architecture.md]). R4. Core crates as no_std x86-64 .BIN . Proven so far is only a no_std , no-alloc blob with SSE2 ( engine-on-templeos.md , 25x slower than native under TCG) [R]. The candidate crates are not that: gridcraft-core pulls chrono with std ; functions pulls regex with std, unicode, perf ; serde, Arc copy-on-write bands, and String all need alloc ; PdfCraft needs image , icu_properties , url and filesystem-free but allocation-heavy parsers. gridcraft-formula (core + serde + thiserror) is the most plausible, with alloc , if chrono is isolated behind a feature. Blockers: no allocator story in the proven spike (needs a bump allocator or MAlloc import), libm for transcendentals, regex replacement, TCG speed, upstream churn (a weekly 0.x release stream will not stay compatible with a fork). Effort L for formula only, XL for engine. Rejected for now. R5. Rust staticlib with a C ABI, linked into Aiwnios. Wrap gridcraft-engine in a 100-line crate-type = ["staticlib"] shim ( gc_open , gc_execute(json) -> json , gc_free ), build with rustc 1.95 or later, register the symbols with PrsAddSymbol as aiwnios/README.md describes [S] . No serial hop, so edits answer in microseconds; Session::execute already restores state on a panic [V]. But it exists on the arm64 Aiwnios build only; the x86 TempleOS guest cannot load it, which breaks the single-source rule of desk3/0*.HC [S] . Effort M. Rank it after R3, as an optimisation of the same service API if hub latency proves too high for interactive recalculation. R6. Port to HolyC. Rejected. GridCraft alone is 8.1 MB of Rust source with 313 commands and 513 listed functions [V]; our spreadsheets plan scopes a calculator-grade P0/P1/P2 of about 60 functions in HolyC [S: spreadsheets.md]. HolyC has no generics, no iterators, no JSON, a stack-ABI and x87 float; the upstream changes weekly; XL and permanent. Ranking: R3 > R2 > R5 > R1 > R4 > R6. R1 and R5 swap places if the user wants the apps' own UI (R1) versus speed (R5): for the stated aim (spreadsheet, slides, docs, PDF, image, music, design tools) the services in R3 give more value for less cost. 4. Per-app fit (question 3) "Best route" assumes the guest keeps its HolyC UI and the host does the heavy work. Effort [M] . 513 functions are an inventory, not proven MIT or Apache-2.0; ArtCraft marks removed from forks PdfCraft alpha, v0.14.0 R3 (MCP: render_preview, text_extract, organise, merge/split/rotate) M High: PDF viewer and organiser, text search CLI zip is 63 MB; fuzzing still finds crashes and hangs (README); hayro render is a stopgap MIT or Apache-2.0; OCR models via cargo xtask models (extra download) WordCraft alpha R3 ( convert , inspect , render_page ; docx/odt/rtf/md in, PDF/PNG out) M High: Docs import/export, page images no version stated in README; optional R2 demo n/a Low heavy; no guest video MIT or Apache-2.0 FilmCraft alpha none n/a None video; apps page vs README conflict on wasm MIT or Apache-2.0; symphonia is MPL-2.0 5. Reuse as spec, code, or build ourselves (question 4) Reuse as spec (zero risk, high value). gridcraft-cli functions --json and commands --json give a machine-readable list of 513 functions and 313 commands; docs/function-parity.md (17.8 KB), file-format-parity.md (31.3 KB) and parity-checklist.md exist in the repo and can be read by the spreadsheet plan's P0/P1/P2 lists. PdfCraft's pdf-spec-parity.md , WordCraft's 422-command catalog and DeckCraft's 200+ commands play the same role for PDF viewer, Docs and Slides. Reuse as code (host side only). - Replace IronCalc as the first-choice oracle and host converter in docs/apps/spreadsheets.md section 8 with GridCraft: it reads xlsx, xlsb and ods, writes xlsx/csv/tsv/json/html, and has a check accuracy runner. Keep IronCalc and calamine as a second opinion; HyperFormula stays blocked (GPLv3) [S]. - In docs/apps/slides.md , python-pptx and pptxgenjs can drop to fallback status once DeckCraft's pptx round trip is checked; its render --all gives slide PNGs the plan did not have. - For Docs, WordCraft's convert covers docx/odt/rtf/md/tex import and PDF export that nothing in the current plan does. - LibreOffice stays the outside-reference oracle; the plans call it "never linked" [S]. Build ourselves. The HolyC grid editing, native recalculation for sub-30 ms edits (the spreadsheet plan's budget), our window chrome, and the approvals UI. Interactive latency over the hub is unmeasured (one-shot CLI start-up times are not known [M] ), so the native engine stays the P0 plan; the hub engine becomes import/export and oracle. What we can drop. The converter choice among SheetJS, openpyxl, calamine (if GridCraft's reader passes our corpus), a custom pptx text-run importer, and any plan to port a PDF reader. We keep sound playback (host afplay , already built). 6. Security and privacy (question 5) What the apps send where. The READMEs of PdfCraft and PhotoCraft claim no AI features, no telemetry and no network at runtime for documents: PdfCraft "no account, no telemetry, no cloud" [V]. FigCraft contacts no server until a user shares; sharing uploads to collab.craftapps.dev by default, unencrypted at rest [V]. GridCraft's page makes no privacy claim; its only AI claim is agent-driven automation through MCP/CLI/JSON [V]. The AI layer lives in craft-ai-integrations ("first draft", 111 stars): OpenAI-compatible APIs, Black Forest Labs, Vertex Gemini, BytePlus Seedance, "ArtCraft Omni API-key route", local ComfyUI and SAM; keys in the OS keychain, an encrypted file or env vars; the README does not say what data goes to each provider and does not mention telemetry; its own test coverage is local mock servers only [V]. The ArtCraft studio itself is a separate AI product with a 62-model catalog [V]. Self-update: craft-update is a dependency of GridCraft and PdfCraft [V]; what it contacts at runtime I did not read [M] . The launcher checks GitHub releases [V]. Our approval rules. The hub keeps tokens and keys on the host and grants live in approvals.json [S]. Rules for these services: no network for any ArtCraft child process (macOS sandbox-exec profile with (deny network*) , read access limited to the user-approved folder, write access limited to a scratch directory) [M: profile text is mine, untested] ; the MCP --root / --automation-*-root flags as the second fence [V]; no craft-ai-* feature ever enabled without its own PROMPT naming the provider and the data; the control channel is never used for services (it is for R1 only), and if used, the token stays on the host. Running untrusted alpha binaries. We never run a downloaded binary without approval. The install flow apps-host/install.py already requires an explicit --sha256 , safe extraction, codesign checks and a registry [S]. It handles .app bundles with Electron; a Mach-O CLI kind needs a small addition. The guest dialog must show: name, version tag, source URL, exact file name and size, the SHA-256 from the release's SHA256SUMS.txt and the one we computed, the codesign/notarisation result, the folder it may read, the statement "no network", and Yes/No. On Yes: host downloads, hashes, extracts, runs codesign -dv --verbose=2 and spctl --assess (a notarised DMG is claimed signed and notarised by the launcher README [V]; whether the CLI zip is signed is unverified ), stores it under apps/artcraft/<version>/ , and records the grant. A SHA-256 taken from the same release proves integrity, not authorship: say so in the dialog. Do not use craft-launcher : it installs into /Applications , may prompt for admin rights, and self-updates [V]. Pin one release, and let updates be a new approval each. Source build instead of binaries. Building runs their build.rs and downloads git dependencies from storytold forks of egui and winit [V]. It needs a clone, which is also approval-gated, and is no safer than a binary. Not recommended. Prompt injection. MCP returns document text; hub rows and tool output are data, never instructions, and an MCP session must not receive guest-supplied instructions as commands [S: hub policy]. 7. Prototype plan with gates (question 6) Evidence favours GridCraft CLI behind the hub for day one over a WASM tile demo: smallest useful artefact, fastest to verify, and it exercises the pieces (hub, approvals, host install) every later step shares.
